quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Bill Turner Memorial EBF Brocklesby Stakes (A Novice Stakes) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: A Bear Affair has always been a very likeable horse with a very good attitude and he could be every bit as good as some of the horses we've brought here. If you win this race there aren't many places to go after until you get to the Woodcote. You don't talk about Ascot horses at this time of year but he's ideal with an attitude to suit that sort of programme. There will be a lot more to come physically, he's not really there in his coat. Mentally, I want him to stay exactly how he is. He will improve a lot for this - Richard Hannon, trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.raceTitle: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Race (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: We thought A Boy Named Susie was good as he did a really, really good piece of work up the Curragh a few weeks ago. This auction race looked a tough ask as he was giving away weight to winners and it is a tough track first-time-out but he is obviously just smart. For an auction race at Killarney, it has thrown up Iridessa, Luxembourg, Lambourn and a few Group 2 winners as well so it's a nice start for him. They hacked and then sprinted but I think he could be a proper one. He has plenty of gears for a big horse - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She did well to win on her debut at Newbury last year. She's has an Oaks entry and will run in a trial somewhere - she'll need some juice in the ground. She is bred to be above average and goes well. She's pretty straightforward and we're just waiting for her to come to hand. 27-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Bet £20 Get £20 With Unibet Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: When you've ridden the dams of horses and stallions, it shows you've been getting on a little bit. Abashiri is beautifully bred, and she's already looking like she could be a good broodmare. I really liked the way she did it, and she's got plenty of scope going into next year. She came here ready to have a run, and it's nice to go into the winter off the back of that - William Buick, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

horse_profiles.owner_name: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith

quotes.raceTitle: Space Traveller At Compas Stallions (C & G) Maiden
quotes.notes: We're delighted with Accredited. He had one run in Dundalk. Ronan [Whelan] rode him and said seven with an ease in the ground. Ryan said he'd have no problem getting a mile and better ground. He'll have to go for a winners' race now. We'll go gentle with him. His first run was a nice run. He'll end up going up to a mile and then probably to stakes level. He's a good looking horse and by Siyouni too - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a good-looking horse who had a nice run at Dundalk last year and then won a 7f maiden at Naas this month on soft ground. Ryan [Moore] said afterwards he'd have no problem getting a mile and better ground. He'll have to go for a winners' race now and then probably to stakes level but we'll go gentle with him. 31-03-26

horse_profiles.breeder_name: Newsells Park Stud & Merry Fox Stud

quotes.notes: We didn't think Act Of Kindness was a Guineas filly which is why we didn't put her in it. However, she wants a mile and we'll look at the Michael Seely Stakes at York - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Godolphin Under Starters Orders Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: With her pedigree it's nice to get her head in front. Whether Act Of Kindness is a 1,000 Guineas filly or a Pretty Polly filly, we'll know next spring - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

horse_profiles.owner_name: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: Action is quite a big horse, he stays well and ideally I would have loved to have gone a stride quicker but he was having such a look in front I was letting him find his feet and get comfortable. I thought the last 50 yards he hit the line well. He is going to learn plenty from today - Wayne Lordan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran a very good race in the Futurity Trophy when second to Hawk Mountain and he'll be trained for a Derby. I'd imagine it'll be Epsom as he looks an Epsom type. He'll run in a trial, probably at Chester or Leopardstown. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Gowran Classic

previous_owners.ownerStyleName: N C Williams, L J Williams Et Al

quotes.raceTitle: Paddy Power Stakes (Group 3) (Registered as the Kilternan Stakes)
quotes.notes: Adelaide River is a lovely, big horse and we always viewed him as a next year horse. We thought he could be like Duke Of Marmalade in that he is after competing in those big ones and went very close in them but he is such a big horse, is definitely going to have to be a way better horse next year - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

Adelaide River is a lovely colt. He always showed a bit at home. He was always the lazy one as well. He went out to the start today nice and sleepy, jumped a bit slow, but thankfully I had plenty of room to get up into a good position. He went down past the 2f pole well and went forward nice pricking his ears, he had plenty left - Wayne Lordon, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He worked very well at the Curragh the other day. He's going to go to a Derby trial and could head to France for one. 06-04-23

horse_profiles.breeder_name: J A Knox And Mrs M A Knox

quotes.notes: I'm not one to bring horses to make up the numbers. I never have done it and never will. This is not about being proved right, it's having faith in the horse. I told the owners Ain't Nobody was in great form and I said we were going to ride him cold, they're going to go hard here. We'd ride him like when he won at Royal Ascot. It's worked out a treat - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

It panned out perfectly. Obviously it was such a big field you don't know what's going to happen. After going 100 yards, I was following the American horse, getting a good lead and he was always going to bring me as far as I wanted, and Ain't Nobody was tough at the finish. He's a nice horse for the future, he's only a young horse on his second run, so plenty to look forward to - Jamie Spencer, rider.

Akkadian Thunder ran a blinder. David [O'Meara, trainer] was keen to have him nice and relaxed early. He said, 'Ride him to have him coming home'. I followed Oisin [Murphy] everywhere and we had a great run through. When we got in the clear, I thought he might pick up and get to Oisin, but fairness to the winner who picked up and won well. Our horse has run a great race - Billy Lee, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A good horse last year, he'll start off in the Victoria Cup. I thought he wanted only fast ground and then he ran a stormer on soft when second at Ascot in September. He's got plenty of ability and a lot of speed, and straight tracks suit him well. 14-04-25

quotes.notes: Al Mubhir just did too much on the way around. He just never let go - Tom Marquand, jockey.

Everything went really smoothly and the soft ground was always going to help coming back to a mile. Al Mubhir\ relaxed well and surprised me how well he did it in the end. He's clearly a talented horse and if we keep getting things right, he's got a big future - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: MansionBet Beaten By A Head Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Al Mubhir did that nicely. The jockey liked him but said he knew nothing so we might have to run him again but he was a bit spicy after the race so we'll have to see - William Haggas, trainer.

You can set your clock by Al Nayyir, he's a dude. He had a good campaign in the Middle East and has come back as good as ever. He's run some big races here as well, he was just touched off last year in the Lonsdale Cup - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Jockey Club Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: "He's a very exciting stayer and I couldn't have been more thrilled with the way Al Nayyir did it. We've got him in on Champions Day and that would be the logical next step but I'd love to avoid Kyprios if we could. We love to have these Stakes horses and that's the direction we want to go. I'm thrilled to have the owner's support and to train a horse of this calibre" - Tom Clover, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Weatherbys Hamilton Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: It was a really good run. Al Nayyir is a new horse to us but he'd shaped up well in his home work. I couldn't quite believe the price he was. He had some very good form and he has a very high rating. Hopefully he can go one better very soon. We've got him in in France and on Champions day, we'll have to discuss it with the owners - Tom Clover, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was a little disappointing in Dubai, where they went no gallop and he over-travelled. We're lining up to go to Sandown at the end of the month for the Group 3 over 2m there. He took some time to come to hand over the winter but he's training well now, so hopefully we'll have plenty of fun with him during the British turf season. 14-05-25

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: Al Riffa didn't run a bad race and he kept coming all the way to the line. From where we were early, with his weight and given how the race was set up, it was always going to be tough. It was no-one's fault but we didn't get the rub of the green. He'll have other days - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Comer Group International Irish St. Leger (Group 1)
quotes.notes: I fancied Al Riffa as the conditions and trip were good and he had a lovely set-up. Things couldn't have gone better. There was plenty of speed on in the first half of the race, he relaxes well and has got a good kick when you need it. I was able to take my time and he quickened up and won well.  He feels like he could go another couple of furlongs and the world is his oyster now. He's one of my favourites and owes me nothing - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey.

That was brilliant. Al Riffa has got a lot of class and he was last to first in a National Stakes here. No one ever felt that he needed that trip but it made sense. He was very relaxed and Dylan said he was a very easy ride over that trip. I'd say it's most likely that he'll go straight to the Irish St Leger from here. There is a possibility of the Pries Von Berlin he won last year but I'd say it's more likely he'll go straight to the Irish Leger. The Melbourne Cup is in the mind thereafter. We all know what comes with that but it's what we'd like to do, if we're allowed - Kevin Blake, stable representative.

Fantastic run, probably unlucky to meet a horse like Rebel Romance in that race, but we're very proud of Al Riffa, who is a real star for us and he's run his legs off for us again today. Hopefully there will be plenty more big days with him to come this season. He's a beautiful horse and he always runs to a rating not too far off 120, and it's hard to find horses like that. Obviously he's a multiple Group One winner and we were probably unlucky to meet a real champion in the Hardwicke. Rebels' Romance is one of the best horses in the world over the last number of years. I wouldn't be against trying a little bit further with him as well - he's got plenty of stamina in his pedigree. I think we'll probably think outside the box with him a little bit now - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

Al Riffa ran a really good race and came home strong. It was his first race, so he was entitled to that. We are delighted with him and we'll see how he pulls up and make plans from there - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

It's been a wonderful day and Al Riffa put up a really good performance so we're very proud. Dylan [Browne McMonagle] gave the horse a fantastic ride. He's had a busy season so far, racing in France, Britain, America and now Germany, so I think he'll have a little rest and then be prepared for the Arc - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

We'll probably make the rest of the season all about the Arc, which will be his main target. Al Riffa should enjoy the mile and a half as his family is all stamina. It looked like mile and a half will suit him on his run today - Jospeh O'Brien, trainer.

Al Riffa ran great. It was a tactical race, but I'm very proud of his run and looking forward to his season ahead. He came there with a strong run and maybe got a bit tired. He's a big colt and hopefully he has a long season ahead. He has options and the Tattersalls Gold Cup or the Prix d'Ispahan would be two obvious races for his next start. Also we're keen to explore 12 furlongs as we think the Arc is a longer-term target so we'll be plotting our route to there - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

Obviously the winner is a champion and we're very close to him. Christophe liked Al Riffa a lot and we've a lot to look forward to. The last run was decent but it's nice to see him back to his two-year-old form today, and he finished very well. It was good to keep him against three-year-olds again before taking on older horses next time, which will probably be in the Irish Champion Stakes. We'll look at the Champion Stakes afterwards - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Goffs Vincent O'Brien National Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.notes: It was a special performance. Al Riffa won his maiden well and the owners were keen to supplement him for this. It was a very impressive performance to come from the back of the field like that. He was a big shell of a horse as a yearling and I thought he'd make a lovely 3yo, I didn't for a minute think he'd make the two-year-old that he has made. His family is all stamina, so for him to be doing this at this stage is very positive for the future. We always thought he was a middle-distance horse, and he's closely related to an Ascot Gold Cup winner, so that's real stamina, but he's not slow. I'd imagine he's a Guineas horse for sure and we'll take it from there. He's a classy horse and very exciting. The plan coming here was to go on to the race on Arc day (the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere) but we'll see how he comes out of it today and discuss it with the owners - Joseph O'Brien, trainer

quotes.raceTitle: John Ormonde Wexford Sand Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.notes: Al Riffa is a grand horse. He was first off it, niggling, but he's a big horse and still immature. The future is bright, he could be anything. He goes on quick ground for a big horse but he might just be better with a bit of cut in it. The National Stakes has been mentioned. I think he'll be a cracking three-year-old - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran great in Hong Kong to finish a close fourth but Dubai was a very messy race. He's come out of it well and will be campaigned for the big occasions. He'll maybe start off in France in the Group 1 Prix Vicomtesse Vigier over 2m next month and we're looking forward to the season. 22-04-26

A smart horse and, after a particularly catching run on his debut when a fast-finishing second to Hans Anderson, he won his maiden at the Curragh as we expected. His work after that improved and we felt he was worth his place in the Group 1 National Stakes which he won very nicely from my brother Donnacha's colt Proud And Regal. That was his last run of the campaign and he looks a much stronger three-year-old this year, more the finished product. He was our nicest juvenile last year and carries our hopes this year. The plan will be to have his first run in the Irish Guineas at the end of May and we will then stick to the mile for his next run. After that, depending on how he is doing, I may consider stepping him up to 1m2f, but I don't see him taking up his Derby entry. His pedigree and the work he is doing where he shows a lot of pace says he is quick enough to stick to the mile. He has been doing all we have asked him this spring and I'm looking forward to getting him out on the track again. 12-04-23

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.raceTitle: Watership Down Stud Too Darn Hot Greenham Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Albert Einstein has run a creditable race in a muddling contest. We have to be happy with that. We'll let Ryan [Moore] speak with Aidan [O'Brien] and the owners, and then a decision will be made about which route we're going to go - Kevin Buckley, trainer's representative.

quotes.raceTitle: 1xBet.ie Supports Irish Racing Gladness Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I think Albert Einstein is a sprinter and that was a little bit of the reason he was here. It was a very tough call to run him in that ground against older, hardier horses. Obviously we just have to do the right thing by the horse. He's always found it very hard to go slow. Some horses find it very hard to go quick but he finds it very hard to go slow. Usually that kind of horse needs a very strong tempo early. The lads will decide but my initial thought is that he'll be coming back and he'll go sprinting. It's a very difficult thing to run against those horses in that bad ground. If you have an older, strong horse, they can maul a three-year-old. He was travelling very strong and in that ground you'd have preferred that he would be travelling a gear or two lower. He's naturally just not able to do that. His tempo is so quick; he is a very high-tempo horse. It was in the back of my mind that this is a big sprinter. Obviously, we'll go and talk to the lads and see what they want to do, but there is a very good chance that's [Commonwealth Cup] the route he's going to go. He will definitely have another run before the Commonwealth Cup. The sprinters are coming here [for a racecourse gallop] tomorrow - Charles Darwin, Brussels and a few others - they are all three-year-old sprinters as well and this fella will add into the mix there. This fella was always a bit different, but we'll see - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Ryan waited and got Albert Einstein to relax as best he could. When he pulled him out he said it took a minute for him to engage but he's a very, very fast horse. We were hoping it was going to be a fast-run race, which I thought it was, but Ryan said he would have liked them to go even faster. The plan was to come here and go to the Coventry. I was worried today because it was so windy and he's so sharp mentally but he had to run. If everything goes well I think he will go to the Coventry, but all those things are decided the week before Royal Ascot. I think his name was changed three times actually. Every time we named him I think Sue [Magnier] maybe thought the name wasn't good enough for him. I wasn't even sure what his name was because it was changed so many times. I'm delighted for the lads and he's very exciting - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Albert Einstein was never far away and that's the first time he's come off the bridle. We're delighted with him. You can see the size and power of him. He learned a bit today. Ger's horse had a very good run the first day. We always thought he was a Coventry horse. You'd like to get another run into him before it, though - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was a bit disappointing on Saturday, but he started off sort of three or four lengths off the leaders and nobody changed position. It was more important that he behaved well and got beat than behave bad and win. We felt he did behave well. He settled but he was a little bit strong in Ryan's hands. But Ryan said he was by no means unmanageable. Ryan felt they were going very slow, and he has a lot of pace on that bad ground. In the full light of day, you'd have to be happy enough. We'll see how he is over the next couple of weeks, and the lads will decide if they give him a chance at a mile or go back sprinting. We know if he goes back sprinting he'll find that very easy, if that's what they decide to do. 31-03-26

We've just got him this year. He's quite interesting and looks like a miler. We're thinking of starting him off in the [Listed] Amethyst Stakes next month. He probably likes going around a turn and prefers it left-handed. He's talented when he puts it together. 22-04-26

He's a big, scopey colt who ran better than his bare form last year and he delighted me at Newbury on Saturday. He travelled well through the race and would have needed it big time, so there's plenty to look forward to. A bit of black type would be nice and he's in the Derby. All options are open. 21-04-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)
Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: Almaqam has always promised and not quite delivered, but we've had the utmost faith in him. We're thrilled to get it done, and hopefully it's onwards and upwards from here and he can have a big year. I didn't love the track when I walked it. It was quickening up but perfectly safe to have a go, and we vowed with the Sheikh Ahmed team that this year we were going to be a little bit more bold with him with regards to ground conditions. Last year we tip-toed around and it was a really fiddly year with a dry summer. He was a big, heavy, immature horse, and he's a bit older now, so we can afford to be bolder with the ground. He can cope with that now. You've got Ascot and the Eclipse, and it's a seriously difficult division with the likes of Daryz, Ombudsman and Calandagan. We've beaten Ombudsman once before, who then beat us at Ascot, and Calandagan beat us quite convincingly on Champions day, but this horse is a big, big boy and he may just be coming into his own this year. I certainly would be having a go [at taking them on] - Ed Walker, trainer.Almaqam, who has a monster rating of 122, has been knocking on the door so I'm glad he's broken his Group One maiden. He did it in style too, we almost expected him to take a step forward from today but what a horse to go to war with. He gave me a wonderful feel and he's clearly improving with age - Kieran Shoemark, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

I'm disappointed to be beaten but it was a really good performance. We're really happy with Almaqam. I was fretting all week about where to run, whether to go to Germany, here or the Irish Champion Stakes, but we did the right thing coming here. He definitely stays the trip and we learned a lot, but I think he'll be better on softer ground. He looked like he wasn't going to stay but then he rallied again. I think it's just the ground. He's a big, heavy horse who I think needs a bit of cut to be able to let himself down properly. He's not been beaten far and my initial feeling is we have to roll the dice. William [Buick, jockey] said if you're going to do it, do it this year. The Champion Stakes is going to be a smoking hot race and I think he wants this trip. If the owner is happy to have a go, then I think we should - Ed Walker, trainer.
Almaqam ran well. He hit the front and he was lengthening all the way to the line - no excuses - Kieran Shoemark, rider.

Almaqam has got a great attitude. Last year we had him in a lip chain in the prelims but we took it off and he's just so laid-back, he's almost asleep. I think that's what got him beaten last time, he was still on his winter holidays and just flopped out the gates and flopped round and didn't really help Tom [Marquand] out. He's definitely sharpened up at home for that run. When the Gosdens' horse [Ombudsman] loomed up I thought we were cooked, but he was really tough. He stays well, and Ryan [Moore] said last year at Longchamp that he'd definitely get a mile and a half, but his pedigree doesn't suggest that. However, Oisin [Murphy] has just said exactly the same. We stuck him in the Arc as I've never hidden how much I think about this horse. The ground is absolutely key, and it'll be hard to know what to do with him through the summer, but good ground is probably as quick as we want it to be - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Chasemore Farm Stud Staff Heron Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I was quite taken by Almaqam. The ground was very soft today but you've got to handle it and he's got a beautiful pedigree. That's only his third start today so you'd imagine he would really progress and he's certainly got the ability. You have to stamina in that ground and I see him as a ten furlong horse in time - William Buick, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was a good winner of the Brigadier Gerard but Ascot comes soon enough and it looks like the ground will be too quick for him to run. We'll monitor conditions and we'll be ready in case it comes right, but it doesn't look likely. 10-06-25

He's been training well and looks great. We toyed with the idea of the Prix d'Harcourt but didn't feel he was quite ready. Given that he really needed the run first time out last year, we want to make sure we've got him spot on this season. He's well on track for the Gordon Richards Stakes if we go there, or we could supplement him for the Prix Ganay if there's enough ease in the ground. As always with him, we'll have to be patient and wait for conditions to be right. But his form last year was unbelievable and it's amazing he hasn't won a Group 1 or Group 2 race. I think a well-run 1m2f is ideal for him, although I wouldn't rule out having another go at 1m4f and we've put him in the Coronation Cup. But life will be difficult in the top races. With Calandagan, Ombudsman and others around, it's the hardest division. 22-04-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Cathedral Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: It was very much a confidence-booster for Almeraq today and if he won it was a bonus. We wanted him to improve for the run, which he was always going to do - Harry Davies, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap
quotes.notes: I wasn't really happy with Almeraq's [low] draw and it wasn't ideal being stuck on the wing. I tried to get in the best I could but he's done everything right and he'll come on from that. He's a big baby still but he'll learn a lot from that and I liked the way he finished his race off. I spoke to Mr [William] Haggas beforehand and he said he wanted this sort of ground. He's a lovely big horse and I think he'll be a better horse in a better race - Clifford Lee, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

Almeraq is exciting and I really like him. He's got a lovely mind on him and he's a horse for next year. He's improved a lot, he ran a lovely race first time and he was sharp out and did everything as you'd like. He's a well-bred horse, there's a lot of speed in the family and he likes a lot of juice in the ground- Jim Crowley, rider, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: Almeric is a smart horse. He's not in the Derby, but he's in the French Derby and a host of others. I think the plan would be to go to the Dante before a crack at the Prix du Jockey Club - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coral Racing Club EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: That was good. Almeric did well at Sandown on his debut and his pedigree suggests he's only going to get better as a three-year-old and on better ground too - P J McDonald, jockey.

After the Satsuki Sho [2,000 Guineas] I decided with the owner that we would take up the challenge in France and were originally aiming at the Grand Prix de Paris, but Alohi Alii was not in such good form, so we turned to this race with a view to preparing for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe. Obviously, Christophe [Lemaire] knows Deauville very well and he is a jockey with whom I've had a lot of success, so he was the automatic choice for the job. I think he could be even better over a mile and a half and I think two months is perfect timing to prepare for the Arc, given he had been off for four months before this race - Hiroyasu Tanaka, trainer.Alohi Alii hasn't always enjoyed the fast early pace in Japan but with a slower French tempo, even though we missed the start a little, I was able to go to the front quite easily and he really surprised me with how he picked up - Christophe Lemaire, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Watership Down Stud Too Darn Hot Greenham Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Alparslan is a high-class horse, and I'm sure he'll turn up in one of the Guineas, but it's a case of which one we go for. We've got time to go to the English and Irish, but it's a nice problem to have and I'm really happy. He's been to Newmarket, and he didn't like the undulations of the track, although that could've been down to two-year-old immaturity. It's a question mark. Whether racing round a bend at Longchamp for the French Guineas would be his cup of tea, I don't know, but the Curragh would suit him well as he's obviously won there. The mile is the question, but when you look at the last 50 yards, he's not stopping. He's going away if anything. I thought we were coming here under the radar. He'd only run three times, and he's entitled to improve off those runs. He's been working very well, and he's got a great mind. He will definitely come on fitness-wise, and I'm sure there's another gear for him - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A smart, strong-travelling horse who progressed nicely last year. He acquitted himself well in the Dewhurst as he didn't handle the undulations at Newmarket. He'll go to Newbury for a trial to see how he gets on with the trip and grade, and then we'll see about one of the Guineas. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Irish EBF Auction Series Race Final
quotes.notes: That was great, a lovely pot to win for Alphecca. Ger [Kervick] gets his first homebred, so he's delighted. They took a chance running her back quickly from Killarney, but it paid dividends. She jumped, travelled and picked up and got to the line really strongly. A mile is probably her trip. She is a filly who I think will get black type next year. She is improving and I think there's more to come. When they beat her in Naas, she missed the break that day, but today she had the hang of the stalls and jumped well and she's very straightforward - Gary Carroll, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won his only race last year in a 7f maiden at the Curragh in June. He's out of a Galileo mare and is the type for a Derby trial. 31-03-26

horse_profiles.owner_name: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)

quotes.notes: I was very happy with Amelia Earhart, she's a fine, big filly by Camelot - a family we know well. She was well suited by the step up in trip. She handled the trip, handled the ground and she's done everything right. She's a really nice filly for the rest of the year. That'll do her good today, she'll have learned plenty and she's enjoyed herself - Ryan Moore, jockey.Amelia Earhart a big and strong filly with a beautiful stride and a great temperament. She stayed the trip well and hit the line well, so you couldn't be more delighted. She'll probably go to the Oaks off the back of that. The step up in trip was always there in the pedigree and it showed today - she's a beautiful specimen and the trip obviously helped - Paul Smith, owners' representative.

Amelia Earhart is very good, she's always run well so it's nice to get her head in front. She was very green when I rode her last time, but thankfully she's put it all together today - Jack Cleary, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's a good filly, even though it took her a long time to win last year. She'd been second twice and fourth in a Group 3 before she got it done really well at Leopardstown, winning a mile maiden by seven lengths. Ryan rode her at the Curragh on Sunday and loved her. He thinks she'll get a mile and a half well. She's the type for an Oaks trial. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: I felt America Queen stayed seven [furlongs] well there as she came back a bit and was up in the van all the way. It was a real tough, hard run. She will go to France now [for the French 1,000 Guineas], and if they go slow, which they normally do, and she gets a good draw, it should suit. It's a gruelling mile here, and I have another filly for the 1,000 Guineas in Rose Ghaiyyath, who we like a lot. If there is any chance of this filly getting a mile it will be in France. She's easy as she relaxes. She has run a blinder and is a pleasure to train. She does nothing flashy but she tries like hell, and you can't ask for any more - Richard Hughes, trainer.

I've trained the family for three generations so it's very sweet. American Affair's grandfather had his day here so we're pretty lucky that we can breed horses like that. He's just getting faster, we went seven furlongs at Wetherby in his maiden, we've learnt to run him over the right trip, we took him back to five and he's just getting better and better. I was quite confident he could do it today, he had the talent, we got it wrong at Haydock. I knew he was probably one of the fastest horses in the race but it's how you control that. We've come down a day early and got him relaxed and it all fell into place - Jim Goldie, trainer.I first won his maiden on him over seven furlongs round Wetherby, it's hard to believe. And then American Affair started getting sharper and sharper and I rode him one day at York over seven and he proper latched on and I said to Jim 'I think this lad could be a sprinter' and obviously he's just got quicker as he's got older as do a lot of sprinters - Paul Mulrennan, jockey.

It's probably American Affair's last go in a handicap. He's done nothing but improve and started off last year in the mid-70s, but the more racing he's had the sharper he's got. He just shuts down when he hits the front and is still quite raw. Jim said we'd learn a lot more about him today as there's no easy five-furlong race here. He's proved he's up to going to the next level - Paul Mulrennan, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Scottish Sprint Cup Handicap
quotes.notes: We probably have to go into Group races. There's the King Charles over five furlongs at Ascot, which would be okay. I don't think we'll go to Newmarket but American Affair is a good horse and he's maturing - Jim Goldie, trainer.

American Affair has done nothing but improve all year. Jim Goldie is some trainer. The last couple of races he's been running with the choke out and not really finishing. Jim said today to ride him ice cold, I got him to switch off and he finished really well. What will he be like next year with another winter on his back? He's still very babyish and raw - Paul Mulrennan, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
quotes.notes: American Affair is a homebred and as he came off the box, I said to him, 'Your granny [Class Wan] won here' and we've had a few generations of this breed. From where he was drawn [13], Paul got the rail and kind of bossed it - Jim Goldie, trainer, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Watch Racing TV In Stunning HD Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: American Affair is a work in progress but the uphill finish and the step up to seven played to his strengths. He's a big horse and there should be a lot more to come from him - Paul Mulrennan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's very talented. We hoped he would bounce back the way he did at Musselburgh and he'll improve for it. We're excited. He'll probably go to York for a 5f handicap next but I've put him in the Temple Stakes and the King Charles at Royal Ascot. We'll probably stick to 5f at the moment. I think he's up to that class over five and he's a simpler ride over that trip. He appears very fast and seems to be comfortable at that pace. 07-05-25

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)

quotes.notes: Christophe Soumillon felt ground was pretty important and American Gal wouldn't want it any quicker than that. We're not going to rush her, we'll see what the weather gods do but I'd be pretty tempted to come back for the Diane. Ascot [and the Coronation Stakes] is more likely to be quick but I think she could do either. She'll definitely stay a bit further and while she doesn't have to make the running, she was happy in front today. It's so hard to have horses that are good enough to have a go in these races and I think she deserves a shot at it, so I'd say the most likely thing is that if the ground is suitable, she'll probably go back for the Diane - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She disappointed in the Snowdrop Stakes at Kempton but Pat Cosgrave could never get her in from a wide draw and it just didn't pan out for her. We're putting a line through that and sticking with our plan to go for the Dahlia Stakes, as 1m1f at Newmarket will really suit her. She very nearly won the Valiant Stakes last year and we believe she's improved since. 22-04-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: We were thinking about Chester or Lingfield for Ancient Egypt, but when I saw this race was cutting up I thought we'd have a go. He disappointed here in the Royal Lodge last year, but he's grown up a lot over the winter and David Egan and Rowan have ridden him at home this year and said to go a mile and a half, which is why we made the running over this shorter trip. I would say all roads lead to Epsom after that and he handled the Dip well here which is encouraging - Charlie Johnston, trainer.It's the first time I've seen Ancient Egypt and Charlie [Johnston, trainer] thought maybe a mile and a quarter was on the short side but he was very determined and finished the race strongly. He ticked all the boxes today and he's done nothing wrong but I'll leave that to Charlie and Kia [Joorabchian, owner] to see if there's a race for him before Epsom - Frankie Dettori, owners' global brand ambassador.Ancient Egypt isn't quite the finished article yet, he's still a bit of a baby but he's a horse who is going to mature with time. He looks like he'll get further so he'll have plenty of options - Rowan Scott, jockey.

I get nervous before a race when nothing but winning will do and we would have been disappointed with second. Ancient Egypt was a bit coltish beforehand and it took a while for the penny to drop, but he won it comfortably enough. He doesn't win gallops at home by much, but always sticks his neck out - Mark Johnston, trainer's assistant.

previous_owners.ownerStyleName: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg

quotes.notes: To be fair, Dr Hay picked this race out even before he purchased Ancient Rome. He's Kentucky-bred so it fitted in well. I think he went well on the [firm] ground today and he's pretty adaptable when it comes to surfaces. He ran in softer conditions a lot of the time in France and last time [at Goodwood] it was soft, but he's a War Front and they go on fast turf - Jamie Spencer, quoted by Bloodhorse.

They did go a good gallop, which was quite tiring in dead ground, and the race fell into his lap in the last furlong. I always thought I was going to be involved; maybe outside the three-furlong pole, he was moving up easily enough and I was following Tom Marquand [on Millebosc], who was kind of dying so we went round him. Ancient Rome is a very lazy horse - you ask him and he'll go for three or four strides, then he's lazy again. Even right at the line he pricked his ears and kind of jammed [the brakes] on, so he's a hard horse to assess. I just planned to drop out, stay on the outside, get cover and come down the outside. Dr Jim said, just ride like Richard Hughes! He's a smart horse and I thought he was a stakes horse, so I'm sure he will be capable of at least Listed company - Jamie Spencer, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He had an injury at the backend of last season and has had some time off. He's a big horse who takes a bit of getting ready but he's undoubtedly talented. He's not a certain starter in the Wolferton but if he does take his chance, I think he's well up to that class. 13-06-24

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Star Appeal Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Andab was dropping back in class, his Group 2 run in Deauville was a good performance and the form has worked out nicely. He quickened up really well today; he's got plenty of class. I was happy to follow and get him relaxed. He wandered a bit at the front but under the lights was a new experience and he's only going to get better - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: We thought Andab would come on plenty for the run, wasn't really expecting a performance like that. He jumped and travelled good, he picked up good when I went for him and got to the line well. He'll have no problem stepping up to seven and will get a mile in time. He took a while to pull up, which is always a good sign -Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran a really good race in Qatar and was a bit unlucky not to win, then had another good run in Newcastle last time when it just didn't set up right for him. He's come out of that well and could potentially go for something like the [Listed] Tetrarch at the Curragh early next month. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: Annaf has come back to form now, which is great to see. I've not been that happy with his work but he's very talented and he's been getting back to where he normally was. We just freshened him up and did a few different things. We'll see where we go now with him now. He could possibly go abroad to Saudi for the race he won last year - Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Saudi National Bank 1351 Turf Sprint (Group 2) (4yo+) (Inner Track) (Turf)
quotes.notes: It's all down to Rossa, not my training. Anaaf keeps improving and keeps surprising us. Where we go next, God knows, but he's got that invitation to Japan and we'll possibly go there. These big meetings are becoming quite a habit really. It really feels like the sky's the limit. These international wins mean so much because it really does put the yard on the map -  Mick Appleby, trainer.

I love everything about Annaf. He's something else and he loved getting shifted about and being taken off his racing line today. He's really thriving and you have to give it to Mick Appleby and his team. He's been on the go since the start of the year and has not missed one beat - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

Annaf has been a star to me this year. My only concern was the ground and I knew the race was going to be ridden to suit him perfectly. He's a classy horse and a lot of people are forgetting he was third in the King's Stand and I'd imagine one of those nice Group races will fall for him. To do this off topweight on ground he didn't like, took some doing - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: BetUK Kachy Stakes (Listed Race) (All-Weather Championships Fast-Track Qualifier)
quotes.notes: It wasn't the plan to miss the break like that with Annaf but he did it well in the end. The plan is to go straight to all-weather finals day at Newcastle, although he could be a nice horse on turf later on - Mick Appleby, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: We bought him out of Owen Burrows' yard as an unraced two-year-old and he has taken his time to get there. He won twice on the all-weather last year and ran some fine races on turf without winning, but he has really thrived on the all-weather this winter. After a break we brought him back in January at Lingfield, where he won over 6f, and he has since added to that with wins at Kempton and in the Listed Kachy Stakes at Lingfield. Clearly he has improved with age and, although he has risen to a mark of 108, there may be a little more to come and I'd hope to campaign him similarly this summer to last. Before he resumes on the grass he'll go for the 6f race at the all-weather finals meeting on Good Friday, where I hope he'll be hard to beat. 22-03-23

quotes.raceTitle: Win £1M With BetMGM's Golden Goals Handicap
quotes.notes: We've always liked Apiarist and he's thriving. He's picked up a couple of nice prizes and he's progressive. He's maturing with every run and the drop back to seven furlongs today suited him as he's raced keenly in the past. I thought Rab Havlin gave him a fantastic ride. He settled nicely and he has the stamina to stay out this trip. I think he won nicely in the end. This opens up options moving forward for him. The Lincoln could be the starting place for his turf season and those big handicaps are run at a good gallop, so they should suit him - Adam Ryan, trainer's assistant.

We've always liked Apiarist. Last time he went too quick and we took our time today. He's a big, raw horse and he's going to be a lovely three-year-old. He could be a very progressive horse - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a lovely big horse and anything he did last year was a bonus. He's grown again through the winter but has really strengthened up. I might start him off in a 7f conditions race at the Craven meeting, just in case he runs a bit fresh, and then step him up to a mile. I'm sure there are going to be some big days with him. 04-04-24

quotes.notes: Apollo One has been very unlucky, but he's been giving 15lb to improving handicappers. I think at Doncaster he actually thought he'd won. He doesn't really like that ground but there you go. That's him done for the year and he'll go home and rest now - Peter Charalambous, co-trainer.

I'm not sure that the rain has helped Apollo One as it just blunts his acceleration. He is not the biggest, but you don't have to be. He has got a heart like his mother Boonga Roogeta, who was as tough as nails. He is just a lovely, lovely horse. I'd say we will probably go off to Epsom now for the valuable six-furlong handicap on Derby Day - Peter Charalambous, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Get Your Ladbrokes Daily Odds Boost Spring Cup Stakes (Listed Race) (AW Championships F-T Qual')
quotes.notes: I would think that Apollo One would drop back to six furlongs for the sprint on all-weather finals day after that - Martin Harley, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day Cammidge Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Aramram worked at Kempton on Monday and worked super. Sean [Levey, jockey] kind of made me run him, I wanted to go down the handicap route. He has improved from last year, that's very clear and I'm delighted. He's ultra-consistent, he's very talented and his commitment is faultless - Richard Hannon, trainer.

I was positive enough on Aramram and the leader was towing him along really nicely, but a couple others just started to move and I flinched on him, and he picked up a lot quicker than I thought he would. He ended up being in front a big long but he was brave once he realised the horse on his far side started to give him a race, and knuckled back down. He's a lovely, genuine horse and he's been super competitive in some hard races - Tom Marquand, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He showed he's still improving when winning a Listed race at Doncaster last month and stepped up on that when edged out at Newmarket, drawn in the wrong place and finishing very well. He'll be in all the decent sprints this season and I think he'll win a Group 1 - he'll probably go straight to the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes on the Saturday of Royal Ascot. He's pretty versatile with regard to ground. 21-04-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: I've taken so much pleasure from riding this family, with Ace Impact and now him. To win a Group 1 with Arrow Eagle is incredible. I knew turning in I would have too much for the rest of them and it's wonderful. Jean-Claude [Rouget, trainer] took his time to find the key with this horse but Jean-Rene and I always told him it would be the end of the year and over a trip that we would see the best of him. We've all been proved right - Christian Demuro, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Grand Prix de Chantilly In Tribute To His Highness The Aga Khan IV (Group 2) (4yo+) (Turf)
quotes.notes: This race has been the plan since last summer and we've stuck to the route we laid out. Arrow Eagle doesn't move as well as his half-brother but he has a lot of heart. I'm surprised he has become as good as he has. The Arc is the target and he might have one run before - Jean-Claude Rouget, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Renaissance Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: It's taken Art Power a while to get his head back in front, but he has a love affair with the Curragh. He ran really well here first time out this year and, as for last time, five furlongs is probably too sharp for him nowadays. To still have that enthusiasm is a credit to him - David Allan, jockey.

Art Power tries like hell and he ran his heart out. He's got an unbelievable temperament. We thought he'd run well because he wanted a fast seven, he ran well at York over seven furlongs too. If it had been softer it would have been better but he goes on any ground. We'll want to be going to the big race [British Champions Sprint] in October again at Ascot. Where we'll take him between, we don't know yet - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Sprint Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Art Power looked great today. He lost a load of weight when he ran in France but he's just come back. He's just brilliant. We gelded him in January, because we couldn't get a job for him at stud. He takes everything well and is great to train. I thought David gave him a fantastic ride. They broke well and when he travels, he's hard to beat - Tim Easterby, trainer.

Art Power has been awesome and he just loves coming to Ireland for some reason. Nobody knows why, but he just seems to come to life here. Bringing him back to 5f we thought might be an issue, but I've always been confident 5f was going to be okay for him, especially when the ground is soft. It was right up his street there and it's all worked out. He was powering away and I heard the commentator shout that he had gone clear too. We'll have to come back to Ireland now for any race we can find here - David Allan, jockey
Art Power loves it here and he has never been beaten here. He is just a fantastic horse. I cannot say that I was fully confident during the race but it worked out - Oisin Murphy, rider

Art Power bounced the gates, travelled strongly and put it to bed quite nicely. He did it much the same last year, so hopefully he can go to Ascot now and get a bit closer than last year - David Allan, rider.

Art Power travelled strongly and quickened up well. Obviously it was a drop in class and it should have done his confidence a lot of good. Hopefully he can pick up a big one soon - David Allan, rider.

Art Power is a lovely horse, very relaxed and he picked up very sharp. He's very straightforward. He felt like a Group 1 horse. He has a lot of speed and he has a great mind to go with it, for a sprinter especially - Colin Keane, rider

We've always liked Art Power and we took our time with him last year and it seems to have paid off now. I think that could be the end of his handicap days. I don't think dad will want to overface him too soon, but I think things like that (the Nunthorpe) or the Abbaye could be of interest to him - William Easterby, assistant and son of trainer Tim. When I went out there, in my mind I was hoping to get a lead but he was so quick off the gates no one could give me a lead so I just rode the race from the front. He's a very talented horse and I don't think we'll see him in a handicap again. I'd like to see him next year in a Group 1 around here - Silvestre De Sousa, jockey.

Art Power is a nice horse and Tim thinks a lot of him. He's got some classy entries, but he had to prove he could do it. He had a big weight today. Mentally he's not there yet, he's still a big baby, going into the gate he didn't know who he was and on pulling up he was waiting for the others. There's a lot of improvement in him. He's a fast horse, and coming back to five (furlongs) would be no problem - Silvestre De Sousa, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Morag's 10 Years At Racing To School EBF Novice Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.notes: Art Power is a little machine. We've had to wait with him, he's a late foal so we had to give him time. But he's got a great temperament, a fantastic nature. There's no reason why he won't run again this year, though I'm not sure where - Tim Easterby, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's been in great form and I'm very happy with him. He ran a decent race out in Saudi Arabia, where the ground was too quick and he was drawn badly. He's training well and will probably run in the Duke of York Stakes, then go back to Ireland, where he's won five of his six races; I couldn't tell you why he runs so well over there. The plan after that would be the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot. He's seven now, but he still seems as good as ever. 23-04-24

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.notes: It looked like Ascending was outspeeded late on. I thought he'd have quickened a bit better but he ran a blinder and Seamie Heffernan was brilliant on him, he gave him a super ride. We were going better than anything halfway up the straight and then the other lad quickened past us. Fair play to Willie. This was always the plan after Royal Ascot, even prior to that to be honest. We're delighted to be here. It's great for the owners, they've looked after us really well and he's run an absolute belter. There are plenty of options. He's in the Irish Cesarewitch and we'll see. He's a great horse, we'll enjoy today and decide after that - Henry De Bromhead, trainer.

I'm delighted! I wanted to go for the mile and six; I thought Ascending had a great chance, we didn't get in and someone put us in this race and we win! Happy days. It's amazing. He's a star. He was bought to go hurdling and he ran very well over hurdles, but I think he never really loved it, so I said we'd try going back on the Flat. David Roach, who works for me, said, 'there's a good one in this lad on the Flat', so we started going that route. Chris's son Andrew [Jones] rode him in some nice amateur races last year and that was great fun, unlucky not to win one day, and then we've just kept going along this route and it's been incredible. I think we'll stay on the Flat - he seems to love it. Billy [Lee, jockey] said he got knocked down after a furlong, so he opted to go out and get a bit of light, and the horse travelled beautifully. He gave him a super ride; he knew he had a kick so he kicked a bit earlier than he'd planned, but he just said he'd try it and it worked well - Henry De Bromhead, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's been running well on the Flat and we'll probably give him one more run at Dundalk and then maybe go for a maiden hurdle at Christmas. His maiden hurdle form is good and hopefully he can win one. 18-11-24

He came to us from Clive Cox having won a Goodwood mile handicap in the summer. His first run over hurdles gave us plenty of encouragement when a half-length second to Tekao at Leopardstown over Christmas. His next run was in the Grade 1 Spring Juvenile Hurdle at the Dublin Racing Festival and he ran well enough to be fourth behind Gala Marceau. He has an entry in the Triumph Hurdle and we'll see how he is much nearer the race before deciding whether to send him over for that. 01-03-23

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.raceTitle: Prix de l'Abbaye de Longchamp Longines (Group 1) (2yo+) (Sprint Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: It's just surreal really. We had a couple of little pre-race issues, we had to work through those. We were within a minute and a half of not running - I had an Uber driver on a retainer of 200euros to get the mare's passport here in time. We try to experience new things. I've never been to the races in France and here we are winning a Group 1 on Arc day - Henry Dwyer, trainer of Asfoora.Asfoora was fantastic. The sprint course is a fair bit drier than the round course and she was basically on the bridle throughout. She was fortunate to have a plum [low] draw and I didn't have to ask her much but her condition was the best it's been on the build up to this race. She still has her summer coat and it took some amount of management - Oisin Murphy, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

It seems surreal, silly and it's all been a novelty. I've really been on a holiday with Asfoora the last two years. It was all getting a bit hard before Ascot as we didn't have the transport, and if I'm 100 per cent honest, if I owned her I wouldn't have come back. Akram [El-Fahkri, owner] was very insistent we did and that she deserved another chance. I'd love to see the replay as I was under a scrum of people for the last bit, but that looked very convincing. When you know they're going to win at the two-furlong marker, you're on pretty good terms with yourself. It was an easy watch and really enjoyable. She'll tell us if she doesn't want to be racing any more, but after that you can't say that's the case. She's been a once-in-a-lifetime horse for two years in a row and who knows, maybe three. That'll be a decision for Akram. He's a sportsman and would love to keep her going, why wouldn't you? We can't rule out coming back next year, but she owes us nothing - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Asfoora has run well but she was 6-4 favourite so you like to see those ones win. She didn't so we're probably a little bit disappointed but it's not as though she's run tenth. She's run well but probably not as well as her last couple. I didn't like her last 50 metres, she was there to run second or at least third and she was a little bit plain in that last little bit. Whether she's reached her peak or she's on the way down, or whether she didn't like the track, I'm not sure. We might go to Ireland for the Flying Five but if anything comes out of the run and we're not happy with her she'll be going home - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

Asfoora has gone as well as we could have hoped and we're very proud of her. You could just tell about 400 metres after the start she just came off the bridle. She's quick but they were a bit quick for her early. Big Evs controlled his own destiny whereas we were stuck behind a couple and got a bit of a bump which probably cost us the win but she's run well and we're more than happy just to be competing - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: We needed a lead-up run at Haydock, so we were always going to come early, but just with the changing of seasons we wanted to be here before it was too cold in Australia and too warm. We came over in the nice interchange period and Asfoora settled in brilliantly. The proof of that was in the pudding today. I've got to have a look at the race conditions again but we'd love to showcase her a bit. Everyone has just been so good to us over here and I'd love to send her down to Goodwood and up to York, but we'll put the horse first - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.notes: It was a fantastic run. Aspect Island is improving all the time and he's come a long way since Yarmouth. Tasleet improved; he got quicker. He's a big horse, but he handled this well. We've learned a bit and he's learned a good bit as well, so we'll be looking forward to next year with him - James Owen, trainer.

That was a step back in the right direction, and Audience probably wants quicker ground than today. I was trying to give myself a bit of space in the straight and Quinault kept coming with me, but he finished his race off and in the last furlong he was coming back again. I think the cheekpieces helped, as that was better than he had been doing this year - Rab Havlin, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: Audience got upset in the stalls and he struck the front of the stalls a couple of times when the other one reared up. Rab said he wasn't himself after that, he wouldn't let down at all - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Audience has always had the talent but Rab knows him well. He was kept in training as a lead horse to Inspiral, as he was in the Lockinge. He's improving with age so there's hope for us all yet. He's matured a lot mentally. It wasn't a fluke in the Lockinge. The mile was too stiff at Ascot. Rab really knows him. He rides him most mornings - and then he takes him home. We'll go to the City of York without a penalty. We've put him in the Foret - last year's ground would have been perfect. He wouldn't want traditionally Parisian ground. He could well be a Breeders' Cup Mile horse as well - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Shaqab Lockinge Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Last year Audience wasn't giving himself a chance, we were running him over sprint trips to start. He was a little bit of a thug. He'd run some great races over seven furlongs last year, really staying on towards the end, and even towards the backend this was always going to be the starting point. We didn't think he'd be good enough to beat Inspiral but he's always threatened to win a big one. It's his first run over a mile and last year he never would have got a mile, he was too like a bull in a china shop. He's come back at the winner a couple of times last year, good horses like Kinross, he's had good horses around him. If he can improve over a mile - which he clearly has - there's some nice races to win with him - Rab Havlin, jockey, speaking on ITV racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Cavani Menswear Fashion Face-Off Frenzy Criterion Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: It is all down to Leah (Mapston) who looks after Audience and rides him every day. He was not right in the spring but he has come right now. I think the hood helps him a lot. Rab (Havlin) went up that ground this morning and it is completely fresh, virgin ground and that was a little bit of knowing your track. He is in races like the Lennox but he enjoyed the straight track here and seven furlongs is very much his trip - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.notes: Aventure ran well in the Ganay when there was no great pace on and didn't quite get the gap when she needed it, although we were up against the exceptional Daryz, who is certainly the best horse we've seen in recent years. The Wertheimers have shown over the years they're very sporting owners and decided to go again with her this year, so I hope she can continue to repay them. Her next race will be either the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud or Pretty Polly. Everyone within the team will have their say. My preference would be Ireland. She loves a good pace to run at and in those conditions she has a real turn of foot - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Maxime [Guyon, jockey] said Aventure wasn't quite as fresh today. She had a good trip round but she wasn't able to pick up in the straight. She's a Group 1 winner and a multiple Group winner. She's had a great career, she's won a Vermeille, been second in an Arc and a Vermeille, won lots of good races. The list is a long one. I hope I get to train her offspring and we'll have to see whether she stays in training at five. It's been a wonderful adventure chasing the Arc for a second season - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix Vermeille (Group 1) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: That was fantastic, Aventure won very well. We didn't know about the Irish fillies but she did very well. When she came out in the straight she really made a good acceleration, and was very confident all the way. I'm very pleased as my mission was to win a Group 1 with her, and that's done so it's a good thing. She will be better in four weeks' time, I think. She's coming along now as I don't think she really likes the summer - she's better now. She's the perfect filly to train - Christophe Ferland, trainer.It's true that Aventure is a filly who really deserved to win one; always finishing second as she was in the Arc, and always beaten by a crack. As a team we decided to miss Deauville [Romanet] and concentrate on this race and she was absolutely on her game - Maxime Guyon, jockey.

Aventure ran really well. Calandagan is a rock, he has a real turn of foot. To finish second in a Group 1 against the boys is great and we were beaten by the better horse. Next stop will be the Prix Jean Romanet - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

We knew Aventure would progress a lot for her comeback, which was a pretty easy success. She's won well there and she'll need to progress again when she steps back into Group 1 company, which will be here in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud. There's never a worry with her; she is an extraordinary filly to have anything to do with and undoubtedly the best horse I have ever trained, to this point at least. Dabirsim was a very different horse and and the fastest horse I've ever worked with in the mornings and the afternoons. But she is so consistent and she's running at these Classic distances; in my eyes she is a queen - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix Allez France (Group 3) (4yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: On that evidence the Curragh against her own sex now comes into the reckoning, because we could look at keeping her to 2,000 metres [ten furlongs]. Aventure has grown and strengthened over the winter and while she is quite lightly made, she has muscled up through her shoulder and behind - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Aventure has run the perfect race, she was exceptional. We had the same fight as in the Vermeille. Obviously there is some regret that we were second but it was a beautiful second in an Arc de Triomphe. When she went after the leader there was a moment when I thought she'd do it but we've once again come across a real racehorse and an exceptional four-year-old filly - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix de Pomone (Group 2) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Round Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Aventure had a proper holiday on the farm after the Diane and only came back to me in July, so I really hadn't got much work into her. From that point of view, I loved what she did and Stephane's comments were very reassuring as well, because he always felt he had the others covered and was delighted with the way she picked up - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

Avicenna is learning on the job, was strong through the line and is a horse to look forward to. He's always looked a good horse and we felt he took a good step forward at home since that first run. He'll get a mile, whether this year or next. I think he'll probably be a miler, I don't know whether he's good enough for a Guineas, he's just won a Listed by a nose. He's a nice horse, we don't need to get carried away yet - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He needs more match practice and is likely to run in either the Craven or the Greenham. I've been really happy with him in the last fortnight and we're hopeful that he could be a Guineas candidate of some description. He's in the English, Irish, French and German 2,000 Guineas, and how he runs in Craven week will dictate the next step. I think he'll get a mile well and he's done nothing wrong so far. There's no reason why we can't get excited. 01-04-26

He's a nice horse, he's done nothing wrong and is two from two having won the Flying Scotsman at Doncaster recently. I didn't think he'd won watching it live. I was probably 50 yards short of the finish line and I didn't think he could make up the ground, but he got the head bob. He was very willing under William Buick and we can take a lot away from that. I'm delighted that having received yearlings from the Godolphin team and Sheikh Mohammed for the first time, the first horse that we've got on the track is a tidy performer. That's very satisfying. I'd like to run him again this season but I'm not sure in which race yet. I don't think he's an autumn-ground horse - William thought he just got away with it at Doncaster. He isn't in the Dewhurst or the Lagardere and they're probably unlikely, unless he's supplemented, but he has come out of his last race really well and I don't want to put a line through running him again. I've got to speak to the team, but I might entertain the idea of something like the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf. He's definitely going to stay a mile but I don't think he's ready for an autumn mile. The Autumn Stakes is often won by a middle-distance horse, for example. I think he could stay at 7f or a two-turn American mile on fast ground could suit him, so we'll have that in the back of our minds and see how he progresses over the next fortnight or so. 24-09-25

quotes.notes: We always felt Aylin would stay and she's proved she's up to this Group level. She was very fit and well in herself, so I don't think you'll improve much on fitness with her. It's just a question now of whether she can hold her form for another month and we can run her in a Group 1 in either the Fillies' Mile or the Prix Marcel Boussac - Karl Burke trainer.

Azure Angel travelled really well through the race and the headgear obviously helped her. I was told she's very straightforward. She travels really well, but her bursts don't last that long, so they thought the headgear would help for that final half-furlong. I probably ended up a bit further back than ideal, but I got on to the back of the favourite and she killed the race off quite quickly - Billy Loughnane, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Handicap
quotes.notes: That was Azure Angel's first run back at five furlongs and it proved to be the right step, she looks very fast. I'm really pleased with her and we can look at a nice handicap with her now. We've got plenty of options going forwards - Edward Bethell.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallions Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands C & D) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: We were pretty confident about Azure Angel running really well today. We knew she wanted six furlongs as she just held on over seven furlongs last time. She seems quite a classy filly - Courtney Wyatt, owners' spokesperson.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's very fast and looks as though she's improved for dropping down to five furlongs. That was the angle we always wanted to play as her work had been very fast at home, but we needed the cojones to do it. Roger Varian had been running her over six furlongs and you'd take note of what he'd been doing, but we may have found her niche. She won well at Redcar and then ran well on her step up in grade at York, where she was drawn on the wing. I'd imagine her main aim will be the fillies' handicap back there at the Ebor meeting. 02-07-25

A huge run. A little bit frustrating Balantina started a touch slow, like she did her first run, but ran massive. I thought it was a good salvage performance to go and pick up a place, as it was tough work from where she was - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Tally Ho Stud Irish EBF Fillies Maiden

When they finish one-two you probably think you should have split them up but it is nice that they both ran well anyway - Donnacha Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

He's in the Derby and Jane [Chapple-Hyam] thinks highly of him and I thought we've got to make a man of him at some point. He responded really well to pressure and he's going to get further. He's a big unfurnished horse so there's plenty more to come - Hollie Doyle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.notes: That was maybe a career-best when you think of the penalty [5lb]. Bay City Roller was well-prepared and it was a strong race. You'd always prefer to win but I thought it was a very good run. He's fine over ten to 12 furlongs on ground with soft in the description, and they'll look for the weather for him - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

It all just came together perfectly today and Bay City Roller was able to show just how good he is. Fundamentally he stays very well and he loves to get his toe in. I think we've properly worked him out now. We know what's required of him next year and how to ride him and that will help us map out a season of Group 1s accordingly. He relishes some cut in the ground and there have been times when he's slightly missed the break. But today I felt he looked the best he's looked and that's credit to everyone at home for keeping him in such good form for the duration of the year. He has a really bright future and he's so well bred - George Scott, trainer.
Bay City Roller has run an absolute blinder. We came here thinking he'd run a big race and it's nice to see him do that - George Scott, trainer.

Bay City Roller was very well positioned by Callum [Shepherd] under the circumstances and ran with great credit, showing a very good attitude. On the day he was beaten by a better horse, one with a big reputation. But we're very happy with the way he's progressing. We feel there's a lot more to come from Bay City Roller if he gets a bit stronger and really starts to express himself at a mile and a quarter, maybe even a mile and a half one day - George Scott, trainer.

Sadly John and Thady's horse came out the front and blasted the race apart slightly with the pace angle but Bay City Roller got some pace to aim at and travelled great, it was a very pleasing run. He's a really genuine horse. He's done everything he needed to today. Stiffer tests await him but it will be fascinating to see how he gets on. I quite like the Lagardere for him because he's very well balanced - George Scott, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: IRE-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: It's never easy giving a penalty away, especially when you've got some strong connections in the race. I felt he needed some more game time under his belt before we stepped up into Pattern company and he got it. He had to get down and fight a very nice prospect, who's bred to go on the surface. He knows how to get down and dirty and that's going to stand him in great stead moving forward. Shaikh Nasser is obviously a major patron of the yard and has some nice two-year-olds. Bay City Roller has been working in among those, so he's seen the horse throughout the year. When he went to Sandown and won nicely, he inquired whether he might be for sale and it turned out he was. I don't want to run him with firm in the going description. His mum loved cut, he's got quite big feet and he'll be a different horse on soft ground. I'd say the Champagne is very much on his radar. From there, it will be a question of whether it's a sales race or a Group 1 - George Scott, trainer.

I think we'll see how it pans out over the next couple of weeks and how it's shaking out. I'd love to have a go. He's a cool customer and he's going to handle the whole jamboree. He's going to stay too. Based on that, he's also going to handle the track, so that's three good reasons to run. He's just a really straightforward individual and we know he's a lovely horse, which is part of the battle - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

It was a very different race to Goodwood. We were coming back a furlong so I wanted to make sure we went a proper gallop. Bay Of Brilliance stays very well and loves this ground. I was impressed, he saw them off early and powered away. He was very dominant with a penalty, which is a hard thing to do. Hopefully he'll be a nice stayer for next season. He's very mature and gets on with the job, I couldn't fault that - Hector Crouch, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A nice colt who did well last year for an immature type. He's done well over the winter and could go to Chester or Lingfield for a Derby trial. He'll stay very well and I'm pleased with him. 27-04-26

quotes.notes: Beautiful Diamond deserved that and clearly didn't see the six out last time. She's all about speed, Clifford just let her roll along and it all came to her. I'm not sure if she'll run again this year, but she's probably done enough for the season and could go away now. She might get six furlongs next year on better ground but we'll probably stay over five. We'll definitely be looking at Group level now - Philip Robinson, owner's racing manager.

Beautiful Diamond is still a bit of a weak filly to be honest. She's had a hard race today and we'll give her a nice easy month and then take it on from there. She's a good filly for the future. Our other two ran blinders too - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Beautiful Diamond was a bit edgy when she came but we've not really pushed any buttons with her at home. I said whatever she did today she'll improve on, and we had to train her with the handbrake on leading into the race - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's done really well physically from three to four and will head to the Palace House at the Guineas meeting to start her season. She was on the tails of some good sprinters last year and I think she's got a chance of being bang there in those Group races. She looks all speed and beyond Newmarket we can look at races like the Temple. 11-04-25

He came fourth at the Breeders' Cup last year when he handled Del Mar really well and we wouldn't be scared to go back. We think he's equally good over five or six and we've got a few options as he's got an entry on Champions Day and we might even consider the Abbaye - Paul Teasdale, owner.It was a brilliant spare ride. I was actually supposed to ride Big Mojo in the Sandy Lane earlier this season but we [Godolphin] ran Symbol Of Honour at the last minute. It has all come together and we've got the job done today. It was genuinely beautiful good ground today. I thought middle to stand side is probably where you wanted to be. The way the race and our draw [15] panned out was very helpful but he still put up a very good performance today. He was very smooth, and I didn't really have a moment of worry at all ? he just got on with it and saw it out well - William Buick, jockey.

It's great, Big Mojo is an exciting horse and he's improved a lot since his debut. It's a nice way to break a maiden, in a Group 3 race, and he's a pro horse. He's only going to improve. He's got a lot of speed and I like him over six as well. He's a quality horse going forward, he's strong physically but mentally he's not there yet - Silvestre de Sousa, rider.
