Billyjoh loved the ground, he never missed a foot on it. I don't think he's beaten a bad field there and being so green, I think you have to kind of upgrade that as well - Frederick Larson, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

Binhareer is just really coming to himself now. He's learned to relax and we've figured out his trip. Black Caviar Gold is a nice filly and we've taken our time with her and let her come to us. She won impressively on rain-softened ground last time and I thought she was ready for a step into this company. She had sore shins in the spring and that's why I was looking for softer ground this year. I think as she gets older and stronger, the ground will make no difference. She's had four runs now and is a fine, big filly, and I hope all her career is in front of her. I'd say that's it for this year - Paddy Twomey, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: Black Caviar Gold had a good run in Galway then we ran her here on ground that was probably a bit quick. I think she's ready to step up and the Weld Park Stakes on Goffs Million weekend could be a good fit for her - Paddy Twomey, trainer, speaking to Racing TV. Black Caviar Gold jumped and travelled away and has done it nicely. We didn't go mad but she picked up well and just got lonely in front, so I just let her drift over and have the rail. She galloped all the way to the line and is one to improve again - Billy Lee, jockey.

Blanc De Blanc is a very raw and big, strong filly. She was keen the last day and jumped well again today but I had to let her go forward to try and get in as I didn't want to be caught out wide and she just grabbed it. We were going a good gallop and we weren't properly doing things right and I thought I might pay the price, but when I gave her a squeeze down to the furlong pole she just took off. She'll get a trip in time, she has a big engine and she's going the right way - Donagh O'Connor, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.notes: Boiling Point is a very honest horse. The ground's probably not ideal for him, but he's so tough and genuine. I'd a good willing partner and he really did help me out a lot there -  Shane Gray, rider.

Boiling Point is a very good horse and is really a Group horse - he will win a good Group race. But Cliff [Lee, jockey] is so good from the front. There was no point pulling him round, even with top-weight. It was all about getting him into a nice rhythm and he was either going to be good enough or he wasn't. We were always going to go far side from that draw (6) and it has worked out really well. I don't know how much weight exactly he was giving the second, but he's just held on. He was running on fumes for the last 100 yards but as I say Cliff is brilliant from the front and I'm never worried when I ask him to go forward. He will go back into Group company now. I don't know where yet - today was the plan - Karl Burke, trainer.

I need to speak his owner Sheikh Obaid but he has had two quick runs now and I would quite like to put him away and wait for the Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot. The stiff seven furlongs there should suit him and I thought all through the winter that it could be the race for him. After that, we can decide whether we step him up to a mile. In my opinion, it looks like he would stay a mile - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran in the Queen's Prize at Kempton and will ply his trade in those sorts of races but he possibly needs to find a bit off his current mark. Billy [Loughnane] wasn't sure he fully stayed at this grade, so we might drop back in trip. 02-04-26

He will come forward a lot for it and all these horses are running with Ascot in mind but Ryan said it might come too quick because he was so babyish. We'll see how much he comes on. He said he'd have no problem getting seven and he's a massive, big, powerful horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Byzantine Dream ran really well. He proved he is up to Group 1 level and that he is good enough to challenge in these top races, even though he's a Group 2 horse at home. We are thrilled with his performance - Tomoyasu Sakaguchi, trainer.

There's more to come and I expect Byzantine Dream to be at his best for the Arc. We've left plenty to work on as today was only his prep run. I think the state of the ground is something we'll have to think about but the priority is how to prepare the horse well between now and the Arc. We'll worry about the ground nearer the time - Tomoyasu Sakaguchi, trainer.  Byzantine Dream relaxed very well in Saudi and I felt in the Tenno Sho last time he never relaxed behind Redentor. He was always too keen and did well to finish second. Today he got into a good rhythm and beat a good field. He'll need this ground or even faster would be better on the big day to be at his best - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Longines Red Sea Turf Handicap (Group 2) (3yo+) (Inner Track) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Byzantine Dream broke OK but I thought there would be a reasonable amount of pace and they went quicker than I expected. He felt super under me yesterday morning, although I only had about two hours' sleep when I got on him, but it was worth it. These are very famous colours [Kazumi Yoshida] and it was great to wear them and get on him. He had a good run in the Japanese St Leger and that was good enough here. He has a great turn of foot and I never had to touch his mouth on the run around and that always helps. From the time they went by the winning post the first time, as long as I did everything right, from there he was going to win - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

My only concern would be if it was really hot like it was last year and the ground was really fast [at Royal Ascot]. Anything else Caballo De Mar is fine on. He's fine with cut in the ground, he's fine on fast. It's just if it's 'summer' fast it would be a problem. But he stays so well, I actually thought he had a better chance of winning the Gold Cup than this race. I think the two miles four there is just him all over, we know he stays. He's a special racehorse. Eliza [McCalmont] rides him every day, and she's done a great job, and everyone at home. Luke [Morris, on Consent] kind of took his nose off a little bit at halfway and actually I think that helped us because we had something to run at. I think we would have got racing a bit early otherwise. The Gold Cup has really been on our mind for so long but he was just jumping out of his skin, so we decided to come here, and we're so glad we did. It is rarefied air, to win a Group 1, so it's very special for all of us. And I'm so pleased for Shaikh Nasser, who's just given me so much, so many opportunities. He was here last year with Shaikh Khalid for the Cadran and it's nice to repay those people who give you so much -  George Scott, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix du Cadran (Group 1) (4yo+) (New & Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: It's a special day for me and my team, we finally got there. The owners have been a big part of my journey, so to train a Group 1 winner feels surreal. I've been training for ten years and we've had loads of stakes winners, but I'm elated we've won our first at the highest level. I was on the floor as Caballo De Mar crossed the line. I don't normally get emotional, that's what it means to me. He has his whole future ahead of him at this level and he might not be done this season - there are a couple of big dances left, then he'll head out to the Middle East. He's a unique character. He's so tough and durable, so we'll see how he is and make a decision  - George Scott, trainer.

Adrie said Caballo De Mar was fine on the ground and it all went like clockwork. This is a very good young horse, he knows how to win and he was second at Royal Ascot so he was entitled to run well. We will take him home and see how he is but he will be prepared for a campaign in the Middle East. He could end up in Saudi for the Red Sea Handicap and then hopefully all roads lead to the Gold Cup on World Cup night in Dubai - George Scott, trainer.

Caballo De Mar is a really admirable horse who knows how to win. We needed to go up a couple of pounds to guarantee our spot in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot, so we've done that - George Scott, trainer.

Caballo De Mar has run a great race. Callum [Shepherd] said he was riding almost with one rein most the way round as he didn't really love the track, but ran a monster race. He's got his whole future ahead of him in this sphere and he'll go to Royal Ascot now. We'll take a view where as the winner's a very good horse coming off the jumps and was well-handicapped - George Scott, trainer.

quotes.notes: Caballo De Mar has been a slow burner but has been well placed by George (Scott, trainer). He's uncomplicated and stayed on really well. He should stay further again - Daniel Muscutt, jockey.

quotes.notes: Calandagan is a fantastic champion and I'm so lucky to train a horse of this calibre. This race was tactical and I was a little bit worried but when he found his stride in the straight he was just unbelievable to watch. This is his fifth Group 1 in a row and he has a big reputation so I felt a lot of pressure today. We're ready to kick on again this season - Francis Graffard, trainer. Calandagan is an incredible horse, he's got his own attitude and I know him very well now - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.

I knew I was bringing the best horse in the world, but was exposing Calandagan in a race that's almost impossible to win. I said to myself it wasn't really fair on the horse to ask that of him, and I really felt that pressure today. I thought to myself, 'What if we have to take him back home to his box, where there would be a plaque saying 'best horse in the world', and for his year to end in disappointment?' We were asking him to do something quite incredible after he had already proved he was the best, so I felt an enormous weight on my shoulders. I love taking on these big challenges, but this morning I was really wondering why we were putting ourselves through it  -  Francis Graffard, trainer.

Calandagan is a fantastic horse and we're lucky to have very nice horses this year who can compete at the top level, so I was able to give him a break before preparing him for this. He arrived in top form and is a real champion. Work is easy for him and I worked him with Daryz before Arc weekend because I needed to get him ready for today. He showed Daryz how it worked and to have a gallop with an Arc and Champion Stakes winner is unbelievable. We always know he will give his all. I was thinking of the Japan Cup for him next, but that's a tough race to win so we will see how he is and discuss it with the team - Francis Graffard, trainer.We went a nice gallop early on, but when Calandagan found his stride he was ready to go on the approach to the straight. I could feel Ombudsman coming to me but I was going much better than him. He's a very good horse - Mickael Barzalona, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: What happened in the race came as a surprise. I was upset I didn't put [last year's winner] Goliath in the race today because everyone was expecting a lot of pace, but I have no regrets now seeing how the race was run. Aidan [O'Brien, trainer] and his team put a lot of work into the tactics and it's always interesting, but Calandagan is an easy ride and I'm glad he had time to come and catch the filly.  Mickael [Barzalona, jockey] said the last 200 metres are long here and he knew he was going to catch her, but when she kicked for home she was impressive and I thought, 'Oh my God, I'm going to finish second by a neck again' - Francis Graffard, trainer.We know Calandagan's quality and today the ground was quicker and he's one of these top-class horses. I didn't expect Jan Brueghel to set the pace but once I saw Continuous beside him and Rebel's Romance boxed in, I was happy where I was because I knew either William [Buick] was going to make a gap or Oisin [Murphy] was going to have to go round. I was just waiting to see what happened and when I saw Oisin making the move, I just followed - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.

Well, Calandagan is not ungenuine! The race went really well for him and I thought he was travelling much more into the rhythm of the race this time. Mickael said he still had to ask him to keep up sometimes during the race but then in the straight, when there is rhythm and he can follow the pace, he can really lengthen and quicken really strongly. I thought he was really impressive there. After Epsom my first conclusion was that he needed the run against that horse on that ground. I thought he'd come on a lot for that and he's getting experience, while his jockey knows him better now. I will obviously discuss it [the King George] with connections but it seems sensible to go to Ascot, a place where he has won before. I need to take him there at 100 per cent. I don't think ground is important to him but you could see there the way he really accelerated on that good going. He's won on very soft ground as well but I hope we get good ground and that I can get him in peak form for the end of July and go there with a real chance. In any case I'm pleased we decided to stay home with him this time. - Francis Graffard, trainer.

The horse had a perfect run and got the ride we were thinking of. Going down the hill he found himself behind Ryan (Moore on the winner) and he gave him plenty of time to balance. Calandagan probably took the lead for a small moment and then when they started to climb again you could see that Ryan was finding more. He's a very talented horse and I'm sure he'll win a Group One as he always runs his race. There are no excuses and I think it was a good performance. Don't forget he ran in Dubai and he hasn't run in Europe until this race. I think he was ready, but the winner is a tough O'Brien horse who keeps finding more. He's in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud. - Francis-Henri Graffard, trainer.

Calandagan was slow out of the stalls and he takes so much time to get into his rhythm. Mickael [Brazalona] said during the race he was happy they weren't going faster because he needed to get going. I don't have any excuses. In the straight we were following the winner and he had the first kick. He came really fast at the end. It was a very good start of the season for him. The plan is to go to Epsom for the Coronation Cup with him, but we'll see how he comes back from Dubai. It's a very good run and Mickael will know him more for the future, too - Francis Graffard, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco Champion Stakes (British Champions Middle Distance) (Group 1)
quotes.notes: I thought the race was over when Calandagan took the lead and to be fair I didn't see the winner coming. He ran a great race and well done to the winning connections. He was slow away and he [Stephane Pasquier] tried to put him in the race then he travelled nicely. He had his chance to win but the winner beat us on the line - Francis Graffard, trainer, speaking to ITV.

It was a fantastic run, but the odds were right. The stride Calandagan showed in the straight was fantastic to watch. I shouted as we thought we were coming to get him, but he could only keep pushing a champion in City Of Troy. I'm very proud of the horse. We didn't have any Group 1 form before and there were lots of question marks, but the way he accelerated was fantastic. He can come back to Ascot in the Champion Stakes, but we'll discuss it. He gave a lot of heart on the track today - Francis Graffard, trainer.

Everything was easy. Calandagan can be a naughty boy sometimes, and we have to ask him gently. Today he wanted to do everything - when he's like this, he is a fantastic horse. I didn't do anything, I just asked him to do it by himself - Stephane Pasquier, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: His form has worked out quite well but it will obviously be a different proposition at Ascot. He's a proper horse who has done everything very easily this year, while he's indifferent to the ground. He's very easy actioned and covers a lot of ground so I don't think the mile and a half will be a problem. 13-06-24

quotes.notes: Carla Ridge is a filly we loved from the day we bought her. She was a bit disappointing at the Curragh but she did today what we hoped she might be capable of and showed that she could be a stakes filly - Patrick Harty, joint trainer.

I knew Carmers would stay and I knew turning in Billy [Lee] looked comfortable and I was happy to see the horse come outside him and just not have him at the front and that he was able to get a breather into him round the bottom. He looked comfortable when the bell rang and I was thinking we had a chance. I think staying is his game and he's a pretty good horse. He's done everything we've asked of him and he will have an entry in the St Leger at Doncaster and we'll see, he's done what we've asked him to do today; he's run three times and won three times and hopefully he'll continue doing it - Paddy Twomey, trainer.Race went to plan all the way, jumped well, had a great position, when Harry came around I just let Carmers go on and was able to just hack away but got him rolling early from five out just to get him going forward; he takes a while to build up a head of steam and I know he'd stay well. I wanted to stretch them so I was always going to try and make it a stamina test and you can see him there pricking his ears going to the line, just doing enough. Staying was always going to be a forte of his. He's so laid back at home, he wouldn't pass out the dog at home, he's just that type of character, he saves plenty. I knew when I got stuck into him he'd keep finding away - Billy Lee, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Yeats Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: He's a horse who des just what he has to do, hence the headgear. I thought Carmers would be in the first three at Ballinrobe but he surprised me how well he won at the line. He came home, licked the pot, rode out this week and didn't care so we decided to come here and see what happens. We knew he'd stay but we didn't want to make it, he's a horse who probably doesn't want to be in front too long. To be fair he kept on well, he's keeping plenty to himself. The Queen's Vase is probably the race for him - Paddy Twomey, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's unbeaten and has done nothing wrong. I liked what I saw from him at Navan last time and the Queen's Vase has always been the plan for him. I think the race will really suit him. 13-06-25

quotes.notes: It was maybe trainer error last year, I stretched Catalina Delcarpio out to 1m4f in the Ribblesdale and I'd say she has too much speed for that. She had a setback after she ran in Ascot so she was just ready to start back when she ran in the Park Express and I thought she'd come forward from it. I think she can step up to ten furlongs no problem but she has pace for a mile. I doubt she'd go for the Lanwades as we have City Of Memphis and One Look as well for that. Catalina Delcaprio is a lovely filly, ran a career best. Probably just didn't all out see out the trip today, but I think when she's a little bit stronger and a little bit older, she will. She's a filly who is just coming into herself and I think she will be a very good four-year-old, and we will take our time. We side-stepped Epsom and races like that on purpose, because I think it was coming too soon for her. We will have a think, I doubt I'll run her in the Irish Oaks. Maybe something like a Blandford Stakes at Irish Champions weekend, something like that, over ten furlongs. We will just give her a bit of time to fill up. She's a very nice filly. When I bought her at the sales, she was a nice filly then. She's improved and improved all the way through her career. She's a nice big filly. Lope De Vega is a fantastic sire, she has a good pedigree - Paddy Twomey, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: Catalina Delcarpio is a nice filly. She was just ready to start and most of mine on debut can be green and she was, but I thought if we would have a first-time-out maiden winner this year it could be her. She trains very well and finds everything very easy, and I just thought she might have enough class to carry her through. I told the owner last week I was going to put her in the Epsom Oaks and then I said I wasn't going to as it was too soon in her development. I have the Irish Oaks in mind for her - Paddy Twomey, speaking on Racing TV.

He'd have a penalty in that [Hampton Court], but he won't mind and could go somewhere like that. The good thing is that Ryan said he will stay further. He could end up in the Irish Derby, we'll see what will happen in the next couple of weeks. He's done his trial now if he does go. He's a hardy boy and he'll only ever do what he has to do. When the cheekpieces go back on, they will be a help to him too - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

We just wanted to get a run into him for this. He's ready. He's done his prep for it now. He'd be very comfortable coming back here for the Guineas - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Racing Writers Association Madrid Handicap
quotes.notes: Causeway was tough and he learned a lot. He took a run last year, he was a little bit lazy. He'll obviously stay a lot further. Ryan was good on him. I think he'll be very comfortable going a mile and could get further. He's brave, he stuck his head out. He can go into a winners' race now and we'll go gentle with him and let him mature away -  Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Bermingham Cameras Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.notes: Causeway is a lovely, big, scopey horse who's laid-back. He had a lovely run at Gowran and was staying on well. He went forward down past the two and then he felt like he parked a bit. There was something that came on the stands' side and he actually went forward again so I'd say it was company he was waiting for - Wayne Lordan, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won the Madrid Handicap on his return at Naas this month. He was tough and learned a lot from that. He took a run to find his form last year as he was a little bit lazy. quotes.raceTitle: Maureen Brittain Memorial Empress Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Celandine has got loads of boot and is very tough and Tom thinks she is not done yet. I don't think we'll be going up in trip even though she's in the Moyglare Stud Stakes, and we may have to supplement her for something nice - Ed Walker, trainer.

She's back cantering and hopefully will be spot on for Newmarket. 11-09-24

quotes.notes: It's 50 years of work by the family, going from a small yard, switching from National Hunt to Flat and and always believing that buying horses and believing that they're going to be good. It's a lifetime's ambition to have a Group 1 winner. Cercene is by Australia, a sire I love, and her half-brother won the Britannia so the pedigree was there and if she was an inch bigger I wouldn't have her. I was hoping Lake Victoria stayed because we'd have a lesser race and then we'd have place and ride her easier you know what I mean. She travelled well, Gary gave her a great ride, and we were thinking that being by Australia she'd stay as well. She was headed and came back again. She waited for something to head her but she's very tough and a dream to train. The plan was today so now we'll draw new plans - Joseph Murphy, trainer.
Cercene will have no problem going up to a mile and a quarter. Gary [Carroll, jockey] said the further she was going, the better she was getting - Joe Murphy, trainer.

Circene looked to be going nowhere and then won well. We think she's a very good filly. The Park Stakes might come a bit soon for her, but she is in the EBF Final here in the autumn, but she might be finished for this year - Joe Murphy junior, assistant trainer.

Cerro Blanco has got some engine and we'd thought about the Wood Ditton but we thought we'd start him off over seven furlongs as he has plenty of boot. We'll take baby steps with him at this stage and maybe look for a novice after this -  Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.notes: Ryan [Moore] felt Charles Darwin lost his action. He said he felt he hit a ridge and he might have bruised a shoulder and that's why he stood up on him, so we'll see. So maybe there's something there - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Committed Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: It's a long time since Charles Darwin ran and he should come on a ton from it. As he gets fitter, you'd imagine he'll sharpen up. The plan is to go to Naas next and then go to the Commonwealth Cup-  Aidan O'Brien, speaking on Racing TV.

Charles Darwin is a very fast, big, powerful, strong horse. He's big, mature, physical and a very good mind as well so he's very exciting. We were obviously hoping that he would get a lead but he's very quick; we would be happy to get a lead, he never sees the front at home in his work, he's always very happy to sit but he's very strong and very quick. Ryan obviously does his own thing always, the gates open and he decides so he was very happy; he said he powered through the line so couldn't be happier really. Albert Einstein was always something that we've never seen before. This horse is very fast, he's a sprinter; I don't know how far he is going to get, he's very quick. The horse on Tuesday [Gstaad] looked like he'd get seven and that means he could get a mile - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Very professional horse, super attitude. Charles Darwin jumped very quick, showed good speed, I was just trying to control him the best I could. They came to me about the two and a half and I asked him to go and he picked up well. Very good horse. He's got a good brain, he's obviously a very mature, very strong two-year-old; another No Nay Never like the filly yesterday [True Love]. He's doing everything right, doing everything really lovely, couldn't be happier with him really. He'll get six [furlongs] - Ryan Moore, jockey.

We're very happy with Charles Darwin. He just needed a nice sharp bit before Ascot and it was nice to do it on lovely ground. Ryan was very happy with him, he's still babyish but I suppose he's being doing everything very easily. Obviously when he goes to Ascot, he won't have much time for learning but he was very happy. Hopefully that will have done the job and we'll look after him between now and then. I think the Norfolk is the likely plan but that could change, it depends on what the lads want to do. Albert Einstein might run next weekend and we always thought he could be a Coventry horse and this was a Norfolk horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Charles Darwin is a lovely, big, powerful and strong horse and we always thought was an Ascot horse. He was very green at the Curragh and the race was a bit messy, and he did everything right today. He travelled and quickened very well. He's not short of speed, so it will be the Coventry or Norfolk for him at Royal Ascot - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won three times in the first half of last year, including the Norfolk Stakes, but missed the rest of the season. He'll go down the three-year-old sprinting route on the way back to Royal Ascot for the Commonwealth Cup and he could be a very good sprinter. He's just a pure sprinter; big, powerful and strong, a big block of a horse. We're very happy with him. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Mutasaabeq At The National Stud James Seymour Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Checkandchallenge has run in some hot races this year and I don't think he has actually run a bad race in any of them. Dropping back into a Listed race today it was just nice to get his head back in front. I know the distance between them was a long way at Ascot the other day, but he was fourth in a Group One and he picked up a good bit of prize money and he had some nice horses behind him. I think a mile and a quarter is right for him. We went back for the stiff mile at Ascot as we felt on that track it was going to suit him and he got his just rewards. He can cope with those extremes out there today where a lot of other horses can't. He is in the Hong Kong Mile, but I think he deserves a nice break. There will be plenty of options for him next year. Horses like him can turn up in those Group One races that cut up a bit and pick up a bit of money. We might also look at those Group Three and Group Two races in France again next year - William Knight, trainer.

I was absolutely delighted and excited with the manner in which Checkandchallenge has done it in what looked a competitive field. He had to go and win today to warrant a run in the Guineas and that's still on the agenda. It looked like there was a bit left there, which there needs to be to be competitive in the Guineas. There's improvement still to come from him, it wasn't all about today. The big challenge is he's got to convert his all-weather form across to turf, but there's no reason why he can't. He did a nice bit of work on the grass gallops last week which pleased us and made us feel he was definitely above average - William Knight, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a lovely horse who won his first two races and earned a place in the 2,000 Guineas. His second start when bolting up in Listed company at Newcastle had plenty of people talking about him and I must be honest I thought he'd win but not in the manner he did. We decided he had to take his place in the 2,000 Guineas but he never got a chance to show his true colours. He got wiped out at the start, which caused him to lose his action, and from there on things never went right. Unfortunately he came back sore, having knocked a joint. It has been hard work getting him back but he's there now and ready to go again. I looked at Royal Ascot but he had a slightly dirty scope before and you must be 100 per cent for that meeting. He heads to Newmarket for the July meeting, where we'll aim for the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes over a mile and then we'll look to the Thoroughbred Stakes at Glorious Goodwood. He'll run at Newmarket as long as they get nice ground and hopefully we can get him back to where he was before the Guineas. He'll have to carry a penalty there for his Listed win but it's a lesser race and hopefully it'll help him get his confidence back. We're all very excited about getting him out again. Further down the line we could look to step him up to 1m2f. 30-06-22

quotes.notes: Chicago Critic has been up and down in trip, from six furlongs to a mile. I think a mile on fast ground is his ideal trip. They didn't go quick and I had a nice turn of foot towards the end so it's nice to get his head in front again. His best form is over a mile and he feels good at that trip - Ben Coen, jockey.

We're absolutely delighted - that was fantastic. We came over because we thought we had a nice horse on our hands, but when you look at the strength of the race, it was a very, very good race and Chicago Critic ran his heart out. Ben gave him a great ride. We got excited up there for a couple of seconds - we thought he was coming, but he just couldn't get there. No fault of the horse, he ran brilliantly. Today was the plan, and now we know we have a horse of this level, we will think about what's next. He'll stay at seven or a mile - I think he'll get a mile no problem - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Royal Ascot Trials At Naas Handicap
quotes.notes: Chicago Critic has been gelded since his last run so maybe that and the good ground both helped. I'm delighted with that and he could be a horse to go to Ascot for the Britannia Handicap - Johnny Murtagh, trainer
Ben (Coen, jockey) said Chicago Critic is very professional, very genuine and should get a mile and a quarter next year - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

Christmas Day obviously had a lovely run the first day, but things just didn't go right for him in a good maiden at Tipperary. Once he fills his frame he'll be a big, strong, imposing three-year-old - Chris Armstrong, trainer's representative.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He made good progress last season and showed a good attitude to win the Eyrefield on his final run. He'll start off in a Derby trial. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Queen Elizabeth II Stakes (Sponsored By Qipco) (Group 1)
quotes.notes: It's amazing. I'm speechless to be honest with you. I'm chuffed for Jason [Watson] and the owners have been brilliant. It's been so dry leading up to today and we were hoping for some rain but that obviously didn't come. It's been a tough year for us all at home. Cicero's Gift is talented but he's been a challenge; he's not been the soundest - Charlie Hills, trainer.Cicero's Gift came into this so well. I worked him the other day and was very happy with him. I'm telling you now, on the way here I just felt like something was a bit different - Jason Watson, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Sporting Times Sri Lanka Fortune Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: They went hard and I'm delighted with how well Cicero's Gift saw it out. We've been very patient with him this summer and it's been frustrating having to wait all those months of the season but we've always had the QEII in our minds as it can often be heavy going there. Back in the spring he wasn't beaten far here by horses like Dancing Gemini. He's got the form, he's been as sound as a pound this season and hopefully his owners' patience can be rewarded - Charles Hills, trainer.

To go and win today is testament to the horse as Cicero's Gift wasn't fully wound up. The soft ground is important to him as he had bone bruising on all four fetlocks last year. We have a bit of money in the pot now so we may have to supplement him for something - Charles Hills, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's been off since the St James's Palace Stakes with a joint problem, but he's done well and is sound now - he's been trotting for the last few weeks and looks great. He's got a lovely mind and this time last year we were really excited about him - he's very talented. He probably won't run until June or July and we'll start in a conditions race over a mile, if one exists. 17-04-24

He was one of the talking horses going into Royal Ascot after winning his first three starts. He isn't very exuberant at home and when you watch him he does nothing flashy. He's so laid back and just does what you ask. We had him out nice and early this year and he won a Wolverhampton novice on his return. That was pretty much what we expected and he then went to Goodwood for a strong conditions race over a mile, which he won very nicely again. On the back of those wins we went for the St James's Palace on Tuesday, although he could only manage seventh on the day behind Paddington. He's a strong, athletic type like his dad, but a little bigger than him. It's an unusual route to this race but on what he's done it was the next logical step. He's clearly effective over a mile but I think he should get 1m2f later on. 21-06-23

She was in very good form on the all-weather earlier this year, winning five times between February and May. She was fifth at Windsor last week and then sixth there again on Saturday. She may go to Brighton, where she's entered in the Bullet on Friday. 07-08-24

quotes.raceTitle: Best Bet With Jenningsbet British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Classic has travelled well every day but we let him roll today. He still has signs of immaturity there but he is a very talented horse. We just didn't want to have any excuses today. It wouldn't surprise me if we see him turn up at the top level, especially on soft ground. I'd say there is a fair chance we go to the Champagne at Doncaster next - Richard Hannon, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's shown himself to be very talented since we had him gelded. He's on the upgrade, performing consistently how we thought he could, and ran a blinder in the Spring Cup at Newbury. I've always thought he was a Group horse waiting to happen and I think he could massively outrun his odds in a very nice race this season. 21-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: R & M Electrical EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: Cogitate is a beautiful looking horse, he has the size and scope and looks to have a big future ahead of him. He qualifies now for the Acomb and that could be a good step. We've won that a couple of times before with Dutch Connection and Phoenix Of Spain so that might be the route he takes.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He wants fast ground and conditions will be key to his chance. I think a stiff mile will really suit him and he already has some decent form in the book. We were looking to get another run into him before the Britannia, but 93 is a good mark and we've decided to keep our powder dry. He bumped into a good horse in Night Raider on his comeback at Southwell but still ran well and wasn't 100 per cent wound up for that. He's done a couple of nice pieces of work recently and there should be good improvement in him. He's a horse who runs well fresh and I hope he's a Group horse. 13-06-24

He's a lovely, big colt we bought last year. He has a very good attitude and does everything we ask of him at home. He'll be a lovely horse next year but before then he should be okay as a juvenile as everything he has done on the bridle makes me think he's a useful colt. 21-06-23

quotes.notes: I wanted to go sprinting with Comanche Brave for a while and I thought a few times along the way that it was stupid, but thankfully it wasn't. He'll go straight to Ascot now for the Platinum Jubilee. I'm very pleased, he's a horse that's improving and he's a young horse for a sprinter. It's our first few goes back at six furlongs with him so he's going to keep getting better. He was nearly a very good horse over a mile and I thought he could be a proper horse back sprinting. Obviously sprinters take a little bit of time to get used to that kind of pace but he seems to be getting better. We were taking Ka Ying Rising on in his own back-yard and going right-handed around a bend really isn't this horse's thing. He's better on a straight track but we were still very pleased with that performance, he wasn't disgraced by any means against useful horses in behind Ka Ying Rising and I think he's taken another step up today. You need that maturity and strength against these older sprinters and he's really starting to get that. I hope he's going to be a proper horse, I think he could be. He'll go straight to Ascot now for the Jubilee. There will be very good horses from all around the world. We want to be competing on the big stage and he'll go there with a live chance - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer.
Comanche Brave ran okay, I don't think he had any excuses, the first two pulled well clear. This is a tough place, any time you hit the board its not a bad result - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer.

We thought we'd have to make it and we were delighted that Ger's filly went on. If everything is right, she'll come back here for the Moyglare. She's so laid-back and is the very same at home -  Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: O'Driscolls Irish Whiskey Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: Composing is a lovely, straightforward filly. Wayne gave her a lovely ride. A filly who will get further, uncomplicated, he said she went to the line with her ears pricked, she has probably the makings of a lovely filly. For whatever reason Minerva is just not getting it together and Ryan said all she wanted to do was go right - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to RacingTV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She had a good season last year, winning a Group 2 over seven furlongs at the Curragh and running well in Group 1 races. We fancied her in the Moyglare [finished fourth behind Precise], but she was a little bit disappointing. We think she can come back to what we thought she was going to be. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de Royallieu (Group 1) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: We were worried about the soft ground because Consent has an extraordinarily good action, but maybe she follows [sire] Lope De Vega and that little bit of softness helped her turn the tables with the two fillies who we've run against. They will definitely keep her in training. I expect somebody might want to make her come back to a mile and a half at some stage, but a mile and six is probably her best trip, I would think. But the temptation is to come back. It would be nice to think so [asked whether she would develop into an Arc filly]. I think she's a bit more stamina-oriented, but I'm sure that's what everybody will want to aim at - Sir Mark Prescott, trainer.

horse_profiles.owner_name: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
horse_profiles.breeder_name: S A R L Lg Bloodstock

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.raceTitle: Boodles Raindance Dee Stakes (Listed Race) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Constitution River is a lovely horse who had very good form as a two-year-old. That was his first run for a long time and he won that well, I don't know what he beat but he couldn't have done it any easier. I'd say he'd have no problem going up in trip. He has plenty of options open to him - Ryan Moore, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.We're delighted with Constitution River. He was a standout in the ring, he's a gorgeous horse. Ryan [Moore] was delighted and you couldn't be happier. We've got the trials at Leopardstown, Lingfield and York. We put them all into the pot, see how they run, and then we make a plan on who goes where - Paul Smith, owners' representative.

quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Stud Wootton Bassett Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: He's a straightforward horse. Constitution River had a lovely run first time and was still very green when he won the next day. Wayne gave him a lovely ride, and he quickened well. Obviously you have to look at the National Stakes with him, and he's going to be very happy going up in trip whenever that time comes - Aidan O'Brien, trainer

He was plenty green and looking around after a few strides, so mentally, Constitution River will improve plenty for today. He's a horse who is  going to stay and is a beautiful big horse, he's going to stay improving as time goes on. A mile will suit and he could even go up to 1m2f by the end of the year- Wayne Lordan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's very good. He won his last two races last year, including the Futurity at the Curragh, but then had a mishap and missed the rest of the season. Roger [Quinlan] was very happy with him at the Curragh on Sunday. He could go the French Derby route. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Finest Surprise Stakes (Registered As The John Porter Stakes) (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Convergent has been working well with nice horses and I think he's a Group 1 horse in the making. The Coronation Cup [on June 6] would be high on the list, but whether he handles Epsom we'll find out. He's a mile-and-a-half horse with a turn of foot, and at that level they're hard to come by. If we can keep him going the right way there's a Group 1 in him for sure - Karl Burke, trainer.

Convergent has run a lovely race and is very much a work in progress. He's a horse for next season as well as this one. He's been running over shorter trips and was keen over the first couple of furlongs, then he got into a rhythm. Turning in I thought we'd win, before I thought we'd get run out of it, and then he's stayed on again. We know he stays a mile and a half well now and we're very happy for the future. I couldn't be happier without winning - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's really exciting as his homework is telling us he's improved again. He finished off the season in good form, bar his last start in Germany when it was one race too many. He wants just good ground and not fast, and he'll probably start off in the John Porter at Newbury or the Alleged at the Curragh. The Coronation Cup would definitely be a target. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: Cool Hoof Luke doesn't want to make the running but I didn't want to sit last because I thought we wouldn't go that fast. In an ideal situation he was going to be second or third with cover but I didn't achieve that. The horse did really well to save enough. He's a Gimcrack winner. The start before the Gimcrack we ran him at Goodwood because we felt he'd get seven furlongs and I made the running on him there and went too fast. I was worried about repeating the error but I got away with it. As long as the horse stays healthy, he has a very bright future. He's a beautiful model and that was quite a deep race, it was only his second run back in a year and a half, it was an excellent performance - Oisin Murphy, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (IRE Incentive Race) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: When you look at Cool Hoof Luke you think he's going to be a better 3yo don't you? We weren't sure about the trip, he's bred to be a sprinter, looks like a 7f horse and yet again the trainer got it right! We were a bit disappointed at Goodwood, but he came back and won today - Anna Lisa Balding representing Andrew Balding, trainer.

To be fair to Jamie for him riding his first stakes winner, and to be an apprentice still with a claim, he was very cool and gave Copacabana Sands a great ride. He pulled his stick through at the right time when he got out and she has hit the line strong. Everything panned out exactly how he said he wanted to ride her. It's a huge day for the filly as she has a nice pedigree and now she's broken her maiden in a Listed race. She's shown that she has ability before now and we only picked her up in February. She's done nothing but go from strength to strength, and improve. She probably prefers an ease so it's testament to the staff here and the job they did. It's also testament to Justin (O'Hanlon) who has recently come on board for race planning. This race was not on my radar and Justin put it forward so plaudits must go to him for picking this race. Justin mentioned the Ballychorus so that could be next - Michael O'Callaghan, trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.raceTitle: Commonwealth Cup Trial Stakes (Registered As The Pavilion Stakes) (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Coppull has wintered well, and by God, he's got a lot stronger. I was really impressed by the way he quickened twice, even though he idled a bit before going again. I'm very proud of him. The Sandy Lane is a very logical step, but we'll come back here. The Commonwealth Cup is a very important race for the three-year-olds and it's nice to be targeting that. It's important to have that pathway before it gets tough against the older boys in the second part of the year - Clive Cox, trainer.

We're happy as Coppull has backed up his Richmond win at Goodwood. We're over the moon to be honest and he could have been second in another few strides. That will be it for the year - Clive Cox, trainer.
When Coppull ran so well at Ascot we felt that Goodwood would suit him. I really was worried about the rain coming too soon and we've literally timed it to perfection - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Blue Point Sprint Presented By Longines (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: That's Cover Up's style of racing. We thought there'd be plenty of pace and William [Buick] rode a very sensible race. He got him cover and he picked up really nicely. This year he's a bigger, stronger horse and he's a bit more straightforward mentally and he loves Dubai. There are no more five furlong races here so we could put him away and go back to the UK - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer, speaking to Racing Dubai.Cover Up came here a better horse, more confident and more professional and he's improved since last year. This flat five [furlongs] with a strong pace seems to suit him - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Ertijaal Dubai Dash Sponsored By Emaar (Listed Race) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Cover Up made hard work of it last year [winning this], but this year he was always comfortable, he travelled sweetly, and by halfway, he had things under control. This may just set him up for a nice campaign out here - William Buick, jockey, speaking on Racing Dubai TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Ertijaal Dubai Dash Sponsored By Emaar (Listed Race) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Cover Up likes a fast pace and he got that today; he picked up all the way. I thought it was a good race; Bilhayl and Ponntos set a high standard, so he had to improve, which he did - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Join Century Racing Club Today Handicap
quotes.notes: That was a grand performance. Cover Up is in the sales next week and it's going to be a lot of fun for someone to buy a horse like that. I think they went a bit quick in the ground, he enjoyed it and came to them - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: BetUK. It's Where The UK Bets Handicap
quotes.notes: Cover Up showed plenty of gate speed, that's not easy from stall ten from the six-furlong start, but he was plenty quick and that enabled us to be well positioned. We were in the firing lane from there and waiting to pounce. I didn't really have a plan to be honest, but his speed out the gate made up my mind for me. He was quickening all the way to the line, he's a progressive horse - Kieran Shoemark, jockey.
The step up to seven furlongs suited and Cowardofthecounty feels like a nice horse with a good future - Ryan Moore, jockey.

Cowardofthecounty looked like he could be a bit special at home but you're never really sure with a two-year-old until they go to the races. He's a particularly laidback horse and couldn't have been more impressive. He's big, well over 500 kilos, which for a two-year-old at this stage is a lot. He could go straight for the Coventry now. He's such a big horse I don't know if he needs to run again, we'll see - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A Group 3 winner at Deauville last year over seven furlongs, he's going to make his reappearance in the Committed Stakes at Navan on Saturday. We're hoping he's en route to the Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot. We think six to seven furlongs is his trip and he's done very well over the winter and is training nicely. 24-04-25

quotes.notes: Crestofdistinction has built well over the winter and he's always shown a lot of ability at home. He's had two racecourse gallops at Kempton prior to this and shaped up well from each one. We put the cheekpieces on because he's such a laidback horse and he's got the potential to keep improving into a nice sprinter. He's going the right way about things and I always thought he was quite smart. He was quite green last year but it was a much different story today, he pretty much dominated as soon as he jumped out - David Probert, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was third and second on his two starts last year at Doncaster and Kempton and we decided to give him a little bit of a break. He had a setback at the start of last year, which knocked his summer out, but he's back in full training and doing well. He should be able to go and win his maiden and then go on to bigger and better things. He could really progress through the sprints and handicap division this year. 02-04-25

quotes.notes: Croupier is a lovely horse. They went quite hard up front and William sat just off it a bit. He rode a very nice race and the horse travelled into it very well. I thought they were coming after him but he kept finding more. We can head to the the Hunt Cup now, that's the plan and it could be a good race for him, the strong pace and big field should suit him. It's nice to see him bounce back because we probably shouldn't have run him on terrible ground in the Lincoln. He's come back in good style - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He came through his nursery programme with credit, will stay at least a mile and is one to look forward to in handicaps this season. I think he has enough upside on his rating to make him interesting. 25-04-22

horse_profiles.owner_name: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Cualificar got in a bit of a mess. He could have been a bit closer but he's a bit inexperienced. I guess so [he'll stay in training]. I'll talk to Sheikh Mohammed to see what we do - Andre Fabre, trainer.

That's what I was expecting. Not the circumstances of the race but, with the extra two furlongs and softer ground, it's what I was expecting. Cualificar is a big horse who became quite heavy in summer, which is why I ran him at Deauville - Andre Fabre, trainer.I was in that position from pretty much the get-go and I knew all the way through the race I'm going to have to find an out. I didn't get any room down the inside so I had to come back to come out and Cualificar still finished the race and won the way he did. It always takes a bit of doing and he's a horse who is improving. It was his first run over a mile and a half and he's happy going this distance. I think Monsieur Fabre [trainer] was happy with what he saw there and, certainly from what I felt, with the horse winning the way he did, he's probably improving at the right time of the year. I think it's an obvious step  - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix du Jockey Club (Group 1) (3yo Colts & Fillies) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Cualificar has run a blinder and I thought he had a good trip. He's really come through the grades quickly and I think he'll get further. I'm very happy with that and I think he'll improve again. He's a lovely, big horse - William Buick, rider.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Harry's Half Million By Goffs (GBB Race)

horse_profiles.breeder_name: E Dieuaide & Domaine Billard Et Fils

quotes.notes: Dallas Star will be entered in all the big races now I suppose and we'll see where we go. I'll have to chat to Kia [Joorabchian, owner] and Robson [Aguiar] and see where they want to go. He came to us over the winter and is a lovely horse - Adrian Murray, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British EBF Future Stayers' Novice Stakes (Sire And Dam Restricted Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Dallas Star is s a lovely horse and has always been a big, raw type. His first run was good at Haydock and then we pitched him in deep in the Chesham, and he ran well, but I stress he's big and raw and has taken time. Rossa says he'll be nicer again next year when he'll want further. I remember saying to someone at Haydock he could be an Ebor horse one day and I haven't changed my mind - he'll be a nice, staying type. This ground isn't essential, but he enjoys it - Dominic Ffrench Davis, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: We've always thought he's a stayer, so we're going to have a crack at the Queen Alexandra. He's never run beyond two miles but I think he should get the trip. 13-06-25

He's been running really well. He came to us with a big reputation from Robson Aguiar, who pretrains all the Amo horses, and he thought a lot of him. He has proved to be a nice horse and I remember saying after his first run that he might be an Ebor horse one day and I still think he will be. I think he'll be a lovely staying type of horse, it's just a case of keeping him on the right side of the handicapper and bringing him along nice and slowly. He's had a bit of a break but you can expect to see him out before the end of the year and we'd like to find him a race he could win rather than pitching him in too deep. 21-09-23

horse_profiles.breeder_name: Newsells Park Stud & Merry Fox Stud

quotes.notes: That was good to see. Damysus has an explosive turn of foot and put it to good use there. He'd done well over winter and has a lot of potential. We knew he'd handle the track as he won well here last autumn. He could go up to a mile and a quarter, but he's not short of speed so he could go back to a mile - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

He is a grand horse, Damysus. He went over to France at the weekend to run in the Prix Dollar but with the rain it was too soft, so all he did was have his lunch and a good dinner in France and then came back on the train! So, he missed a piece of work while he was eating and sleeping in France, but he has gone and won nicely here today. We are very pleased with him. He won at Deauville over a similar trip. We will put him away now as I can't imagine there is much left for him in our season. I think ten furlongs is right up his alley and we'll start him out next season in the Gordon Richards Stakes at Sandown. I can see the pattern of races now - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Dancing Gemini has run a cracker but that ground was rattling fast. I asked the clerk of the course on Friday if he'd put a bit of water on it Friday but he wasn't playing ball."That's quicker ground than he's ever been on, but we've only gone down a neck. We don't duck and dive and will go to Ascot next. He went down on his sword and is a Group 1 winner waiting to happen - Roger Teal, trainer.

We always thought Dancing Gemini could do what he has done today and that is why we were pitching him in all the Group races last year. Unfortunately, it was such a wet summer last year and we never got a chance. Everyone kept labelling him a soft ground horse but he's not a soft ground horse. I was delighted to see him win like that again today. I know some of the field will improve for today but Mr Fabre's horse was fit and he's no mug - he was third behind us in the French Guineas when we were runner-up. Haatem is also a serious horse. The Lockinge and the Prix d'Ispahan are the options now. We've got to get him a Group 1 and we'll do what is best for him so it's not decided yet. We'll see how the dust settles after today - Roger Teal, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Doncaster Mile Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Dancing Gemini likes this track! I'm absolutely delighted. We've always had high hopes for this horse, doing what he did there in a quality field I'm very excited. We thought we'd start at a mile. He's bred for further and he's got that blistering turn of foot - sometimes if it's not broken don't fix it. We've got some talking to do now because there's the Group Two at Sandown he could go to but he could just go straight to Newbury - and it's local! - Roger Teal, trainer.
Dancing Gemini ran well. I rode him to finish and he just emptied out. He'll be better back in trip - Dylan Browne McMonagle, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Emirates Poule d'Essai des Poulains (Group 1) (3yo Colts) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: We'll let the dust settle and then we'll have a discussion. Whether Dancing Gemini will stay a mile and a half around Epsom or maybe do you come back here over a mile and a quarter - there's lots to discuss. He's always had that kick and maybe he might have too much speed for a mile and a half, and coming here might be the wise thing. He'll have come on for today and he's had no prep - Roger Teal, trainer.

That was really impressive. We've held Dancing Gemini in high regard all year and he did a piece of work last week that was breathtaking. I knew we had him in good shape coming into today and I said to Lewis if he can back up that bit of work you'll be going pass that lollipop in front. It was a very nice performance. We won this with Tip Two Win and he could possibly be as good. He's got a similar profile, he's got speed, he's got a turn of foot and he's got a good cruising gear. He's in the Futurity here but we'll play it by ear, we'll see how he comes out of today. If all's well and the owner is happy we might take a punt on it. If not we'll leave him for next year, maybe do a trial and go on to the Guineas - Roger Teal, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Chapel Down British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: Dancing Gemini in probably one of the nicest two-year-olds already. We don't get many but we know when we've got a good horse and I've got a lot of butterflies about this horse. He's still a tad green but he went away nicely and he was very professional - Roger Teal, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He did a nice piece of work last Wednesday and it's all systems go now. He won't be doing anything too special between now and the race, just some healthy exercises. He's fit and he's ready, and we just want to keep him ticking over. He did us proud in the Lockinge when just pipped by Lead Artist so hopefully he can put in a similar performance.  10-06-25

He did well over the winter and is a lot more relaxed this year. He was working very well going into his return in the bet365 Mile at Sandown, so we were a bit disappointed with his run. He probably wasn't as fit as we thought we had him and he got a bit tired a furlong out. He had a good blow afterwards and maybe was a bit rusty. We'll see how he comes out of it as to whether we roll the dice and go back to the Lockinge, but one bad race doesn't make a bad horse. We also have the option of going back up to 1m2f this season now he relaxes better. 29-04-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: William Hill Two Year Old Trophy (Listed Race)
Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Bronte Cup Fillies' Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Danielle is tough. She was well-clear on ratings, but this was always going to be a messy race. I'd have loved to have got a lead if I could, but I didn't want it turning into a two-furlong dash. I let her go to the front and the ground was quick enough for her. At the bottom of the straight I let her go so she had time to let herself down. She toughed it out well and will come on a lot for that - Rab Havlin, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Irish EBF Gillies Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Danielle has run with credit all season and she relished the conditions. She was the one to beat today. It was a drop in class for her - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Oaks Trial Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Danielle ran fine, came down the hill well and just found the ground a little lively in the straight. She won on soft ground at Wetherby and loved it and we need to look for those conditions again - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Burrows Mazda York Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Danielle has improved from her last start, when she was run down by a filly who had been out previously [that season]. It was a good starting point, though. She had a good blow after the race, but she was always going to be a filly who improved markedly for the turf. She'll stay a mile and a half no problem, and I expect that's where the boss will be looking. Let's hope she keeps improving. We'll see how she comes out of the race. She probably had a harder race at Chelmsford last time, but went through the gears a lot better. She's improved a lot - Robert Havlin, jockey.

horse_profiles.owner_name: Robert J W Moran & Ballylinch Stud

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Gowran Classic

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: Dark Lucinda is a nice filly. She worked well the other day and I thought she'd run a good race. I was keen to come for this race because she's in the Gowran Classic in three weeks and that'll be where she goes. The connections, Ballylinch, are obviously local as well - Paddy Twomey, trainer.

Darn Hot Gallop has a great temperament and we had wanted to win a handicap and run her in a Guineas trial but she coughed a while ago. She's tough and may well get further on that evidence - James Tate, trainer.

previous_owners.ownerStyleName: H H The Aga Khan's Stud Sc
Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: Daryz is an exceptional horse, but he's not straightforward to train every day, he knows he's a boss, and Jean-Philippe [his work rider] does a great job in ensuring they respect one another. What I was looking for today was a race that would guide me as the how to build him up for his next race. He was very relaxed through the run, he was able to follow the pace easily and his jockey always had him where he wanted him. For me, the important thing was to give him a relatively straightforward race as we continue to build up to Ascot. What really blew me away was the way he accelerated in the Ganay, that was the surprise. Today was different because he had a race under his belt and we were bringing him back in trip. But honestly, I never had a worry about him handling the trip.  The Prince of Wales's will be next and I'm not in a rush to go up to a mile and a half before the Arc. It's a distance which wears on a horse who has the brutal acceleration he does and I'm relieved to say that the plan we hatched in January is going well so far - Francis Graffard, trainer.

It was the perfect comeback race. They didn't go that fast, but Daryz settled really well and he was able to deploy that acceleration of his that we know we have. I didn't feel too much pressure beforehand because on paper it was a race that he should well and truly have won and he didn't disappoint us. His objective will be the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Ascot in June, and the race that falls in between is the Prix Aga Khan IV, so we'll discuss that as an option - Francis Graffard, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Daryz was tough. When I was planning to run at York I said to Princess Zahra that we are not going to win but we need to toughen him up for the autumn and I think the defeat at York helped us to win today because my horse for the first time was very professional and mature - Francis Graffard, trainer.I was quite confident in the final straight. I saw that Minnie Hauk had made quite a significant acceleration and Daryz immediately reacted behind her in her slipstream and he showed tremendous fighting spirit - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.

We were really pleased and we'll discuss everything with Princess Zahra - it's a very open Arc. Daryz haasn't done anything today that would put you off. The good things were that he settled and handled the ground - Nemone Routh, racing manager.

Today wasn't straightforward because they went absolutely no pace and Daryz had to drop the bridle before showing proper acceleration. He's a very good horse who is up to Group 1 level and is progressing with every run, although where he goes next we'll have to wait and see. Straight after he won his Listed race we thought he was our horse for the Grand Prix de Paris, but he's done all his winning over a mile and a quarter so there seemed no need to stretch him out straight away. He's entered in the Arc and, while he's yet to encounter really soft ground, he might easily run in the race this year. He's bred to be very good; his dam and granddam were both Group 1 winners and he has five stakes-winning siblings, while he really takes after Sea The Stars. We've taken our time with him and Mickael [Barzalona] said he's taken another big step forward today - Nemone Routh, Aga Khan Studs' racing manager.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix Ridgway (Listed Race) (3yo Colts & Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: You can see Daryz is a big, imposing horse so we haven't rushed him. He's always showed us he has quality and this was a good performance. The Grand Prix de Paris has been his target and today was all about telling us if we could go or not,  and he'll head straight there - Francis Graffard, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Beverley Bullet Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I'm really pleased, Democracy Dilemma has been knocking on the door and he's a tough horse to pass once he's got his head in front.   He really wants a flatter track but it was worth the risk and it's lovely to have a stakes winner for the Hays.   He might go to Newbury for the Dubai International Airport World Trophy, he'll have a penalty in Listed races now so we have to go for Group races really. He'll have another race or two then probably go to Dubai for the winter - Robert Cowell, trainer.

What a fantastic run. Democracy Dilemma has just kept on improving and he's done nothing wrong the whole year. These are exciting times for Fitri and Jim Hay, and there are plenty of good sprints on the agenda. We know that Chester suits, and York is a good flat track. He just needs a flat, sharp track. He's just genuine and honest and he's a yard favourite - Robert Cowell, trainer.

Democracy Dilemma had some problems with the gates last time and Jake Launchbury and Craig Witheford have done a fantastic job of getting that sorted. Chester is a place where you can't miss a beat, so it's a job well done by Robert and the team. When you have that plum draw here you don't want to be giving it away. It was a big help and he's a pretty talented horse, and everything came together - Tom Marquand, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: I've always liked Democracy Dilemma but I thought he was saving a bit for himself as he's a little bit coltish and the visor helped him. He showed a good turn of foot there and I reckon he'll go to Royal Ascot over the five furlongs after that. There might be something before Ascot, but we'll probably have a day out there - David Evans, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He had a bit of an issue in the starting gates in Dubai but it was promptly solved by Shayne Ryan, the chief starter over there, who did a great job on him. He's come back since, and while he's had no problem with the stalls at all, he might just be going through a bit of a cool patch because of the travelling back and forth to Dubai and getting racing again. We ran him on ground that was a bit too soft for him up at Musselburgh in April, but I think once he gets back in the groove he'll be back winning. I think the key to him is fast ground. He was taken on for the lead and finished down the field at Windsor on Monday. He'll bounce back and be in the winner's enclosure shortly, but it's going to be on his terms rather than ours. 20-05-26

previous_owners.ownerStyleName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

horse_profiles.breeder_name: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C

quotes.notes: It took me all of last year to get to know how to ride Deressa, she enjoys a nice pace and to be coming at them. I would be happy enough with that trip but she'll get further in time. She enjoyed that ground, she's a filly that is improving away, a typical Aga Khan pedigree - Chris Hayes, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.raceTitle: Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.notes: I thought we might just get our nose in front - it was a head-bob. I'm delighted with Desert Falcon as he's run a cracker. That trip is all right for him on that type of ground and he's shown that he's versatile and can compete in these big sprint handicaps - Rowan Scott, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's won three of his last four and I wouldn't say I've been surprised by him. He's been in great form. He didn't look as if he'd stopped improving last time when he won at Haydock and he got a really nice positive ride from Ryan Sexton, who grabbed the race by the scruff of the neck and was always in control. He loves a turning 7f, but he's the sort you might put in the Ayr Gold Cup and think about the Silver Cup with him because they'll go quick - he's not a slow horse at all and you can see him coming home strongly. The only thing about him is that he wouldn't want the ground too soft. He's enjoying the dry summer when one or two others aren't. 23-07-25

He's probably a slow learner but has stepped forward a lot from the barrier trial, there is plenty in there. He'll sharpen up for the run - Declan McDonogh, jockey, speaking to Racing TV
