quotes.notes: Diamond Necklace is like her dad [St Mark's Basilica] as she has improved from two to three. She was very classy last year and she's got a lot of natural ability. She went through the race very easily and handled the ground very well. We had it in our heads she'd be a filly for either the Prix de Diane or the Oaks. We thought she could go up to a mile and a quarter [Prix de Diane trip] and could even go further, so she's very exciting - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix Marcel Boussac - Criterium des Pouliches (Group 1) (2yo Fillies) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: We thought Diamond Necklace was a bit babyish to come here but Christophe [Soumillon] rode her at Leopardstown and he said to let her come and we'd leave her alone after that for the year. We've only really seen the St Mark's Basilicas coming to hand in the last month or six weeks. St Mark's didn't win his Group race until the Dewhurst, and we all know what he did at three, so they are obviously very like him. She is up there, and Precise is very good as well. We try to give them all their chance of winning a Group 1 before coming back for a second one, so this was her chance. I'd imagine she's finished for the year now. I'd say she will probably start with a Guineas prep like we do with them all and we'll take it from there. She's not short of speed and is going to be a lovely Classic filly - Aidan O'Brien, trainer. Diamond Necklace did everything remarkably well. I knew how good she was since Leopardstown when she gave me such an amazing feeling. It's difficult to say she's the new Zarkava but for me today was something rare. For me she's a special filly - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Ballylinch Stud Irish EBF Ingabelle Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: She was a little impatient in the stalls and Diamond Necklace didn't jump out properly and after that I had to change my plans as a I was quite far back. She responded really well when I asked her to quicken, she does it so easy. It would be lovely to see her on Arc weekend- Christophe Soumillon, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.raceTitle: Grand Hotel Malahide Irish EBF Fillies Juvenile Race
quotes.notes: Diamond Necklace is a lovely filly with a great pedigree. Her dad didn't win a maiden for another three weeks so that's St Mark's Basilica for you. He went on to win the Dewhurst and how he improved from two to three was incredible - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's very like her dad and has made great progress. He didn't win until the end of his two-year-old campaign, so we were kind of surprised at what she did in winning all three races, finishing off in the Prix Marcel Boussac, and we couldn't wait to get her finished for the season. She's very strong, very natural and takes no training. Christophe [Soumillon] rode her for her last two wins and was besotted with her. Listening to the lads, she might go to France [for the French 1,000 Guineas] and Precise could go to Newmarket. After that, she could go back for a French Oaks, but we'll get her started and see. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: Diligent Harry is a grand old boy and they went a good gallop. I was able to jump and get him into a rhythm. I struggled to pull him up after the line. He seemed to have taken a step forward from last time and he's versatile as five or six furlongs is fine for him - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

If anything I was getting a little bit lonely in front from the furlong pole. Watching Diligent Harry's replays, when one comes to him he really sticks his head down. This horse has a lot of class. He was third in a Group 1 last year. I've ridden him out the last couple of weeks and Clive [Cox, trainer] was extremely positive on his chances. He said he's got a big one in him - Saffie Osborne, jockey.

We did our fight there, then the first and second came at us late in the day. I'm very proud of Diligent Harry, it was a big run. I'm very pleased and he's in a good place. I couldn't be more happier bar winning. We've got him in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot as a stiff five furlongs is more in our favour - Clive Cox, trainer.

We were worried about the drop back to the minimum [trip], but Clive thought there would be plenty of pace on which would suit Diligent Harry and he was right. There are plenty of options going forward after that - Martin Bosley, trainer's assistant.

quotes.raceTitle: BetUK All-Weather Sprint Championships Conditions Stakes
quotes.notes: It was a great ride. I'm looking forward to the summer with Diligent Harry, he's exciting. He's got a bit of confidence, gelding has helped him and he's matured - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Ladbrokes 3 Year Old All-Weather Championships Conditions Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.notes: We're a little bit away from that [Commonwealth Cup] at the moment but let's hope Diligent Harry takes a step forward. I still think he could be quite special - Adam Kirby, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Unibet New Instant Roulette Novice Stakes
quotes.notes: Diligent Harry is still a bit of a baby but he has some size about him and he should be a nice horse for the turf this summer - Clive Cox, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran well last week at Southwell when third under top weight, which was his best run of the year, and he now runs on All-Weather Championships finals day at Newcastle on Friday. He won at the meeting two years ago and I'm looking forward to running him. 17-04-25

It was great to see him back to near his best when second in the Group 3 Hackwood Stakes at Newbury. He had enjoyed a good campaign before that, having won twice at Newcastle, the latter being the All-Weather Sprint Championships. The form of that race is pretty hot as the runner-up, Witch Hunter, went on to win at Royal Ascot, while further down the field Vadream has gone on to win the Group 3 Palace House Stakes at Newmarket. He has yet to win on grass, but his head second to Commanche Falls last time, one of the most consistent horses in training, shows that there are big races to be won with him. I think the Hopeful Stakes at Newmarket is a possible logical step after that fine effort. At some point we will give him a break before preparing him for the next all-weather season. 02-08-23

quotes.notes: Distant Storm ran a good race and Will [Buick] feels that he will come forward a bit for that as well. We were a bit further behind the second Gstaad than we were in the Dewhurst, but Will was pleased and felt that he got a lovely run. Full credit to the winner - he routed them and they were going good honest fractions I felt. There is room for improvement there. The ground has been tight over the past couple of days but everyone had to go on it and I think it was a usual first run of the season, not that you would ideally come into a Guineas needing a run, which he will naturally come forward from - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

After Distant Storm was beaten in the Acomb by today's winner, we thought we'd give him one more run and put him away, and then when he won the Group 3 here last time as he did we were drawn into the Dewhurst. William [Buick] said he rode like a horse who will be better with some time over winter to develop. He felt that the immaturity was coming out in him today, but he's lost nothing in defeat as we see him as a Guineas horse next year. Whether he runs in the Craven Stakes or has a racecourse gallop before that, we'll have to see - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tattersalls Stakes (Registered As The Somerville Tattersall Stakes) (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: It's not the first time I've got one beat in the Acomb but it was my mistake. William was keen to get a pitch on Distant Storm early on and, to do that, he asked him from the gate and the only other time I've seen him be keen was when he was on the lead at home. We were adamant today to drop him in and let the race develop in front of him and in doing so we've seen his acceleration. I think we've seen a nice horse in the making. William was impressed and, with the way this season is stacking up with two-year-olds, my initial impression is to look at the Dewhurst. If it were sound ground conditions I'd be happy to take them on. He's definitely up there - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Weatherbys British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive)
quotes.notes: Distant Storm is one of the nicest breeze-up horses I've seen with an eye to the future, we always felt this is a horse for next year and we'll give him a bit of time. He's still very unfurnished. He's a nice-looking horse, but still needs to strengthen before you go up a level ? if you pitch them in too soon, you'll go quickly backwards. There will be races in the autumn we can dip our toe in and allow him to progress. If he ticks the next box we can look at the Group 1 target we have pencilled in. He could be an Acomb horse - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

previous_owners.ownerStyleName: O T I Racing, P J Bartholomew Et Al

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Doncaster Mile Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Docklands did it well. His consistency is something that is all credit to him. He just keeps rocking up every time we ask him to. We're here today with a lot of other better horses because of him, he's such a star, he's a flagbearer from our early years and he's only six so we've got at least this year from him. I don't know how we'll ever replace him but we're lucky to still have him at the moment. We'll aim at the Champions Mile in Hong Kong and then the Queen Anne Stakes - Harry Eustace, trainer.

The race was okay. From our position in the field, we needed a stronger gallop. Docklands ran on well, but he was too far back. The track was fine, the ground was fine, but the Japanese horses were too good - Harry Eustace, trainer.

I wasn't happy with the pace early on; Docklands did his usual thing, was a step slow, and I kept cursing him, if I'm honest. But he's an absolute star, he loves this racetrack and because they went slow, they probably got racing a bit further out. It's very special. When he was second here, we knew we were coming back for another go. In a curious way, he got trapped in a pocket at Epsom and didn't have a hard race, and came here spot on. I'm glad he got beat at Epsom and won at Ascot! - Harry Eustace, trainer.Everyone kept scaring me about the whip rules, I thought it was easier just to throw it away at the 200! The race was very slow and I just kept creeping as much as I could. We got the room at the right time and Docklands burst through, and he just kept responding - Mark Zahra, jockey.

It's frustrating because Docklands is just at that level where everything has to go absolutely right for him, and it just didn't quite. He just got in a pocket and he doesn't quicken - he lengthens. The winner and the German horse just kept us in a bit longer than Richard [Kingscote] would have wanted, but I can't give any real excuses as they've obviously gone a nice fair gallop and everyone's had a chance. He's a legend of a hose for us and that's another good run. He'll definitely go back to Ascot for the Queen Anne [second last year] as that's always been the plan, but this year it's a much deeper race than last year. It's nigh on the race of the week and he'll go there sort of 20-1, but he loves the track. He could run his absolute guts out and finish fourth - Harry Eustace, trainer.

It looked like we were coming with a run to be a nice third but Docklands hasn't raced for a while and I think he has got a bit tired the last 200 metres. Asking him to really quicken and work around the bend into the straight probably wouldn't have been ideal, either. We'll see how he is in the morning but the plan would very much now be to run at Flemington in two weeks' time. We'll put him in the mile and the 2,000-metre [ten-furlong] races but I think we'll keep him to this distance, although I would be very happy either way. I think it was more fitness than him not staying today - Harry Eustace, trainer.

We're very proud of Docklands. It was a big step up but he keeps answering everything we ask of him. He just loves this race track and, when there's lots of pace on, he just travels and that gives you confidence. He was second best on the day but we'll take that. All we need to do now is make him a winner this year. Australia has always been the end of year agenda and we'll work back from that. We know we're competitive at Group 1 level now and I'd say the aims in Australia have changed after that performance but we'll see - Harry Eustace, trainer.

Credit to jockey and horse. I thought it was a very cool ride. Docklands has always been pretty good and I do think he'll stay further so once he travelled that well in I thought we'd gallop really well to the line - Harry Eustace, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He enters quarantine on September 12 and heads down to Australia for the Cox Plate, which is very exciting. If we can get him there in form as good as he's been in his last few runs, we hope he can be very competitive. 11-09-24

Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: I always felt I'd hold off Daytona, but Dorset was very good - Jack Cleary, jockey.

Dorset gave me a great feel throughout the race. He jumped out of the gates good and the plan was to be forward on him. He was really enjoying himself out in front. He was very tough then the whole way to the line. He should handle a mile fine, and that ground out there was no problem to him - Jack Cleary, jockey.It's fantastic to win this race. Dorset is definitely a Group horse and you'd have to maybe give him a go at the Dewhurst now - Chris Armstrong, trainer's assistant.

quotes.raceTitle: Barronstown Stud Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.notes: Lovely, straightforward horse, Dorset came forward lovely and he'll get further. Plenty of options, he could go for the Tyros or the Superlative - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was progressive last year and won his last two races, the Goffs Million and a seven-furlong Group 3 at Leopardstown. He'll have a Derby prep and could be a French Derby horse. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: You always have a bit of anxiety when you're backing up quickly but Double Rush looked very good. In fairness Charlie Hills [previous trainer] said when he came to us that he's a very good horse and I think he's right. We'll discuss it [Royal Ascot] with the owners when the dust settles but he obviously likes Newmarket so the July Cup would be an option too and would give us more time to have a prep run - Andrew Balding, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

Oisin came back and said Double Rush was a push button ride. Charlie Hills obviously did a good job with him. We'll treat him like a good horse and maybe look at Royal Ascot  - Anna Lisa Balding, trainer's wife.

I think Double Rush is going to be a nice, improving horse through the season. Some of our horses just weren't right last season and he had a nice mark. He probably didn't handle the track today and a flatter track would suit him better. There is a nice valuable handicap at York around a week before Royal Ascot which we could aim at. We will see how he improves and take it step by step. We couldn't put a hand on but the horses just weren't last right season. They looked great but just weren't letting themselves go. They seem nice and healthy this year - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Aesop's Fables At Compas Stallions Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: We're delighted with Drop Dead Gorgeous, she's a lovely big filly. She's still a baby and learned plenty today. She was very green when she got there but we're very happy. She'll stay further. She probably will [step into an Oaks trial], something like that I'd imagine. She's a quality, big mare. We'll see what comes up for her and how she comes out of it. It was just nice to get her started -  Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's a lovely, big filly and it was nice to get her started this month at Naas, where she won a mile maiden.  She has an entry in the Park Express on Friday but it could come a bit soon. She's going to be an absolutely beautiful filly next year, she's big and strong, and she's a baby still. She'll work on Tuesday and that'll tell us if she could run on Friday. It's possible as she did take her race very well. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai Gold Cup Sponsored By Al Tayer Motors (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: That was great. Dubai Future is a very talented horse. My concern was the trip. He's a strong traveller but he relaxed today, he switched off. They didn't go a strong pace early on but he relaxed for me. When I let him down I let him organise himself before I really went for him and he responded to pressure. It was a great performance by Saeed - Silvestre de Sousa, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Nad Al Sheba Trophy Presented By DP World (Group 3) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Dubai Future had a little bit of a setback last year which is why he didn't run. I didn't want to lead with him today as it was his first time back after a break, so I told him [de Sousa] to go in behind. He'll now go straight to the Dubai Gold Cup - Saeed bin Suroor, trainer.

We've tried to win this race in the last few years with no luck, but this year we had two runners and had first and second. Dubai Future has improved a lot this year and he won at Royal Ascot. Physically and mentally, he was better than last year and we thought he was the right horse again for this race - Saeed bin Suroor, trainer.

Dubai Future did well. Danny's given him a very good ride. He's a jockey I like a lot, he gives the horse a chance and we've had some good luck with him. I said to keep a hold of him and keep him relaxed in the race, which he did. He tried and he finished the race well, and he'll go for the Princess of Wales's Stakes at Newmarket next. I love it here, I love being in the winner's enclosure - but it's so hard to get winners here. It means a lot for the family to get winners and to do so with Fazza and Hissa here too - Saeed Bin Suroor, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai Racing Club Classic Presented By The View at the Palm (Listed Rated Conditions) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Everything went pretty smoothly although Dubai Future was a bit keen early on. I had a lovely spin around and when the gap opened he shot through it and we probably ended up in front a bit sooner than ideal. That said he galloped all the way to the line and I would like to think he can build on this up in class - Pat Cosgrave, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Matchbook Best Value Exchange Novice Stakes
quotes.notes: Dubai Future has done that really, really well, couldn't have been any easier. I would have liked to have waited a little longer turning for home but as soon as the gap came he was very willing and he just took me straight through it. He's a proper horse. I'm not sure about the plan now. I suppose there's a chance he could go to Dubai, he's proven himself quite capable now but that's not my decision to make - Callum Shepherd, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He provided our first carnival winner this season in the Listed Dubai Racing Club Classic last week - a race he finished second in last year - and thrives here in the winter. After the impressive manner in which he won last week, there are possible races for him over 1m6f in the Listed Al Khail Trophy on Friday or the Group 3 Nad Al Sheba Trophy on February 17, before going back to 1m4f for the Group 2 Dubai City of Gold on Super Saturday. 26-01-22

quotes.raceTitle: Darley EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.notes: I was delighted with Earth Shot. I was a bit concerned about the ground but she strode out well. The owners sponsor the mile and a quarter fillies' Listed at Newbury on the 17th of May and I suspect she'll go there. Tom [Marquand] was keen that she has another race relatively soon before we put a big target in front of her so we'll do Newbury if she's OK then decide whether to go to Epsom [Oaks] or Ascot [Ribblesdale] - William Haggas, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.It was an impressive performance. Earth Shot had that really nice introduction at Newbury behind one of our other exciting fillies [My Ophelia] and that performance was everything you'd want it to be. She took a while to work it out with the track being the track. She took a bit of a hop and a jump over some of the ridges early on but she worked it out late and, as ever with ours, William [Haggas] likes to leave a bit to be improved on into the season and I'm looking forward now to seeing what she really can do - Tom Marquand, jockey.

horse_profiles.breeder_name: Manor Farm Stud & J E Rose

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Racing Writers Association Ron McKnight Memorial Madrid Handicap
quotes.notes: The only time East Hampton encountered ground that resembled soft, he won on it. We brought him to Dundalk the last day but he didn't like the surface so we put him away for this. Obviously six furlongs was as far as he'd gone so the trip was a worry but I was delighted to see the low draw. Luke gave him a fabulous ride, dropped him in and switched him off as much as he could. He will learn from it, he was fresh today. He saw it out well, though and didn't stop galloping. As long as the ground has an ease, we'll keep going - David Marnane, trainer.
It's great to be back and it's our first runner on grass [this year]. I didn't know how fit they all were but Ebt's Guard has been working extremely well. - William Muir, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Vickers.Bet Restricted Maiden Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Ebt's Guard has been slightly unlucky in his runs. First time out he got beat half a length and then last time we had to go the long way round - William Muir, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Give Thanks Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: She is a progressive filly, and I'd say Elana Osario has got stronger with time. She never ran as a two-year-old and only made her debut this night last year and has never stopped improving. I'd say Robert (Moran) will leave her in training at five so hopefully she keeps improving. She had to battle and she was a filly coming out of handicaps taking on a filly that was third in an Oaks, so it was a big ask and I'm delighted that she was up to it - Paddy Twomey, trainer

Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: Elmonjed loves the track. The draw helped today. He's a really tough, genuine horse and loves it here for some reason, which is great. He's gone from handicapping to Listed company, and we kept him in training to run in this race, as we said why don't we have a shot at a Group 2. It's fantastic. He's in the Wokingham, but I don't suppose he'd be running in that. I didn't put him in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes, so I'd think we'd have a go at the Prix Maurice de Gheest. It's clear a fast, flat track is what he likes. He'd have to go for a Group 1 now because he has a Group 2 penalty. We may put him in the July Cup. The Nunthorpe is too sharp for him, so we'll fiddle our way around. The Al Quoz Sprint could be a target next year - William Haggas, trainer. It's the first time I've ridden Elmonjed but he's a lovely horse who went about his business and was very professional. He loves this track, today set up nicely for him and the recent rain probably helped - William Buick, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

Jim [Crowley, jockey] said 'run him on Saturday, I would!' We'll see. It's a different sort of track but Elmonjed likes a big field and being covered up and helped through. He's not really happy being on his own in front as long as he was today but he hung on. He'd be better on faster ground too - Maureen Haggas, trainer's wife

The horse is tough since he's had the headgear put on him. Elmonjed was idling without it and needed it to make him concentrate. He hits flat spots in his races and it wouldn't amaze me if he got further one day. It's very much one step at a time with him, but he could be good enough for a bigger prize in time - Angus Gold, racing manager to Shadwell Estates.

quotes.raceTitle: AC Plastics Limited EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: It looked like the runner-up had got away from him a bit so Elmonjed did well to win under a penalty and I really liked how he put his head down in the final furlong. He surprised us a little at Lingfield and has really improved from his debut. He was gelded in the summer because he was misbehaving but he's a good-looking horse and progressing with time. He's entered at Chantilly next Saturday and that's a pretty quick turnaround, but we'll talk with Sheikha Hissa and William [Haggas] and make a plan. He's going in the right direction and is a really nice horse - Richard Hills, assistant racing manager for owners Shadwell.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Shadwell have another nice horse on their hands. Elmonjed has done well to overcome that greeness early on what is a sharp track - Tom Marquand, jockey speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.notes: Endorsement is a horse to go into all those nice staying races, but he's a horse to look forward to for next year and it is nice to get his maiden out of the way. He is still a bit babyish and he'll come on a lot mentally and physically from this run. He could go to the Zetland at Newmarket and then on to the Group 1 races in France, but he's a horse who'll be a lovely middle-distance horse next year - Chris Armstrong, Aidan O'Brien's stable representative.

horse_profiles.owner_name: T & Mrs L Standish & Mrs A Spence

quotes.notes: Enfjaar had bone bruising among some other things last year, but Jack rode him in work last week and he looked good. This was a tough race, though, but we won it two years ago with a horse who went and won a Group 1. I'm not saying this fella will, but I hope he will! We'll reassess and see where they put him, but he'll probably be out of handicaps and into Group races now. There's lots of lovely races in Britain and abroad. He's exciting - Richard Hills, owners' representative.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: We trained him for the Wolferton last season and he was unlucky not to win. He looks as good as ever and he's likely to start back in the Listed Festival Stakes at Goodwood in May. How he goes there will dictate his early-season programme. If he wasn't to win, he could go back to the Wolferton, but if he won at Goodwood we might be more ambitious. He hasn't been over-raced and is a lovely older horse to have around. 01-04-26

quotes.notes: We got very excited after English Oak's Buckingham Palace win as we thought he could be a potential Group horse but things haven't quite gone his way. He seems to have relished being out here [in Dubai] in the sun and his last piece of work was nice. We had planned to be further forward from that draw but he didn't jump that well so we just rode him to travel well and to come home and it seemed to suit him - James Doyle, jockey, speaking to Racing Dubai.

English Oak is clearly a classy sort, he travelled superbly through the race. We had a massive advantage on the stands' side, even after going a furlong or so we were a long way ahead of the others. He's very speedy. He's got a high cruising speed, he does feel pretty fast. When I let him go there he quickened up pretty smartly. It will be interesting to see what the guys want to do - James Doyle, rider.
He's a slow-maturing horse who was like a rabbit in the headlights first time. English Oak has seen the trip out really well and is definitely one to keep on the right side - P J McDonald, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's been disappointing since winning at the meeting 12 months ago. He needs to spark back into life, but he's started to come back down to the mark he won off last year [1lb higher now], so it's not impossible. He looks well and we gave him a bit of time after his last race. 10-06-25

He was a bit disappointing after putting up such a good performance when winning the Buckingham Palace at Royal Ascot, so we hope we can get him back on track this year. He's been gelded and I hope that will help him. He's a bit behind and is taking a long time to come in his coat, so we're not in a rush with him. He'll probably start back in a conditions or Listed race. I think he's best at that specialist trip of 7f but we'll see how we go. 16-04-25

horse_profiles.breeder_name: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C

quotes.notes: Erzindjan needs to be held on to but loves passing horses and has some great form. He had two very good runs last year - one in the Cambridgeshire and one in the John Smith's. I love York so like to go there if I can. His form was outstanding, not just for me but also for the trainer he was with in Dubai as well. If he ran up to that that level today, then we thought we had a live chance. It's nice to have a winner today and hopefully we are going in the right direction. I'll speak to his owner Mohammed Al Suboosi and see where we go from here - Terry Kent, trainer.

Erzindjan ran better at the Curragh than his finishing position suggested. He was very good at Cork last year. The step up to a mile today suited him well and we'll go back up to stakes level with him next time. Maybe a race like the Amethyst at Leopardstown would suit - Kris Weld, assistant trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Stud Gleneagles Irish EBF Maiden (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.notes: Erzindjan handled that ground well and his run the first day put him right - Oisin Orr, rider

quotes.notes: Estrange has run a really good race. I'm very proud of her. She's a lot of class, how she can move up so easily in a race is a great asset.   I'm delighted with my filly on ground that I think isn't her optimum. We rolled the dice on ground I had said we would not run on. We made a collective decision and we've run on it and run well. The only two older fillies that have won this in recent years both won Arcs, Enable and Alpinista so she's not done too badly today - David O'Meara, trainer.

Danny [Tudhope, jockey] said Estrange normally falls asleep in a race but today she was trying to chase a little bit and didn't quite drop the bit. She ended up being in front for a long time, which isn't really how we'd like to play her. It was a means to an end. She's four from five now and has won a Group 2, so it's brilliant. The drop of rain helped, although I don't think she's absolutely reliant on heavy ground but we wouldn't really want to be running on quick ground. The Yorkshire Oaks would be the next target, it fits in well timewise - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred Nifty 50 Lester Piggott Fillies' Stakes (Group 3) (Formerly Known As The Pinnacle Stakes)
quotes.notes: Danny said Estrange has a great temperament and is a dream to ride. You can put her anywhere and when you want her you just give a small squeeze and she comes to life under you. For me and for the yard it's brilliant to have a filly like this.  We'll stay away from quick conditions but the Pretty Polly in Ireland could be considered, there's the Lancashire Oaks back here and the Yorkshire Oaks. Dare I say, if she was good enough it would be great to be considering Longchamp. She hasn't won a Group 1 yet but she potentially is the best we've had, she looks very good - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet Irish EBF Gillies Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Estrange has always had a lot of ability and it didn't really work out at Yarmouth last time as she got behind a wall of horses and it was a little bit quick. We'd been waiting for this race on easier ground over an ideal trip. She's still learning and will be a better filly next year. Hopefully it's Group races next year. She'll get a good winter under her belt and come back next spring. She's only going to get better, that's for sure - Matthew Sigsworth, owners' representative.

quotes.raceTitle: Darley EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: We were expecting Estrange to run well as her work had been very good, but you couldn't expect her to win in that manner - visually it was so impressive. She had no experience going into it so she's bound to improve. We'll speak to connections, but a lack of experience will be a thing and we'll be mindful of that before chucking her in too deep - David O'Meara, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: We're very much looking forward to her. She was very impressive at Goodwood and we probably shouldn't have run her at Yarmouth on quick ground, when she also had a rough passage, so it was good she corrected that at Doncaster. She's entered for the Middleton at York or there's the Pinnacle at Haydock and it depends on conditions as she wants ease in the ground. There's the Lancashire Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks later on and we're hoping she can go right to the very top. 14-04-25

British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Hilary Needler Trophy EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)

quotes.notes: Evolutionist has run a fantastic race. She is all heart and Shane [Foley] said the ground was quicker than she wanted it. He was going a nice gallop but couldn't have gone any quicker on that ground. He just let her get into a nice rhythm and she finished off well. A furlong and a half out, I thought we were going to do it. She will stay further and I'd say we'll go to Prix de Diane now off of the back of that. The Irish Guineas would come too soon and she's had a hard race there. She is a very good filly, very progressive and hopefully a step up in trip will find some more improvement. I think a mile and a quarter is going to be spot on for her - Karl Burke, trainer.

We knew Evolutionist was a very good filly and she'd been working very well, but I was worried that some of our nice horses had been running below par in the last week. We had a few I thought would win, but they ran badly. Thankfully she's done it nicely there. The whole race set up very well because she stays very well; she'll stay a mile and a quarter. We have an interesting conversation as to whether she'll come back here or go to Newmarket. I'd say she'll definitely end up back here [in France] for the Prix de Diane. As for which Guineas she goes for, we'll see how she comes out of this and go from there. Shane [Foley] said she outstayed them but also has a turn of foot. Her last piece of work was very good, so we're very happy with her, but I'm sure she'll come on for the run - Karl Burke, trainer.
Evolutionist missed the break a bit which may have cost us second in the end but she wouldn't have won. She's a nice prospect for next year - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A very nice filly who did very little wrong last year and has strong form, including finishing third behind Precise in the Fillies' Mile. She goes to France for a trial and is in the three Guineas. 31-03-26

He put in a really good debut performance a fortnight ago when second at Wolverhampton. He was green as grass and got beat by what looks a high-quality horse of Sir Mark Prescott's [Warrior Mode]. He's well bred and should be winning his maiden before going into the handicap division. 02-04-25

quotes.notes: Expanded has run a great race considering we only ran him at the Curragh seven days ago but Ryan said that if James Doyle hadn't attacked him early on Ancient Truth he would have won. He was here for experience more than anything, to run against The Lion In Winter originally, but we've always liked him and he went to the Curragh on the back of five pieces of work. As we know he handles the track, he could be back here next year - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.notes: Expanded is a lovely horse with loads of class but still very raw. When he puts everything together he is going to be a smashing colt - Chris Armstrong, assistant trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was a neck second in the Dewhurst as a two-year-old in 2024, which was a massive run on his second start, but then he just didn't have a clean run at things last year. He'll have a run before the Lockinge Stakes and we'll see what happens. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Queen Elizabeth II Stakes (Sponsored By Qipco) (Group 1) (British Champions Mile)
quotes.notes: When he challenged Charyn they went head to head but Charyn is the best miler and it's like a victory to finish second again. It's hard to win a Group 1 here in Britain but one day we will. Facteur Cheval got a little squeezed in but it wouldn't have changed anything, we were beaten by a better horse. We'll run in the Golden Eagle in Australia on November 2 - Jerome Reynier, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

The pace in the first 800 metres was too intense and then Big Rock gave way quite early and Facteur Cheval got left on his own to make the best of his way home, which was not easy. Watching the race back, even if Maxime had gone across to join the others he would have been on the wing without cover. The ground in Dubai was fast but with a better covering of grass, and here it was too firm for him with less of a cushion. He also lost his off-fore shoe - Maxime wasn't sure where - so he got unbalanced and was never comfortable. It's a race to forget - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai Turf Sponsored by DP World (Group 1) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Facteur Cheval is a great champion. We didn't know how he would handle the faster ground because he's more used to racing on soft and heavy surfaces, but you can see how well he did. He gave me a really great turn of foot and really wanted to fight to the line. I didn't want to go too early because he's been running over 1600 metres and was stepping up in trip slightly, for all that I think he'll stay 2000 metres - Maxime Guyon, jockey.

It's like a victory today, we really thought he was going to beat Paddington but he had the stand rail, and we were in the middle of the track. Facteur Cheval was stuck in the middle of the traffic, but he's run a great race. He was third in a Group 1 the other day, second today in a very nice Group 1 and I hope that next time we will be able to win at that level. He keeps improving mentally and physically, so probably the best is yet to come. Fingers crossed he will be coming back in good shape and we can aim for the Queen Elizabeth at the end of the year with him. There are two options beforehand - the Moulin de Longchamp or the Woodbine Mile in Canada. Maybe, we will wait until he is a five-year-old for an international campaign - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I feel he's ready to stretch out in trip and that he can sustain his effort for longer. A mile on quick ground, like he encountered in the Queen Anne last year, doesn't play to his strengths in the same way that running over the same course and distance at the end of the year in the QEII does. I was second in this race last year with Zarakem and I feel it could suit Facteur Cheval. He spent the whole of April recovering from his trip abroad at the start of the year and we enjoyed a good May getting him in shape. He did his last good piece of work last Saturday and I'm very happy with him. 11-06-25

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai Gold Cup Sponsored By Al Tayer Motors (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: We ran Fairy Glen in the Balanchine over a mile and one [furlong], which was a bit short for her but she's blossomed since. She had never run two miles before so we were a bit sceptical but she goes on this sort of ground and I though Mickael [Barzalona] rode a sensible race - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer.Fairy Glen was happy throughout the race and when I asked her to pick up she did it nicely - Mickael Barzalona, jockey

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)

quotes.raceTitle: Denny Cordell Lavarack & Lanwades Stud Fillies Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: We said Faiyum would grow a leg on this ground, that's why we've been so patient with her. She's twice the filly now than she was earlier on in the year and when second to Barnavara. I'm not in any rush with her and I'm not sure there's anything for her over ten furlongs. We'll talk to Barry [Mahon, Juddmonte racing manager] about whether we'll wait and have a proper campaign on soft ground next year - Ger Lyons, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Aesop's Fables At Compas Stallions Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: We knew Faiyum was nice but she's green as grass so there should be buckets of improvement in her. Her sister handled that ground so we didn't think it'd be a problem. The Park Express closed the other day and I put her in because I said it'd look silly if we didn't as we like her. No more than you'd expect for a Juddmonte filly so fingers crossed she can continue to progress - Ger Lyons, trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)

quotes.notes: The ground was so quick at [Royal] Ascot and you could see Fallen Angel's head came up coming round the bend. As long as there is no jar in the ground, she is fine but when there is jar in the ground, she just doesn't let herself down. I was more than hopeful she would come back but I would be lying if I said I thought she would win three Group Ones on the bounce. She got very idle at home and was only going through the motions. We needed to sharpen her up and she worked very well in them [cheekpieces] the first time we used them, so it was a no-brainer not to put them on her at Ascot and then after that we knew it was the ground as to why she didn't perform at Ascot. She is tough, and I think running her over a mile you can afford to be aggressive with her. She stays further but her run style is that she doesn't like being pulled around and she shows that in her work at home - if you try sitting in behind horses and asking her to quicken, she doesn't do a lot. She loves being competitive. This time last week Richard Brown [owners' racing manager] called me and said we can't run her on the good to firm ground. Of the course the weather changed and that nice Storm Amy came across to save the day for us! Ascot [Queen Elizabeth II Stakes on QIPCO British Champions Day] is the plan. We spoke beforehand with Richard and said if she performed well today - even if she hadn't won - we would give her a shot at the boys so I can't wait for two weeks' time. I can't imagine Ascot will dry out as quick as a place like Newmarket. It's very tacky and soft there today so I'll say it will be good ground at fastest. The plan is for her to stay in training next year as long as she finishes the season sound. I think Fallen Angel is a mile and a quarter horse really. I am sure she will stay, and we will discuss it next year. We could maybe go for something like the Prix Jean Romanet at Deauville where they might leave us alone in front - that will be interesting - Karl Burke, trainer. Fallen Angel is a strong galloper at a mile. There's a bit of a tailwind today and the ground drying all the time was a slight concern but it's not quick. She just galloped them into the ground -  James Doyle, jockey.

She's so tough, very honest and James (Doyle) gave Fallen Angel a great ride. She could stay 1m2f but she's probably best ridden aggressively over a mile. The cheekpieces have sharpened her up. She'll go for the Sun Chariot if she's okay and then we could take on the boys at Champions Day at Ascot - Karl Burke, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.raceTitle: Prix Rothschild - Fonds Europeen de l'Elevage (Group 1) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Straight Course) (Tu
quotes.notes: I'm absolutely delighted to have a Group 1 winner for Wathnan, they've been huge supporters and long may it continue. I'm delighted for Danny [Tudhope] as well. I was a little surprised James [Doyle] went the way he did [riding fellow Wathnan runner Crimson Advocate]. I know Crimson Advocate beat us at Ascot but we needed that bit better ground and the cheekpieces made a bit of difference. Also, Fallen Angel's work has taken a step forward since Ascot and especially over the last two weeks. I wouldn't say we were confident but we were bullish going there. She doesn't want any firmness in it like she had at Ascot where, coming round the bend, her head just came up a bit. She's such an honest, game mare and she was battling back in the last 100 yards then, as she did today. She only does what you ask her to do and Aidan's filly coming to her helped her. What I'm really pleased about is that she's emulated Laurens in winning a Group 1 at two, three and four now. The Matron I would imagine is the next port of call and hopefully we'll have some nice ground at that time of year. There is the mile and a quarter Prix Jean Romanet but we'll enjoy today, get her home and see how she is, and then I'll speak to connections, but the way she's won that I'd be happy to stick at a mile - Karl Burke, trainer. Fallen Angel is a superstar. I haven't ridden her since last year when we won the Irish 1,000 Guineas. She means a lot to me and the team as well, that's three Group 1s now as a two-year-old, three-year-old and now as a four-year-old. It's amazing and I have to thank the Wathnan team for giving me the chance to get back on her. She has a good mind on her, a great mentality. Karl [Burke, trainer] always says she never shows a lot at home but she obviously saves it for the track and it's a great day for us all. We went quick. My plan was always to go forwards because she's a straightforward filly. She'd the cheekpieces on today and was a bit lit up in them but she wore them the last day. I thought she was doing a bit too much in my hands but I've always thought she's a filly you couldn't go quick enough on and she's toughed it out. She had to be tough, they were coming at her and it got close at the line, we got headed at one point but she came back. She's a tough filly. She dug deep and got the result and we know the softer the better for her, but she tries so hard every time. She's a superstar - Danny Tudhope, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

Absolutely delighted with Fallen Angel. The ground was probably a little bit quicker than ideal, but I was so pleased with what she did in the last 50 yards - she battled on, and she's just a superstar. I think in the autumn when we get a bit of ease in the ground, she'll be back into a big one for us. We might go up in trip - it will be somewhere between a mile and a mile and a quarter, but ease in the ground is going to be important - Richard Brown, owners' representative.

We were disappointed with the Guineas. We sent Fallen Angel to Newmarket fit and she didn't blow that much afterwards. The ground maybe was a bit quick on the undulations, but that's looking for excuses, we were beaten fair and square on the day. She just sparked up in the last week, and physically she looked fantastic today - Karl Burke, trainer.

Fallen Angel jumped great and is a very straightforward ride. You can put her where you want in a race, she stays very well and I thought the last furlong would be her best furlong - Danny Tudhope, rider.

We were very confident coming here today. Fallen Angel is so laidback and travelled so well in the race. She hit the line strong and will go another furlong no problem. We've always liked her at home and she's quite versatile as regards ground - Daniel Tudhope, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's in great form and looks fantastic. She won't run on ground any quicker than proper good ground. We'll keep an eye on the Dahlia Stakes on Guineas weekend, but she'll definitely go to the Prix d'Ispahan on May 21. She'll have entries at Royal Ascot but we won't run her unless the ground is right. After that there's the Group 1 fillies-only mile race for her. This is likely to be her last season and we're hoping for a swansong at the Breeders' Cup. 31-03-26

He won his only race on turf at Keeneland by almost seven lengths and we're going to target either the Coventry Stakes or the Windsor Castle. I haven't had much luck in the Coventry. It's a race everyone and their brother seems to want to win and it's produced many good horses over the years. He's a big colt and, physically, you'd think he'd be able to run the three-quarters of a mile in the Coventry, but it will be determined when we get a little closer and we see how both races are shaping up. He's by Showcasing out of a Pivotal mare and definitely has an affinity with the turf. We put him and American Rascal together in a workout and I'd have to say American Rascal was better, but Fandom is very straightforward, came out blazing at Keeneland and has trained very well since. 12-06-23

quotes.notes: Field Of Gold needed the race but he's run a nice race and the Lockinge will remain the plan. He's only had one race in nine months, so he needed the race to bring him forward and you'll never beat a front-runner around here spotting them a lead like that - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Queen Elizabeth II Stakes (Sponsored By Qipco) (Group 1)
quotes.notes: Field Of Gold has run a very good race. He came into it well but the lack of a recent race just caught him out in the final furlong. He's had a long time off and was having a good blow afterwards. He's worked well at home but it's nothing like coming here with a prep race. I didn't like the high draw. It wasn't ideal and he was always on the wing, rather than in amongst it where the pace was on the other side, but it's a lack of a recent race that has caught him out, a lack of match practice. He's a huge striding horse and I don't think he'd necessarily want to tackle two bends at Del Mar [in the Breeders' Cup Mile] - John Gosden, joint-trainer.Field Of Gold relaxed and travelled through the race well. Coming down to the two it felt like he was picking up to be competitive, but a lack of a run cost us. He's run a massive race after being off for so long - Colin Keane, jockey.

We got left back a long way, that's life, and the pacemaker goes and wins it. If you let them have those fractions they'll do it. Field Of Gold ran on but didn't seem well balanced on the track. It's a different kind of track than he's run on and he just got a little imbalanced coming out of the dip into the bend but I'm not making any excuses. He ran a huge race in the Guineas and was flying at the finish. He was not flying at the finish here so it was very different. We'll have to see why [he wasn't at his best]. He's having a normal blow and we'll have a good look. He didn't seem comfortable and William said as soon as he asked him, the engine wasn't there, simple as that. And if not, he'd have run on and probably been with Rosallion in second or right up there but he didn't fire today - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

That was a great performance. Field Of Gold had always impressed as a two-year-old, but he was a big boy and slightly outgrew himself. It was never the plan to go to Ireland, it became the plan, so he's had a trial, two Guineas and this. It's a lot of racing and we're not even beginning to be half-way through the season. Maybe freshen and go to the Sussex, something like that, we'll see. I think if he hadn't have run in Ireland, I would have probably been keen to go to the Eclipse - John Gosden, joint-trainer.I thought we'd be behind Will [Buick] and Ryan [Moore] would be behind us, whereabouts I wasn't sure exactly but it worked out to some degree and he showed how good he is on the day. I had a lot of confidence in Field Of Gold but I needed them to have brought him a little bit further because he'll only do so much when he gets there. I didn't want to land there and be a sitting duck for something to come at me so If I asked him I thought they'd do well to catch him - Colin Keane, jockey.

I was sorry to get beaten in the 2,000 Guineas when Field Of Gold finished so well, but to come on a plane and see something different, he'll have learned a lot, and they grow in mentality and in stature. Colin [Keane] rode him beautifully. In truth, I was concerned he might over-race with no cover on the outside, but I told Colin if he relaxes on the way down [to the start], he should relax on the way back. When he quickened he went, and it took two or three strides and he was off. Let's hope the owners want to go to Ascot and have a look at the St James's Palace Stakes - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

The race wasn't probably run in the fractions of the Craven Stakes and we were sat some way back. The winner has kicked and gone and we ran out of racetrack. Given another 25 yards the race would have been ours.    You'll probably find Field Of Gold has run a better race than he did in the trial but a trial is a trial. When this track gets fast like this it can ride slick with a crosstail wind and they can get away from you. It just got away from us, I'm afraid, as we came into the Dip from where he was clawing the ground back. I could see it was lost going into the Dip as we were just too far back and the winner got first run. We'll talk with the family about where we go next but I think you're looking at a St James's Palace Stakes after that - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

This is a trial, it's not the Guineas. You're not fully wound up for this, the race now puts them where you want them - that's the idea of the trial. He went to his girth and had a good blow, but then he's entitled to. Field Of Gold did it in splendid style and it's nice to race on some really good ground today and he just flew off it. It would be nice to win, but it's not something you necessarily worry about - I don't think about it at all. I suppose Kingman was slightly unfortunate as he went four lengths clear and thought he'd done enough and got caught late on by a very good horse in Night Of Thunder, who has become a top stallion. It's lovely to have a horse going for the Guineas and it's great for Juddmonte, because they have both the winner of the Greenham and this, so they're double-handed if they want to. But the family will decide whether one goes there and one goes to France or what we do - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (New Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Fields Of Gold ran a solid race. He was right up there and travelled well but got a little bit caught out by the ground. He's a big, strapping horse and very much a next-year horse - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Field Of Gold is very exciting. He's always shown great potential at home and it's nice to see him finally deliver it on the track. He's a horse who will stay a mile but he has acceleration and a very good turn of foot. He's a big horse - 16 hands - and is going to be better as he strengthens and will hopefully make a better three-year-old. The Lagardère looks the obvious plan at this stage - Barry Mahon, Juddmonte racing manager.

quotes.raceTitle: Weatherbys British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Field Of Gold has taken a big step forward, albeit he probably ran in a nice race at Doncaster. He was slowly away that day but he was quick today and I was just trying to get a lead for as long as I could. We hit the front a long way out but he knew his job today and he's got a huge stride and plenty of scope. He really galloped out and he's no doubt going to stay a mile - Kieran Shoemark, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: This colt is so genuine and has given everyone a lot of fun with five wins from nine starts, which reads even better on the all-weather having a five from seven record. He does not go well on the grass so we will continue to race him on the artificial surface. He has risen through the ranks where he now finds himself with a rating of 93. There is a race at Wolverhampton on May 18 while there is a 1m2f option at Lingfield in mid-June. I would love to try him over 1m2f soon as I feel the extra trip could bring out improvement in him and add to his already commendable winning record. 28-04-21

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Jenningsbet Northumberland Plate Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (Gbbplus Race)

quotes.raceTitle: McGuinness Maintenance Services Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.notes: We got Fingerpaint from Juddmonte a couple of months ago. Ideally, we would have preferred more juice in the ground but you have to get them out at some stage and to be fair to the team here they have produced lovely safe ground. The boss wanted me to take my time on her, I would have sat closer but she was feeling the ground a bit. I thought she was a stakes filly when I rode her at Juddmonte, before she came to us - Chris Hayes, jockey

quotes.raceTitle: Lord North Handicap Sponsored By DP World (Handicap) (Turf)
quotes.notes: First Conquest broke OK but wasn't fast enough to get up with the pace, so we took our time and the rhythm was OK. He was very good once he got a clear run. He's still an immature horse, but he did everything well today - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.
First Conquest may be a horse that we take out for the Dubai Carnival. We'll have to see if we give him another run beforehand - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: bet365 Wood Ditton Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: First Conquest knew his job and it could be that he's a mile and a quarter horse going forward. He looks a handicap prospect and we used to have to pitch them into the deep end after this but changes to the programme book means we have other options - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: First Instinct has had a couple of starts this year where she's probably not been the quickest out and I was conscious that she'd have to be here. I gave her a kick out of the gate and within three strides she was rocking, and she actually took me by surprise. She's tough, she's fast, and she appreciated that tiny bit of give in the ground - Tom Marquand, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Goffs Irish EBF Polonia Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: Mr Haggas was bullish with First Instinct and thought she had a good chance. She jumped so fast coming out of the gates that I nearly came off, but she got into her stride really quick. Billie (Lee, on Town And Country) was coming quick, but I was pulling out more. I'd be happy at today's distance - Chris Hayes, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: First Instinct has been faultless. I was a bit worried that the ground today might just blunt her speed but she fell asleep early - which was key I think - and showed that trademark turn of foot which she showed on her first run. I think she'll be even more effective on better ground - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Sumbe Prix du Calvados (Group 2) (2yo Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Fitzella's run a massive race and it's always the 'what if' question when you're second. If Andre had decided against it this morning she would have won a Group 2 in devastatingly impressive fashion and she'd probably be favourite for next year's 1,000 Guineas. But that's not what happened. Luckily the remarkable filly she finished second to is trained a thousand miles away from where my horse is trained and we might find it rather easier to avoid her than if she were with Karl Burke. Oisin said it was definitely a career-best and she's got options; she's in the Moyglare, she's in the Cheveley Park and the Rockfel, while the Breeders' Cup remains an option as well. We were going further clear of the third with every stride so she stayed really well, we were just beaten by a better filly. She's every chance of staying a mile, probably not this year though unless we go to the Breeders' Cup - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

Oisin [Murphy, jockey] was upset when he came in after the Albany because he felt he sat too close to a very strong pace. He did realise and took back, but the damage was done by then and we felt on reflection that it was Fitzella's class which allowed her to finish fourth. The plan today was to hold her up and race more patiently, and to use her finish, but she absolutely pinged the lids and Oisin went to plan b. It worked very nicely and he didn't go hard - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred 'Supporting Macmillan' EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Fitzella has done it with the minimum of fuss. We've loved her from day one, I think she was our most expensive yearling last year. Everything we've done with her at home, she's learned and done it so much better the next time, which is exactly what she's done today. She's going to go up massively in grade and I think we'll go for the Albany over six as eventually she's potentially a miler. She's gorgeous and beautifully bred - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A gorgeous filly who has been a star for us. She rushed the gates in the Cheveley Park and crashed her head into them. It's hard to say she completely didn't run her race, but we were expecting more. Because she didn't get into a rhythm after that, she didn't handle the Dip. We were thinking about the Breeders' Cup if she had been right there in the mix, but that will be it for this year. We don't really know what her trip will be as a three-year-old. I think we'll enter her in the 1,000 Guineas and run in a trial. If we come back after the Nell Gwyn and find she doesn't handle the Dip, we could maybe go to the French Guineas. She might be a sprinter as she's fast, but I thought she stayed 7f well in the Prix du Calvados. 08-10-25

quotes.notes: We've always liked Five Ways. He shows a lot of ability in his homework and he won well at Salisbury last time, so we just thought it was worth a go. He'll stay further in time, we'll just have to see if we go again this year. He's a lovely horse for the future. We were a bit disappointed first time out, but the ground was a bit loose and he had a bit of wheelspin and probably needed the run - Andrew Balding. trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Michael Brunton Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: I'm delighted, I bred Five Ways, his dam, grandmother and the one before that. Andrew's always thought he was a good horse but I'm surprised by how easy he's won. We hope he's a nice horse but I've been breeding horses for over 50 years so I know not to get too excited. It was a quick time so it's all looking good. I think he'll stay further and it will be time for a reassessment after that - John Hobby, owner-breeder.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Gowran Classic
Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.raceTitle: Oddschecker Ellen Chaloner Stakes (Listed Race) (Formerly The Kilvington Stakes) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.notes: That's Flora Of Bermuda's first victory for us so we were keen to come here and get her season started, hoping she'd be the class filly in the race. She was tough there, since we've owned her she's been pitched in since all the top sprints so it's great to get her head in front. She's put on a load of weight over the winter and really thickened out so hopefully we can build from here. I've always thought about trying to explore seven [furlongs] with her, I imagine with our brief we'll be aiming towards Ascot but later in the year trying seven might be something we'd like to do as well - Richard Brown, owners' representative, speaking to Racing TV.
I am absolutely delighted. Flora Of Bermuda is such a superstar. We just hope one day she'll get one of these but to be third in another Group One is magnificent - Anna Lisa Balding, trainer's wife.

Flora Of Bermuda ran a hell of a race. She's been off the track for a long time (207 days) and for her to come back and run like that, with the right horse beating her, I think that means she's a really exciting filly. She's always shown a lot at home, Andrew has always liked her and mentally and physically she's developed. We were hoping for a big run and she hasn't disappointed us. I think so (run at Royal Ascot), why not? As PJ (McDonald) said when he got off her, she's got a heart like a lion and you can't ever take that away from her - Anna-Lisa Balding.

Andrew (Balding) was confident Flora Of Bermuda would run a big race and get the trip and I talked to Oisin (Murphy), who thought she was better than her mark. She's starting to mature and behave better now and the race was very smooth for me - PJ McDonald, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: British EBF 40th Anniversary Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/(IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: We think a lot of Flora Of Bemuda. It was a bit of a punt on the ground, but we felt we would learn something if it didn't work. She's got a lot of talent, enjoyed the ground and would have no problem staying six if we put her up. I think that as long as she stays in one piece, black type will not be a problem.  She's in the Lowther and that was always the plan - Andrew Balding, trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: He will have no problem going 7f. We were here to see if Ascot would come too quick for Flushing Meadows, the Coventry would be the race for him, but it seems more likely he'll come back here for the Railway Stakes, we'll take our time - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was second in a couple of Group 3 races last year. We're happy with how he's done over the winter and we think he's a horse for a Derby trial up to a mile and a quarter, and he might get further. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Al Wasl Stakes Sponsored By DP World (Conditions) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Flying Comet bounced out really well and I was happy to track the Godolphin horses with William [Buick] on my left on the favourite. He travelled and, although I was on the wing without cover, I felt I had the race in control all the way through - Silvestre De Sousa, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: There was a lot of pressure as Forever Young was much the best in the field. It's not down to me, it's all down to the horse's ability. Our next target is the Dubai World Cup - Yoshito Yahagi, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.My plan had been to retire Forever Young this year but I can give him an extra two months to come to this race again. He has only run one time in a JRA race, so I would like to see him run there. I don't know if it would be the Arima Kinen, as we have not thought past the Dubai World Cup. But another Saudi Cup, that is my dream - Susumu Fujita, owner.

This is like if the Japanese team won the World Cup. The Japanese racing industry never expected us to win the Breeders' Cup Classic. We appreciate Forever Young and we got to number one in America. Yes, he will be back next year - Yoshito Yahagi, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai World Cup Sponsored By Emirates Airline (Group 1) (Dirt)
quotes.notes: We had to win this race and I am disappointed. Forever Young ran a great race in Saudi and I expected him to win if he ran his race but it was a tough race as he was the horse to beat. It was tough and we did our best. He wasn't traveling at all. It wasn't an easy race and hard to keep winning - Ryusei Sakai, jockey.

This is my second win in the Saudi Cup, but no matter how many wins you have in this race, it is still a great feeling. I believed in Forever Young. When he came here to run in the Saudi Derby, he was not in the best condition and yet he still won. Since that time, he has improved a lot and was in better condition today. We will go to the Dubai World Cup - Yoshito Yahagi, trainer.

Of course it will be very difficult to manage Forever Young's condition from Dubai to Kentucky but I really believe my team will be able to get him in good order. He did not travel well from Japan to Saudi Arabia so he was not in great condition but he still performed very well. After travelling from Riyadh to Dubai he improved and he has so much potential, I always have a lot of confidence in him - Yoshito Yahagi, trainer.

horse_profiles.breeder_name: S A S U Ecurie Des Monceaux Et Al

quotes.raceTitle: Royal Ascot Trials At Naas Handicap
quotes.notes: Fort Vega was a doubt on the quicker ground but we decided to let him take his chance because it was such a good race for him. He's in the Irish 2,000 Guineas, we might think about the Jersey Stakes - Sheila Lavery, trainer
Fort Vega is a really nice colt and still needed that run. A mile on that ground should be perfect for him. He has some smart entries but we won't lose the run of ourselves - Sheila Lavery, trainer

quotes.raceTitle: Every Race Live On Racing TV Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Forty Years On is nice. I haven't had much to do with her at home but George [Scott, trainer] has filled me with confidence and said to ride her like the best filly in the race. She's stepped up a furlong there and it's done no harm. She switched off nicely and I had loads of time to get her into a rhythm. I was worried I got there a bit soon but I had to and she stayed on to the line really well - Darragh Keenan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Forty Years On showed the benefit of a nice first experience at the races. I was a little concerned that the ground had dried up but she more than got away with it. She's very straightforward and has a great mindset. I'd like to look at her numbers to quantify what she did, but she's a three-year-old with some wonderful owners so there's no downside in dipping our toe into a Guineas trial. That would most likely come in France as she'd handle the ground there. She might just have an advantage over those who haven't had a run this season - George Scott, trainer.

Fregada got a touch of sore shins six or seven weeks ago and we backed off her. She did that very well, was impressive. She gallops all over anything we have at home. When she gets a bit of racing she will be really good - Johnny Feane, trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)

quotes.raceTitle: Prix de l'Opera Longines (Group 1) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Her race record has been pretty spectacular this season and it really was push button stuff today. I thought we were going sensible on the front end and Friendly Soul had a wicked turn of foot when I needed it - Kieran Shoemark, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Sumbe Prix Alec Head (Group 2) (3yo Fillies) (Round Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Friendly Soul has only got one blot on her copybook when we rode her wrong in the Musidora. She likes to use her stride. She doesn't have to be on the lead but she doesn't like to be restrained. I don't think she particularly found the ground to her liking, it's tacky and holding out there. If the ground is like last year the Opera would be an option, but not if it's tres souple [very soft]. A mile and three around Del Mar [ Breeders' Cup Filly and Mare Turf ] is like a mile and two in Europe, as it's not a demanding track. It's just the shortest straight in America. But she'll tell us if she wants to go -  John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Friendly Soul was drawn nine in the Musidora and came out of the gates with the racecourse stables on her right and she cocked her jaw. She's a strong-willed lady and cocked her jaw all the way around there which explained that run. We gave her time afterwards, brought her back for this and she's done it in good style. She's the type of filly to get better as the year goes on and I think she's going to be a lovely filly next year - John Gosden, joint-trainer.
Friendly Soul hung throughout the whole race. She's not done that with me before. I couldn't steer her - Kieran Shoemark, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Pretty Polly Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: I think it was a good race. Our other filly (Strutting) was fourth - I think she is more of a staying filly. I was impressed with the second when she won here at the Craven meeting. I think it was a solid race today as the front two drew away from the field. Friendly Soul is a lovely filly and I think she is a mile and a quarter filly. She won't be an Epsom filly but we might make a visit to Chantilly (for the French Oaks) - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: William Hill Two Year Old Trophy (Listed Race)

quotes.notes: Frost At Dawn is a star. She's had plenty of seconds and now a third, but how can you complain? I'd just love to find that win at this level - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Women In Racing/British EBF Cecil Frail Listed Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I think Frost At Dawn is better over five and we'll come back to that trip and might go and run in the King's Stand as the owner is very keen to go to Ascot. She ran a good race at Bath behind the winner when they beat the track record and then she probably veered off the line at Newmarket last time. The older she gets the faster she's getting as she's a bull of a horse. She likes that quick ground and since we've put the visor on her she's improved. She's a quick filly and the stiff five at Ascot would be right up her street. If it was fast ground there I think she could run a massive race. She'd be the fastest I've ever had - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Nad Al Sheba Turf Sprint Sponsored By Emirates Skywards (Group 3) (Turf)
quotes.notes: I had the luck to have a good draw today, so I just played my card. It's the first time I've ridden Frost At Dawn. She's fast and I think she would travel even better over six furlongs - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Highclere Thoroughbred Racing Geoffrey Freer Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Furthur ran a stellar race at Ascot when he was narrowly beaten in the Queen's Vase and we had big hopes in the Bahrain Trophy, but it probably came too soon for him. He's had a nice break since and that was more like him. He's not an overly enthusiastic horse in the morning, but he relaxed beautifully and Oisin rode him lovely. I'm very pleased - Andrew Balding, trainer.

Furthur wasn't an expensive horse and he's given us a huge amount of enjoyment. Hopefully there's more to come as well. We might look at the Bahrain Trophy if he comes out of this alright. He stays well, and might be a Leger horse later in the year - Andrew Balding, trainer.

horse_profiles.breeder_name: Moyns Park Estate And Stud Ltd

quotes.notes: I'm very proud of Galen's run - he had a big penalty, so it was a good effort - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

He's always been a good horse and Galen ran well in Dubai a few times where he just didn't get the rub of the green. He obviously had the fitness edge. Dylan didn't think there was much pace and was happy to go to the front and it was a good performance. I think he does enjoy being ridden like that and the cheekpieces helped him concentrate. We'll look at the Mooresbridge Stakes and then possibly the Tattersalls Gold Cup - Joseph O'Brien, trainer

We couldn't have been more pleased that that. We jumped and I let Galen swing along, good even fractions the whole way and from the top of the straight I let him stretch. He was strong through line. He's going the right way and only going to get better. The ground was a big help, he's a really good mover - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.raceTitle: Molton Brown Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden
quotes.notes: Galen had a setback after his run here last year, he ran a good race here on his comeback and he came forward since then. I don't think they are his conditions, but I'm delighted that he won well - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran great in Hong Kong, ran well in Bahrain and then below par in Saudi Arabia. He's had a rest and will come back for the Wolferton, in which he was just beaten last year. If you look at his form, he's clearly better going right-handed. 22-04-26
