quotes.raceTitle: Revamp Conservation And Restoration Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.notes: You would like to think there would be plenty of improvement as it was Geryon's first day away from Glenburnie and first day on turf. The best-looking horse I had by Lope de Vega was Endless Drama who was second in the Guineas and this is the second best one I've had by him - Ger Lyons, trainer.

We had a magical day in August at Goodwood, and to have another one on this stage is pretty cool! We bought Get It relatively cheaply at the Horses-in-Training sale a couple of years ago and he's won the Racing League, he's won in Bahrain, Stewards' Cup, Wokingham - how many horses have won the Stewards' Cup and Wokingham? Not many. He's a dude of a horse and all credit to everyone involved. He's been a star - George Baker, trainer.

My very clever daughter Tallulah drew 28 when it came out of the hat and we wanted to be this side. Get It has been a real legend for us in Bahrain but he's won a Stewards' Cup for us now so nothing else matters. He'll go back to Bahrain this winter - George Baker, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's all speed. He showed ability at two when he was fourth in the Windsor Castle, but he wasn't straightforward last year, hence the gelding operation. I hope he can enjoy a productive campaign and we'll be able to manage him better now. 21-04-22

Breaking the course record at Ascot in May was exciting, but did I expect him to win a Wokingham off a mark of 100? No, of course not. I think what he did that day was utterly extraordinary. It's not a front-runner's track but to do what he did - and to beat More Thunder, who has shown himself to be a Group performer since. Any year you have a Royal Ascot winner is so special - it's really hard to win there so days like that are pivotal. He won by a head and if he'd lost by a head perhaps the season might look a little different. I think those two Ascot runs took an awful lot out of him. The ground went against him in the Stewards' Cup and he's down to a mark of 102 now and will go to Bahrain this winter. If he can have a wonderful winter there then fantastic, but if we end up at Ascot in June off 97 or 98 so be it. He's not going to go on forever but these sprinters do tend to have a bit more longevity. All roads will lead to Ascot again and then the Stewards' Cup. Horses don't tend to win those races on a multiple basis, but if any horse can I just feel on his day he can do it. He bounces off proper fast ground. 15-10-25

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Magnolia Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Gethin is a work in progress, but I'm pleased with the manner of his win and he should take a step forward from this. He's in the Ganay, but it's potentially the strongest in years so we'll assess our options and make a plan. I've never made any secret that I think the world of him, so I'd like to believe we'll be going into Group 1s with him at some stage - Owen Burrows, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

Gethin is in the Dante and I liked this race as it gives us a bit of time. There's Chester, Lingfield and York, so we can dream and see what's what. We'll see what the opposition is but he's a well-balanced horse and it's a Derby, isn't it. He's still a big, raw baby, so he'll improve for getting that out of his system. He was a bit fresh in the stable earlier, but he's a work-in-progress and you can't be anything but impressed with him - Owen Burrows, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British EBF Future Stayers Oath Novice Stakes (Sire And Dam Restricted Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: It was an impressive performance. I was always confident that I was going to win quite well. Gethin just had a wander around when he got to the front but he's entitled to do that. He's gone through the line well. He's gone through that ground well. It would be nice to see him in the spring on better ground doing something similar, but he'll be a nice middle-distance horse. I don't think he needs to rush up in trip - Callum Rodriguez, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

horse_profiles.breeder_name: P Taplin & Mike Channon Bloodstock Ltd

quotes.raceTitle: Weatherbys Racing Bank Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Getreadytorumble has a lot of boot and is from a very fast family. He had a few issues at two but has come to hand nicely. The ground was a bit too quick for him, but he had a bit too much class for the others. I'm hoping it will be onwards and upwards when we go into handicaps - Jack Channon, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Extra Places Every Day Handicap
quotes.notes: I've won on Glenfinnan before so was probably entitled to have another go on him. He did well to finish off like that considering that he was a bit keen through the race. I'd say a stiff six would be fine but he did get the seven well. The ground not being too fast probably helped him - Oisin Murphy, rider.

Today worked out well on Glenfinnan, who has plenty of pace. He enjoyed travelling quite strongly and, when I switched out, it always felt he'd hit the line in front. He galloped out strongly and I hope he can finish the season on a high. The stiff 7f probably suited, but I don't know what races Andrew has in mind for him - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran really well in the Wokingham, where he finished fifth behind Unequal Love. We thought he was worth perservering with over 6f, but at Goodwood in the Stewards' Cup last time the track was probably on the quick side for him and he finished well down the field. He's by Harry Angel and probably a little bit of cut would do him good. It may also have come too quickly for him after the Wokingham - he had another run at Ascot in between too. He seems to be coming back to form now, though. He's entered in the Ayr Gold Cup but we might give him a run over 7f first, possibly at Thirsk on Friday. 28-08-24

quotes.raceTitle: Jenningsbet In Kippax Seaton Delaval Handicap
quotes.notes: Godwinson has done really well to get himself out of trouble, he got into a good rhythm and was always going to produce something, it can be tough to close off a slow pace. This seems like his way of doing things as he has put a couple of wins together in a similar style. He loves to be fresh but unfortunately the ground hasn't been kind to him, we just need a drop of rain. I suppose those big handicaps like the Lincoln and competitive races like this suit him, where it is busy and he can sit in. He's going in the right direction - Tom Marquand, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

Godwinson got a great run through but he gave him a very confident ride. Fair play, that's what he wanted to do and I thought that was a good idea. We thought the ground had dried up a bit too much for him but clearly not. I didn't think he was well handicapped - but he wasn't that well treated, he only won by a nose and a head! - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap
quotes.notes: That was a surprise, it felt like the handicapper had Golden Mind. He was drawn on the far side and I was adamant he should stay there. He's a good old horse and that's three he's won this year - Richard Fahey, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Free Bet With Unibet's Betbuilder Rebound Handicap (London Sprint Series Qualifier)
quotes.notes: There didn't seem to be much pace so when Golden Mind broke well I was able to get across and went fairly steady, getting the race my own way to be honest, and he's quickened up and done it well in the end. He gets 7f and I could see him going up in trip again - Oisin Orr, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Blandford Bloodstock Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.notes: Golden Orbit has shown a nice attitude and has galloped all the way to the line. She'll be a nice filly next year - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: An exciting filly. To win over seven furlongs, with that pedigree, gives us significant cause for optimism. She has an Oaks entry and will run in a trial somewhere. We haven't turned any screws yet, but we saw her ability at two and, hopefully, it will all come together at three. 27-04-26

quotes.notes: I'm delighted for Goliath. That will have done wonders for his morale and he clearly enjoyed being back over a mile and a half. Clement [Lecoeuvre] rode his last piece of work on Tuesday and my only instructions were to let him stride on and not to fight him. The idea of going to Germany was that it's a bonus race for the Japan Cup. Before that he could go to the Breeder's Cup, which would please his owner John Stewart - Francis Graffard, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix Gontaut-Biron Hong Kong Jockey Club (Group 3) (4yo+) (Round Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: I think Goliath just got beaten by a better horse on the day. It was his first race after a long break and he had a little bit of trouble after Saint-Cloud. He fought very bravely and I thought for a second he'd won. We'll probably take him back to 12 furlongs, I think that's his right distance. We'll see where we go. I think Baden-Baden could be a very good option - Philip Baron von Ullman, part-owner and breeder.

Goliath had the perfect run. We knew Junko was going to go to the front and he travelled nice and relaxed in behind him. When they entered the straight and he pulled him out, we can see he didn't pick up like he's used to doing. Christophe [Soumillon] was very easy on him and he seems to be fine after the race, but we'll investigate. It's very hot today but obviously he didn't give his running - Francis Graffard, trainer.

Today was a real test in terms of Goliath's temperament and whether he put himself under pressure. The twice he has really dropped the bit and relaxed was when Maxime Guyon made the running on him here, and then at Ascot, when they went a really honest pace. Those races are when you've seen the real Goliath. Every other time we've tried to restrain him and take a lead and it hasn't worked at all for him. Both John Stewart and Philip von Ullmann said to me after Hong Kong, 'Let's forget all the plans we had for this year and go back to square one; you tell us what you want to do with the horse.' I wanted to find an easier race for him to boost his morale and get him back on the right track. They left it to me and it seems to have worked - Francis Graffard, trainer.

We acknowledge there are no excuses for Goliath. While the pace was slower than anticipated, we expected this outcome. Achieving this level of competition in any sport is a remarkable feat, and we look forward to returning to compete with the strongest horses from around the globe - John Stewart, owner, posting on X.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix du Conseil de Paris (Group 2) (3yo+) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Goliath had a lot of things against him; he was carrying a penalty and he needed the run because he's a huge horse. This ground is not what he prefers and the race was full of potential traps, with a small number of runners. But Christophe [Soumillon] has begun to really get to know him and he has a lot of confidence in him. He gave him a chance to stretch out when he started to pull in the false straight. He took a gulp of air halfway up the straight and Christophe respected his horse before they went on again," he said. "I'm delighted to have won but this was all about getting a run into him on the way to Japan, and he's now got that out of the way, that's the most important thing - Francis Graffard, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Qipco Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: I know Goliath, with a good pace, could quicken like this. We came to Ascot to find a strong pace and still at Royal Ascot he was too keen, so I was really hoping for some pace here. But to be fair when I saw the 25-1 I was like 'Oh my God, nobody believes in him'. He travelled so nicely though and when he was like that, I knew he'd be able to quicken strongly - Francis Graffard, trainer.

We came here because we wanted to avoid the French style of racing, with no pace, and unfortunately today they decided to do a little bit of the same. Goliath was a bit too keen through the race; he's difficult to manage, but not too bad today. I walked the course and there was a good cover of grass and I thought it was safe ground for him, but he's probably better with a bit of cut. He has to settle in his races to be able to stay and to produce a good turn of foot, but we are very pleased with the run - he's a very nice horse and we beat some very nice horses, too. He's entered in the King George, but we'll see what the weather forecast is. I don't know - it's a long journey and a tough race, but why not? - Francis-Henry Graffard, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He did really well last year, winning four times. He's been a little disappointing this season but I think possibly the handicapper's got hold of him. He went up from 68 - the mark he won his first race off last year - to starting this year on 92. With a bit of luck, he'll start winning again soon - and he runs at Newmarket on Thursday. 02-07-25

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won the Glencairn Stakes at Leopardstown last season before running well in the Irish Derby. He finished fourth in the York Stakes but picked up an injury in the race and missed the rest of the campaign. He returned at the Curragh this month, finishing fourth in the Alleged, and we were very happy with the run. Hopefully it can be a nice stepping stone towards the Tattersalls Gold Cup. We've always thought an awful lot of him. At the moment we think a mile and a quarter is his ideal trip. He's a big, high cruiser and he's really filled his frame this year. The form of the York Stakes looks pretty good too. The ground was a little bit too soft for him at the Curragh but it was a very pleasing run and it's all roads towards the Tattersalls Gold Cup. 27-04-26

quotes.notes: We were hopeful of a good run after being a bit disappointed with Green Sense's effort at Ascot. The Cheveley Park Stakes looks an obvious target for her now and we could even have a look at the Prix Morny en route - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tote Never Beaten By SP Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.notes: Green Sense probably did more than we thought to be honest. We hoped she would run well, there's a fillies maiden in a few weeks we were set to go for after this. You would have to be impressed by her attitude, she went through the line well. Cowardofthecounty won this last year before going to Ascot, we probably should have given him another run in the meantime, so probably we'll go somewhere between now and Ascot with the filly, either the Marble Hill or the Coolmore Fillies Race at Naas- Joseph O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She won the Prix Robert Papin last year and is now in a tough spot as she's heavily penalised in Listed and Group 3 races. quotes.notes: Gstaad is a lovely, uncomplicated horse and Ryan [Moore] gave him a beautiful ride. A very straightforward and genuine horse. Ryan said he was a little bit lazy through the race but when he got him opened up, he went to the line very well. He got beat in three Group 1s last year and we felt he was a little bit unlucky each time and we were obviously delighted when he held on to go to America to win his Group 1. Sometimes, when that happens, horses don't get back but we felt there were circumstances every time he got beat. He's very straightforward, he just needs a little bit of room to get going. Ryan was drawn wide and you'd say that's a disadvantage for some horses but it was lovely for him as he was going to get a clear run at it. You never know how long they'll last when they're racing at that level, but he lasted to America and then won very easily first time over a mile. It's lovely to have a horse where it doesn't matter if they go fast or slow as he's happy to go along and if the pace is on then he's happy to sit in. He's a very solid, big horse. We always thought he'd end up getting even a little bit further than a mile. We always thought he could turn into a Cox Plate horse but there's a lot of water to go under the bridge before then - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

I am pleased with Gstaad and that was a great run. Ryan [Moore] was very happy today and he has done everything right. It was his first run of the year, and you can see he's a big horse. It was great to get him started. I think there were two lengths between us and the winner (it was actually two and three-quarter lengths) and eight lengths back to the third. We couldn't be happier really. He's a big, powerful horse and that type of horse can only progress. We used today as a start off and tried to do our best to win on his first start as a three-year-old. We are still delighted with how he has run. We always thought that he could go further, although I don't know where we would go from here. The Irish Guineas would be the logical step, and I imagine that's what the lads would be thinking about - Aidan O'Brien.

quotes.raceTitle: Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf (Grade 1) (2yo Colts & Geldings) (Turf)
quotes.notes: I didn't do anything really, I think Gstaad is just good. He's been a little bit unlucky in Europe on his last few starts, we should've won one of them. He jumped a bit slow today, but he was travelling very well in the first part of the race. When I saw there was a gap in the back straight to try to go forward and let him sit behind the pace, I made the move and I was cruising the whole way. I knew when I came out of the turn that I'd win. It's very rare to see amazing horses winning a Breeders' Cup hands and heels like that - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

Next year Gstaad will be older and stronger, but he ran a good race and you have to be very happy with him. I think the race worked out lovely. He would be one for an English or Irish 2,000 Guineas - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Sumbe Prix Morny (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Gstaad ran a great race, we're delighted. It's a long time since he ran but we're over the moon. We had it in our head he could go back to the National Stakes, so that's where he could go next. He'd have no problem with seven furlongs - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

Gstaad looks a very good horse, doesn't he? We've always loved him. He had only had the one run. He has always worked like a good horse. He's big, he's scopey, he has a good stride and is very genuine; he goes with his head down and he has loads of speed. He looks like he will get further than six [furlongs] - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Gstaad was very impressive. I thought he travelled beautifully, and we got to the front a long way from home. He's a tall horse and is obviously improving with each run and that was a very good performance - Ryan Moore, jockey.

He was a little bit babyish going down but Gstaad was a pro in the race. When Wayne (Lordan) kicked he got a bit disorganised but from the furlong pole I always thought I was going to get there. I'll think he'll sharpen up for it, he'll get another furlong - Chris Hayes, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was always a hardy horse and won the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf on his final start of the season. When he finished second in the Dewhurst, Christophe made the decision to take him back after he jumped, and was caught in the middle of two. When he came back, they all came back and there ended up being no pace. We felt there was more to come from him after that and he went and won in America, coasting around and not doing a lot when he got there. I wouldn't be afraid to let him flow because he isn't a keen horse but has a long stride and a big action. He's being trained for a Guineas. Ryan rode him at the Curragh on Sunday and he had it in his head he could be one for Newmarket. But we'll see how Puerto Rico and Albert Einstein are over the next few weeks. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: The trip was a doubt in my mind and that's been compounded by the ground. Half Sovereign travelled lovely turning in and I thought we were in with a squeak, but she just didn't get home - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs "Carrie Red" EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
quotes.notes: The plan was to come here and then go for a valuable Tattersalls sales race [at Newmarket] as she's only got a very low weight because of her cost. Then there's a nice Listed fillies' race in France at the end of October. Because Half Sovereign only cost 12,000gns as a yearling, you're a little bit negative in your thoughts of her, but she's done nothing but improve with every run, so who knows where she'll end up - Karl Burke, trainer.
Half Sovereign is a big, rangy filly who will be better next year. She did that well considering the track and ground didn't really play to her strengths - James Cowley, assistant to Karl Burke.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.notes: Half Sovereign keeps improving and she's a big filly. I thought we got easily in front and I was pulling up as we got to the line. Karl's got plenty of ammunition and maybe a nursery is the way forward with her, but we'll see. I think she could be versatile with the trip - Sam James, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: EBF Stallions Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: I was very pleased with the way Half Sovereign ran first time. She was green, missed the break over six furlongs, I was on my head the whole way and she came home really well. We expected her to do that today stepping up to seven and she'll even get a mile. She's a lovely big, strong filly who will probably get better as she gets older - Sam James, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: Fetched a huge price at the sales and we're very grateful to Lady Bamford for sending her back to us. She was always a big, leggy two-year-old and she's gone forward physically and got stronger. She goes to Deauville on April 7 for a French Guineas trial [Prix Imprudence] and will go for the French Guineas if it all goes well. 31-03-26

He's a very talented horse and he'll keep improving. I'd probably look to go for the handicap [Wokingham] at Royal Ascot with him - Kevin Ryan, trainer.

quotes.notes: Hankelow would definitely stay another furlong and maybe another two, so the Prix du Jockey Club would be top of the list. He loved that ground and he's never had the soft he's wanted, so we're very happy with the run without winning - Karl Burke, trainer.

Hankelow has got such a great mind on him and can only get better. I think he will be better on a more level track - I'll see what Cliff (Lee, jockey) says - and certainly with more juice in the ground. He didn't have the best preps going into Doncaster last time. It was nothing major, but it was just a bit stop-start for the two or three weeks before. I think that is what got him beat that day. The step up in trip suited him today. You only have to look at him going round the prelims to see he is a very relaxed horse. He a good horse. Whether he is quick enough for a Guineas or whether we step up to a mile and a quarter - we have plenty of time to think about that - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: He's never even had a gallop away from home, but is a beautiful horse - as he's entitled to be as Hankelow cost a lot of money. He's shown plenty of ability at home without overdoing himself and he'll improve a bundle. I wouldn't run him on anything quicker than it was at this stage. He'll stay and over a mile I'd say he's a Group horse in the making - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A proper high-class colt who's really starting to work and look well. He's on target for the Guineas, providing the ground is right as he doesn't want it firm. He was going to go straight there but he's further forward than I thought, so he might go to the Craven. If it's obvious he's not going to be quick enough for a Guineas, we've still got plenty of time to go for the Dante or something like that. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: We might as well have a look at Goodwood now, but I don't think Havana Hurricane wants soft ground as it just dents his turn of foot. I don't know if we'll go five or six furlongs just yet, I need to have a think about it - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

I said to the owners, win lose or draw, Havana Hurricane cost you 9,000 guineas, you've made more than that and you're here to play. We've had a great day, but I think he's pretty special. He won really easily. Charlie gave him the most lovely ride. He waited, he was incredibly patient, and I'm very proud. Tom [Clemmit, groom] is in charge of the bottom yard which is where all the two-year-old colts are, and he does this horse and has done a great job with him. He's pretty laidback, pretty easy, but my staff do a great job and they've done a great job with him - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.Havana Hurricane is a lovely horse. He didn't stay six furlongs at Epsom, and I was very confident coming here today, which is a very strange thing to say coming to Ascot, but he quickened up very well - he's a smart horse. I felt he was the best horse in the race at Epsom, and if he had got home he would have won, and with a stiff five here, the race was made for him. You've got to get a bit of luck in running, and I did - Charles Bishop, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred British EBF Woodcote Stakes (Conditions Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: That was a great run. Having not really handed the hill, and Charlie [Bishop] might possibly have got there too soon, having had to work to get there, Havana Hurricane has run a blinder and I'm thrilled with him. He looked like he was going to win a furlong out and maybe, on this ground, he was outstayed. The winner is probably a really good horse, but we're very happy with ours for our nine grand! - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: It was exciting to see him win the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot. He didn't stay the 6f in the Woodcote when he was second behind Maximise but he showed a great turn of foot back over 5f. He's in the Super Sprint but we won't necessarily go there - we might go for the Molecomb, although the Super Sprint is before that. Then we'd possibly need to look at the Nunthorpe. He's got great speed. 02-07-25

quotes.notes: Christophe [Soumillon] was very happy. He said he couldn't believe how babyish Hawk Mountain was still, but said he won very snug.  He said he was very green. I'm delighted we sent him to the track if we are going to send him to the French Derby. He's been around the track and seen it - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.He will come forward a lot for that run and there wasn't much choice but to make the running from stall one. Aidan [O'Brien] asked me to ride him for himself and he's a horse that gets comfortable in his own rhythm. He was very relaxed throughout but he just had a look around a couple of times, bumping the rail early on and then turning into the straight when he just went a little bit wide. But when I asked him to pick up the answer was there. He'll be much better in a race with more pace in it, so it was a lovely performance. It was really deep ground when he won the Futurity and today it was much quicker than that, and he handled it very well, while I loved the way he moved as we cantered to the start. It was the same story in the straight. The more I asked the more he went away, all the time under a hand ride. I didn't have to touch him. I think there are a few more lengths under the bonnet there. He'll get 2,000 metres [1m2f] with no problem. After that we'll have to see how he takes the race. He was very good at a mile, while 2,400 metres [1m4f] is another game - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Futurity Trophy Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.notes: I'd say Mountain Hawk is a Classic horse that could start off being a miler and go on up to a mile and a quarter/a mile and a half. He's a classy horse, he gets a mile well and he's tough. He's a massive horse, a big, powerful strong horse. He has an unbelievable mind and he's very straightforward to do everything with. You couldn't be happier with him, he's one of those nice, uncomplicated, powerful big horses. He's big but he's athletic. - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Hawk Mountain travelled like a nice horse through the race. For a few strides when Wayne [Lordan] came beside me I hit a bit of a flat spot but that's all it was. Once I got going again I always felt like I was winning. It was just a matter of keeping him together. He felt like he was still a bit green and I felt there was plenty left in him - Ronan Whelan, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Racing & Equestrian Club Beresford Stakes (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: As soon as I got a backhander into Hawk Mountain, he just came alive underneath me. He was very strong at the line. He even spotted something at the line and pricked his ears, so he had loads left. He'll be a middle-distance horse next year, but I definitely think he has the class to go a mile and a quarter. That will open up options for him and he'll have no problem going a mile and a half. He's versatile ground-wise and got through that ground very well today - Ronan Whelan, jockey.Hawk Mountain is a smashing colt. Obviously, he's got the sire and the dam [Wootton Bassett out of Hydrangea], and he has plenty of size and scope. Whatever he does at two we think will be a bonus. He's in the mix for the Futurity Trophy in Doncaster or maybe he could go to France, the race at Saint-Cloud. He's one to look forward to for middle distances next year - Chris Armstrong, trainer's representative.

quotes.raceTitle: John Ormonde Wexford Sand Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.notes: Big, rangy, relaxed horse, could be anything in time. Wayne (Lordan) says Hawk Mountain was very green but has the makings of a lovely horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won three last year, including the Futurity Trophy at Doncaster. He went very well at the Curragh on Sunday. Dean [Gallagher] rode him and he was very happy with him. stable_tour_quotes.notes: The time before she won at Newcastle at 200-1, she was badly drawn at Redcar and finished ninth. She's a big, heavy-topped filly and they take some learning as you daren't push them at home. quotes.raceTitle: Racing Value At bet365 Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Hey Boo gave me a great feel. I managed to get her mid-div, she switched off lovely in her race. She picked up well, and I thought she was quite professional for a filly having her first start on a racecourse. She's knuckled down well, I love her attitude, she's done it in a nice style - George Bass, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's won her first two starts this year at Chelmsford and I think a lot of her. I've run out of words. I'm just overwhelmed by everything. Hochkonig has done so well and of course Nina got it right and was so intelligent. quotes.raceTitle: Raymond & Kathleen Corbett Memorial City Plate Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: No horse deserves a win like this horse as he's been running great, including in the Jersey Stakes last time. Holguin still looks unfurnished and I think he's going to get better and better - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Joe Mercer Memorial EBF Maiden Stakes (IRE Incentive Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Holguin probably wants another furlong. He's our first two-year-old runner so we didn't know what to expect but he's got lots of scope and will be a nice horse. Berkshire Shadow went on and won the Coventry but Holguin will have another run before we make a plan. It looks like six furlongs will be his thing - Andrew Balding, trainer.

horse_profiles.owner_name: N White, S White, T White & E Burke

quotes.notes: Rab [Havlin, jocked on Chancellor] was always getting closer and closer to me, but Holloway Boy pulled out what he needed. It probably wasn't ideal for him but he kept pulling out more. He hasn't won many races, but he's never run a bad race. He ran against Nations Pride and Romantic Warrior in Dubai and he's going to be very competitive in Dubai again this season. It wouldn't surprise me to see him win one of those races, he's pretty high class - William Buick, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Best Odds On The Betfair Exchange Superior Mile Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Holloway Boy is a very talented horse - he always has been - but he just saves a little bit for himself, as you saw there in the last furlong when he was just pulling up a little bit. He'll handle any ground and will run right the way through. I wouldn't mind traveling with him abroad, maybe to Dubai or Saudi, as he's the type of horse who could go anywhere - Karl Burke, trainer.
Holloway Boy ran his usual game race but was carrying plenty of weight. The Balmoral at Ascot at the end of the season would be perfect race for him - Karl Burke, trainer.

Holloway Boy has run a great race again. I just said to the owners he's strung three races in a row now in big handicaps. It's so hard and he was giving 18lb to the winner, who was a much higher-rated horse a year or so ago, and we've also given about a stone away to the second. He travelled beautifully through the race, possibly we got there 100 yards too soon but I don't think so. We were just beaten by better-handicapped horses on the day. It would probably be wise to look for a Listed event or a Group 3 now - he's that type of class. The draw didn't help us either. We're disappointed to get beaten but he's run very well - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tattersalls Stakes (Registered As The Somerville Tattersall Stakes) (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: We're delighted with that as Holloway Boy missed eight to ten days with a dirty scope when he missed that Champagne Stakes. Danny Tudhope said he would be suited by a mile so we could look at the Vertem Futurity Trophy or beyond that the Breeders' Cup - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Japan Racing Association Vintage Stakes (Group 2) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: Holloway Bay has pulled a front right-fore shoe off, which hasn't helped, but the winner just had a bit more turn of foot. Danny says he feels like a top-class horse and he's got a great cruising speed, although probably just lacks that kick at an important stage. He's run a great race and the Champagne Stakes is the obvious target, and Doncaster should suit him better than here - Karl Burke, trainer.

Unbelievable. The truth is we were going to go to Musselburgh for the Sunday Series but Holloway Boy pulled a little muscle so we didn't go then the owner rang me up. He said he was supposed to have a box but was let down and wanted to get some tickets. I entered the horse and thought 'I'm not going to run him' but I thought sod it, we'll run him, give him a nice day out. It was superb by Danny, we were always going to ride him that way. He rides this track fantastically. We thought he was a nice horse but I didn't quite think he was that good. He's only had a quiet blow, he hasn't had a hard race - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He had another good winter season in Dubai and we brought him back early to try to get a nice summer out of him. If he gets invited to Hong Kong, he could go out there for the Mile, otherwise there's a Listed race at Ascot in early May. He's come back in serious form. 31-03-26

He raised a few eyebrows last year when making a winning debut in the Chesham Stakes at Royal Ascot. I won't say I wasn't pleasantly surprised, but I would not have run him in the race if I did not think he was smart. He subsequently ran big races in Group company without getting his head in front again. On his final run in the Futurity Stakes people labelled him as a lairy horse, but I think he is more of a lazy colt. I think the combination of being in front too soon and wearing a visor first time resulted in his odd run. His preparations for the 2,000 Guineas have not gone smoothly but we are getting there now, and his work last week was very pleasing. He's another who could go under the radar and although Auguste Rodin looks seriously smart, there are few others that frighten me. 07-05-23

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Gowran Classic

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Futurity Trophy Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.notes: Hotazhell is  a smashing horse, he's very tough and he loves a battle. I don't think he'll ever win races by large margins, he loves just looking at the other horse and saying 'I'm better than you'.  He's a little bit feisty, he ain't called Hotazhell for nothing.   I'd say he'll start off over a mile and take it from there. He'll probably stay a mile and a quarter. I'm not sure he'll stay a mile and a half but you never know, he's a very relaxed horse and he just might.  He's done very well, he's won a Group 3, a Group 2 and now a Group 1. That's just the start of his career hopefully and he'll go on next year and get better - Jessica Harrington, trainer.

I knew the step up in trip was always going to be an advantage to Hotazhell as was the slower ground - Shane Foley, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.  He got a bit free coming down the hill but today Hotazhell came around a bend and did it well. When he gets to the front he pricks his ears and doesn't really do that much. He's straightforward at home but when we come racing we saddle him in the racecourse stables rather than the saddling boxes and keep a red hood on him just to keep the lid on him. He'll go to Doncaster - Jessica Harrington, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.
Hotazhell is a nice colt. They went a good gallop and he picked up well. He is tough and he just does enough. We might go for a nice race over 1m in September - Jessica Harrington, trainer

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran some crackers in top races last season, such as finishing third in the Irish 2,000 Guineas and fourth in the Irish Champion Stakes. He's looking good at the moment and seems to have strengthened up a good bit over the winter. We're very happy with him and the plan is to start off in the Amethyst at Leopardstown on May 10. Hopefully that might be a winnable opportunity for him as he won't have to carry a penalty. The main aim will be to get him to the Breeders' Cup at Keeneland in the autumn. We think a mile and a quarter is his trip and he'll go on any ground. He won the Futurity as a two-year-old on soft and just missed out in the Saratoga Derby last year on firm. 27-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: Ice Dancer is a fine, big filly. She might go to the Silken Glider next. Whatever she does at two will be a bonus - Chris Armstrong, trainer's representative.

horse_profiles.owner_name: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

quotes.notes: We thought Illinois would be a Gold Cup horse next year, and obviously it was the plan Kyprios would come here this year and he would step up next year. The plan was for him to go to the Coronation [Cup] and I was training him as a good mile and a half-horse, and then when Kyprios retired we switched him to this race. We have to be happy with the run and he had a lovely preparation the last day. Maybe if we knew he was coming here straightaway, we might have had him going earlier and maybe lighter. He might go to Goodwood and meet this horse again and I would imagine he will progress again then. He got tired at the two-furlong pole today, like a lot of horses do, and we will see if we can improve him another little bit for this distance. It shows how good Kyprios was as Trawlerman had been second to him a couple of times, I think - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Ladbrokes Big-Value You Can Bet On Ormonde Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: That was very pleasing, he's a lovely horse. Illinois is a big, fine, strong animal so he will improve for the run. Ryan was very happy with him. He was waiting for someone at the bend to take him there and they didn't so he just had to go. He was just playing around in front at the end there but he's a lovely horse. He's very versatile. We've just been talking to Aidan and you could drop him back in trip for the Coronation Cup or you could step him up to Cup races. He'd do whatever you want for you. You can see what he did last year, he's a proper horse. He's a two-time Group 2 winner and carried the penalty today and did it really well. He's a lovely horse to have, we're lucky - Paul Smith, representing the owners.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred St Leger Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: They are two very good horses and clearly there's nothing between them. Sean gave the winner a very good ride and neither stopped all the way down the straight. We knew the winner had improved a lot since Goodwood and he's a classy horse. Either of them could go to Melbourne, they're two classy stayers but Illinois would have no problem coming back to a mile and a half - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Illinois stays very well and looked like he was going to lose second, but fought back and that usually suggests that he wants that staying trip, as he showed at Ascot too - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

We felt any of the three could win. Ryan made the decision to ride Illinois, and he had the choice of the King Edward VII Stakes or this race. He's obviously a St Leger-type horse and is going to improve from three to four. He's a bit of a baby mentally still, so he might have a little rest now and maybe go to York on the way to the Leger, something like that. I think he might have a little bit more class than a Cup horse. His sister won the Arc, so he's that type  - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Illinois ran a lovely race and just got a bit tired in the deep ground. He was working lovely, but he's a big horse and we didn't want to over-squeeze him for his first run because we felt the season was going to be long for him. We've often felt with those type of horses that if you over-squeeze them early in the season, it can catch you in the middle of the season so we just had him ready to run and he ran a lovely race. Ryan said he struggled in the ground and he will come forward a lot from it - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.
Ryan was very happy with Illinois. He's still a baby and will improve plenty - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Shoda Market Cafe Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.notes: Illinois is a beautiful colt. There's not too many that when you go down past the two and a half, they say point me. I actually got there too soon because I thought he'd take a bit of stoking. He has a lot going for him - pedigree, scope, size, action, wind. He was pretty much a steering job and I'm going to miss these Galileos - Seamie Heffernan, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran some great races last season, winning the Ormonde Stakes and finishing second in the Ascot Gold Cup and behind Scandinavia at Goodwood. We're happy with him and he'll go into the staying bracket again. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Harry's Half Million By Goffs (GBB Race)

quotes.raceTitle: Racing Foundation Supports The NHC EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: I thought Innichen did a good job. He's still learning. When I went to present him to the front he needed a couple of flicks to get him up into gear but he's a bonny little horse and it's nice to get his head in front. He'll definitely get six furlongs, it's whether the competition at six is worth taking on or whether we should utilise the fact that he now has three runs under his belt. He'll get sharper and sharper as he goes - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Mitsubishi Electric Curragh Irish EBF Curragh Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I knew Ipanema Queen gets 6f so I was happy to make it a test. I felt like she might empty but when I really got stuck into her she was good and tough. She got tired late on but got away with it. She's very fast and feels like a filly who will appreciate easier ground. She has a good attitude - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: She's a nice filly. Ipanema Queen was ready to run early on but then she got a little bit weak and we gave her a break. She was well coming here but I'd say she was only 75% today and there should be more to come. We have her entered for the Group 2 here on Derby weekend. We wanted to run today because if she did well we would try and run her in the Albany at Ascot. That's the plan - assistant trainer Robson Aguiar.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won a 7f maiden at Goodwood last year and was then fourth and fifth in a couple of races in France. We think he's much better than people think and he could improve a good bit. He's a 1m2f-1m4f horse. I'm not sure whether he'll make a Derby ahead of the others - he could end up at Royal Ascot instead. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: Italy ran very well. He's a lovely big horse. He will progress - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

He was never away before so Italy would have been very green, and they went a good gallop. He has a bit of quality and Wayne gave him a lovely ride. He taught him plenty and he will have leaned a lot from that. He could come back here for the Tyros - Aidan O'Brien, trainer

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He had some very good runs last year over seven furlongs, finishing second in the Superlative and Acomb Stakes before a third in the National Stakes. We might go up in trip with him and he could turn into a nice horse going a mile and a quarter. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dante Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: That was brilliant. We just really didn't know [coming into today]. We were hopeful as Item has done some great bits of work. Andrew has really liked him, and we went into the winter dreaming. The dream continues. It would be amazing to have a Derby runner. It's what we all do it for. Andrew has said very publicly he would love to win the Derby - Anna Lisa Balding, wife of winning trainer Andrew Balding.I thought we were going along nice and evenly. Item was still a little bit in my hands, but it was his first run of the season and he was entitled to be a bit fresh as he has been off the track for a while. As the race went on, he relaxed and got into a nice rhythm. I was pretty happy after that. I thought he got to Wayne [Lordan, rider of runner-up Action] well. I thought that he was going to go away but he just seemed to prick his ears and just ran around a small bit. But it was only his third start, so he is entitled to do that. I don't think you really know how they'll handle Epsom until you go there but he jumps, he travels and is a well-balanced horse, so hopefully he'll be fine - Colin Keane, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: British EBF Future Stayers' Novice Stakes (Sire & Dam Restricted Race) (Plus 10) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.notes: It's a difficult track, but the key today was to bring Item here and educate him regardless of where he finished. He showed a lot of ability and has a big engine. He's learnt as much before and after as he did in the race, because he probably finds galloping the easiest part. It's hard to know exactly what level he's run to, but the feel he gave me and the way he took it all in is exciting for connections. Doncaster [for the Futurity] will really suit him and he certainly won't be the worst horse in the race. He found the line well today without me getting too serious on him. With his big, beautiful stride I don't think softer ground will be an issue - Rob Hornby, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

I didn't expect Jakajaro to lead this field in such a high-quality race but he's just getting better and he's getting faster. I don't know why. He had talent when he was in Ireland and he contested some pretty snazzy races last year. This year he's been a different horse altogether. Maybe it's just that he's a year older and we know a little bit more about him. He'll have to go up to stakes company now, he's earned it. He's in the Temple Stakes and he could quite easily go for something like that - Robert Cowell, trainer.

It wasn't the plan to make the running with Jakajaro but Jamie walked the track beforehand and the far side was the place to be. It's nice that he's retained all his old abilities - Robert Cowell, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: La Celia Wines Sprint Nursery Handicap
quotes.notes: Jakajaro was a horse I thought would win a maiden. This is a good horse. He was still green today and hopefully he will go on. He's in the big sales race here in September and that will be in his target - David Marnane, trainer

stable_tour_quotes.notes: His win at York last week was really good. He won decisively and certainly merits going up in class now, as he did that very well. He's entered in the King Charles III but will probably go next to the Temple Stakes on Saturday as long as the ground is good or softer. We'll see about Royal Ascot after that. He's moving in the right direction, which is really positive. The race he won at York was won last year by American Affair, who went on to win the King Charles III. There will be options but I think he is slightly more ground-dependent, in that it's got to be good or slower for him. It's 11 years since we won the King Charles III (or the King's Stand as it was then), and it would be great to win it again if we could. 20-05-26

Aziz Kheir Aust Partners & Kevin Blake

quotes.raceTitle: Cashel Palace Hotel Derby Trial Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: We were a bit worried about the fast ground because James J Braddock's maiden win last year was on soft. You'd have to say that he handled it well. Before today we were thinking that he might be a horse for the King Edward in Ascot. That's the race we were working towards, but I suppose we now have to consider other options as well. This is going to be a horse that will hopefully turn up in top international races through the course of his career. Today was obviously a big step forward. We've always thought he'd love going 1m4f - Joseph O'Brien, trainer

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's smart and a very good work horse. He had a good run in a tricky race in the Ballysax Stakes and will have learned a lot from that. We've always had him in mind as a middle-distance or staying horse and he looked like that at Leopardstown. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: James's Delight enjoys the soft ground and we have an entry in the Champions Day Sprint. We're forecast some hotter temperatures so we'll play our cards accordingly - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Churchill Tyres Supporting Macmillan Sprint Handicap
quotes.notes: That was wonderful, I'm so pleased. It was a very confident ride from Ryan, as always. The way that he changed gear there today fills me full of excitement. James's Delight does appreciate the ground, although he won on good ground on Guineas day at Newmarket he prefers this end of the scale.  We'll see how he comes back before we think of the Wokingham but winning today means he'll have a penalty and that will be on top of a mark of 102 so we'll see. But he's clearly a three-year-old going places - Clive Cox, trainer.
James's Delight did that well. Last time over seven furlongs was a bit of a non event and he enjoyed this trip of six furlongs a lot better - Richard Kingscote, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: We were thrilled with his Group 2 success in the Greenlands Stakes at the Curragh. I'm delighted how he's been able to move through the ranks and he's come back really fresh and well. If we had any rain in the meantime it would be in his favour. 10-06-25

He put up a pleasing performance to win at Newbury last month on his debut in the colours of Paul and Clare Rooney, who we've had some great days with in the past. James's Delight is out of a Pivotal mare and I thought that may count on his debut where the ground was on the soft side. He showed a great attitude and I was impressed with his positive response in the closing stages. He has qualified for the Goffs sales race at Naas in Ireland later on and we will obviously seriously consider that option. He is a horse to look forward to. 02-08-23

horse_profiles.owner_name: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)

quotes.notes: Jan Brueghal has a good record but he was off since the King George where things went wrong. It was nice to get him back today and that was a good performance - Ryan Moore, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.Ryan [Moore] was delighted with Jan Brueghal and obviously we'll plan to go to the Coolmore Coronation Cup on Derby Day - Kevin Buckley, Coolmore UK representative, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

Jan Brueghel is very tough and Ryan [Moore] gave him a class ride, but you know he doesn't surrender. He'd improved a lot from the last day, and you could see he was pricking his ears at the finish. He ran a lovely race first time back when it was only a mile and a quarter and he got beat by a good horse of Joseph's [O'Brien]. It was a bit unfair to pitch him in early over a mile and a quarter, but we just needed to get him out. He's a very brave horse and if you pass him slowly, you're in trouble. Ryan gave him an incredible ride, balanced him and got him in a lovely rhythm, and you can see him starting to come from a long way out. Everyone knew before the race that it was going to be a good gallop, and Wayne [Lordan, on Continuous] was there to make sure it was a good gallop. All anyone wanted was for it to be a solidly run, evenly run race, and then we'd see. Then we'd know after the race what to do next, what distance to go for next time, what to not do. The worst thing is when you come out of a race and you say, 'But if they'd gone a good pace, then?' that's a problem for everybody. He's a very good tough horse who was unbeaten last year, and he'd still be unbeaten if I hadn't run him too early at The Curragh this year. - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Jan Brueghel stays this trip very well and he's an uncomplicated horse. Aidan had him, as he always does, in unbelievable shape. He showed a great attitude. The second horse is a very talented horse and I am sure he'll win a big race soon. The ground, being just on the slower side of good, suited him and he stayed on really well - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred St Leger Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: We knew the track would suit and the trip would suit. I think Jan Brueghel showed he's successful going that extra distance and I think he's a Gold Cup horse in the making. Don't be surprised if he steps up a bit next year, But he has a bit of class and he's done that really well - Sean Levey, rider.

Jan Brueghel was very green. I didn't really want to make the running because he was a bit raw. The horse in front stopped and I was kind of left there and he was waiting. It was a difficult track for him and he's carried a penalty too, so you'd have to be happy with what he's done. He'll get better still. There's definitely more class in there, you've just got to get it out of him - Ryan Moore, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai International Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: We were worried about the ground for Jan Brueghel. We knew he had improved a lot from the last day and that he'd stay further but we weren't sure about the ground. You could see him changing legs when he turned in. He will stay much further and will be very happy going a mile and a half. We were thinking of coming here and then on to Goodwood and then going to the Leger - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: McDonnells Bar Newbridge Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.notes: Jan Brueghel just wasn't straightforward to train, he took a bit of time, he's a big horse. He's probably a fair horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He could go back to the Coronation Cup again, having won it last season, and he'd have a run before it. Obviously the Coronation Cup has a different look to it this year, up a lot in prize-money, so we'll see how he gets on. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: That was a great run. I'm very pleased. Obviously the winner was impressive. Jasour just switched leads right before the line, which might have cost us second, but he's run a blinder. I'm thrilled he's going the right way. I think we are close enough to warrant a kick at the July Cup, a race in which three-year-olds have done really well in the past. That would be my first thoughts as they cross the line, and as long as he comes back ok from here, he's a horse who deserves to be in the top flight - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Commonwealth Cup Trial Stakes (Group 3) (Registered As The Pavilion Stakes)
quotes.notes: Jasour was class last year in the July Stakes, then in the Morny they split and he was in the middle and just went too free. I think he got a little bit frightened as a juvenile, so we've worked and worked and he had some precious turnout up until Christmas at home. The whole team has worked really hard to be sure that we've kept him right and Jim [Crowley, jockey] seemed to really strike a chord with him in the July Stakes, so I'm just pleased the whole plan has come off. I was a little worried the ground would be too easy for him, but that didn't seem to be a problem. The Commonwealth Cup is absolutely the plan, and the Sandy Lane would be nice. We're looking forward to seeing him on a better surface and Jim has given him a super confidence-building ride. Winning was a super bonus I wasn't entirely sure would happen - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Kingdom Of Bahrain July Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: It's the first time I'd ridden Jasour but riding him from off the pace has been the key to him - Jim Crowley, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's won at the track and was third in last year's Commonwealth Cup. He was only sixth on his reappearance at Haydock but he didn't have a great lead-up with a bruised foot and he was a little bit fresh, so I'd hope he can take a big step forward from that. 10-06-25

Right from day one he looked a little bit special. His homework suggested he was good enough to win on his debut, but he was a little unlucky there as he went down by a neck having jumped the road at Salisbury. He won next time out at Nottingham, again over 5f, but I thought he was crying out for an extra furlong on that occasion. He could have gone to Royal Ascot but he just wasn't ready. He progressed from his win to his third run in the July Stakes at Newmarket. I was positive about his chances there and he duly obliged, running out an impressive winner. We now have to decide which route to take. I am not one to waste my owner's money on lots of fancy entries, so you can tell how much I thought of him as I had given him an entry in the Gimcrack before he ran at Newmarket. But if he went to the Gimcrack he probably could not go for the Group 1 Prix Morny which is just over a week later, but if he goes to the Richmond at Goodwood on Thursday there would be the ideal time between races. So, at the moment I'm leaning towards Glorious Goodwood, but we will see how the horse is before finalising plans. 02-08-23

quotes.notes: Sometimes certain races in the sprint division can be winnable and this looked one. When the rain came yesterday it looked like it might inconvenience some, whereas JM Jungle always turns up. If you don't put your hat in the ring, you've no chance, so we said we'd give it a go. He's much stronger this year and looked so calm before the race that I knew he was going to run his race again. They went lickety-split and Jm Jungle loves that. Earlier in the season Jason Hart said the race he'd love to ride him in was the Nunthorpe, simply because of how fast they go and how much he likes York. It looks the natural next step because he's a Group 2 winner now and you want to be going up from there. We put him in the Abbaye earlier this week and that's a similar race. If you get a good draw up against the rail, with his speed he'd be in the van early doors - Sean Quinn, joint-trainer.

JM Jungle deserved that and he's won a load of consistent races and the handicapper has never missed him for being placed, so it's great he's got his day. I rode him in the three-year-old Dash here a couple of years ago and I got stuck behind a wall of horses and I was never able to get into a rhythm that day. He never handled the track that day but today I was out on a wing and able to keep momentum rolling forward and I think that has helped - Jason Hart, jockey.

When the draw came out and the ground was dry we were delighted. This was the plan all along, but Jm Jungle will roll away in all the big five-furlong handicap sprints for the rest of the year - John Quinn, joint-trainer.

JM Jungle is in very good form, and up to Haydock he had been running really well and just got touched off at York and Hamilton. Then he won nicely at Haydock. He's got a lot of speed from the gate, so we felt that this track would suit him - John Quinn, trainer.

JM Jungle has been running consistently and I thought he was unlucky to bump into a well-handicapped horse last time. He went to bite the second horse and I had to drag him back off, but he's done it well in the end - Jason Hart, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's another who did well in Bahrain and he arrived back in such good form that we decided to keep going for now, so he'll either head for the Scottish Sprint Cup at Musselburgh or a valuable race at Bath a week later. He gave Jason [Hart] a good feel on his last run in Bahrain and he could still be improving. He's an out-and-out 5f horse. 20-03-24

quotes.raceTitle: Asahi Super Dry T J Smith Stakes (Group 1) (Turf)
quotes.notes: A lot of thought has gone into it long before today. It's all sort of mapped out, we just needed Joliestar to run today to cement her place on the flight [to Britain]. She's only run in the best races right from a 3yo and she's been a model of consistency since. This preparation compared to last prep she's overcome luck in running, speed, tracks, she's become just more dominant ? maturity and confidence have been number one. She'll have a bit of downtime now and work back from Ascot. She goes so well fresh so she'll represent us all well, Australia and New Zealand -  Chris Waller, trainer.

Joliestar had done it again. She's now won Group 1s in three different states; that's an incredible feat. She's a bloody superstar. She won really well today. This year she's just jumping a little handier. It makes a big difference when you can just be fourth or fifth, rather than getting back like last year, when she had no luck with barrier draws. It can make all the difference. She's off to the TJ Smith Stakes next and then, all being well, Royal Ascot. We're going to have to go and get a top hat and tails! - Sir Brendan Lindsay, representing the owners.

quotes.raceTitle: Memberships At Ascot Paradise Stakes (Listed Race) (A Queen Anne Stakes Trial)
quotes.notes: Jonquil is a talented horse, and his record was a bit in and out last year, but the Greenham, French Guineas and Celebration Mile take some winning. He didn't win the French Guineas, but he nearly did. Hopefully we get faster ground later in the year and he can win a big one. The Lockinge would be an obvious next step. He had a tough campaign last year, so if we can get a clear run now, then hopefully he can prove he's a decent horse - Andrew Balding, trainer.

Jonquil was a bit free early but Colin did a lovely job getting him to settle. I was always fairly confident we were going to get up, but we had to pull out everything to get there. Everything is possible and [going up in trip] would change the landscape for him -  Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Emirates Poule d'Essai des Poulains (Group 1) (3yo Colts) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Jonquil was given a wonderful ride and he's done us proud. It would be frustrating to get beaten on the nod but we've got a really exciting horse and it's onwards and upwards. We feel he stays the mile but he's got a lot of speed and we might end up dropping back to seven-furlong options later down the line. At Ascot we've got a number of options. There's the Jersey Stakes, the St James's Palace Stakes and he's in the Commonwealth Cup. He's not the only horse Juddmonte have so we'll just have to see where they all fit - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Watership Down Stud Too Darn Hot Greenham Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Jonquil was a smart horse last year on his debut and although it didn't go to plan second time out, we've had plenty of time with him. His work's been great and I'm thrilled to win it. - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Sri Lanka, Jewel Of Asia British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Jonquil will have learned a lot from today. He's a nice two-year-old and he's got the pedigree and physique to back it up. They were always quite positive when they sent him from Juddmonte and he's shown a gritty attitude. It was nice to see him come back at the end. There's stamina in his pedigree but he's got that bit of speed from his dam too. Seven furlongs is okay for now, but I'm pretty sure he'd stay a mile this year if we wanted him to, and further next year. It's exciting. He's got a nice future - James Savage, assistant trainer.

quotes.notes: The problem is with William [Buick] he's that good he wins by too far! He's rode me a winner or two over the years and he's obviously a first-class jockey. It was amazing for Jordan Electrics to do what he did carrying so much weight. He's superb to train; at one time he was difficult to travel, but he's mellowing as he gets older. We'll probably come back here for the Scottish Stewards' Cup next - Jim Goldie, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: Unfortunately he picked up an injury so he's going to be off for the first half of the season, but we're thinking he'll be back and it's not career-ending. He's sound but he's going to need time to get over what happened. We'd like to win an Ayr Gold Cup, so we'll target that and possibly the Portland. That's a fickle double, it's usually one or the other. He's a grand horse. Technically at his age he's supposed to be diminishing but he doesn't seem to be. The man who feeds him rides him and he's managed very well. He's a Hamilton specialist. It's probably going to be a bit more difficult for him now, but he's thereabouts in those top sprints. 07-05-25

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: Josh's Joy is a gorgeous filly to look at; she's a big strong individual. She's probably just taken a few runs to really get together. I found that today was the first time that late on in a race she has actually found an extra gear and really picked up. If anything, I think her last furlong was her best furlong. She was well entitled to do that, she has had her three runs and she is a nice filly, so I think going on from that coming back in trip is no problem, she's got plenty of pace and I think she'll step forward again for it. She's a big filly and she probably hasn't fully come to herself yet. She is constantly getting stronger and growing into herself and I am sure she will straighten herself out as well - Gavin Ryan, jockey.

horse_profiles.owner_name: Al Shaqab Racing, Amo Racing & Valmont

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: K Sarra's pedigree says she should get a mile and a half. She was very green through the race and I'd say with a furlong and a half to go, the penny dropped. It's fair to say there was a little bit further to go, I might've got there. She's definitely going the right way and a bit more chilled out than her brother, Pride Of Arras. She has a good mind - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Win £25000 With BetMGM's Golden Goals EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: K Sarra still has a lot to learn, she was very green still. She's done everything right so far, her works been okay at home and she's bound to improve quite a bit. She's bred to be a decent filly so we will see - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She ran in the Fred Darling and has come out of the race well. She'd had only one start on the all-weather and she had been working well. She'll step up to a mile and a quarter next as we thought she might be better at middle distances. She's a sister to Pride Of Arras and they're a family who catch on quick, and she's pretty straightforward. 27-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Sports Racing Aston Park Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: I think the Fillies & Mares will be the big plan for Kalpana. We tried the Arc last year, and it didn't work out, but I don't think any horse has won three consecutive races on Champions Day, so that would be a nice target. The next stop would be something at Royal Ascot. Both the Prince of Wales's and Hardwicke will be available, and we'll decide nearer the time. If the ground were very soft, it might make the Prince of Wales's more attractive. Fitness was telling a little bit in the last half-furlong, but she looks like she's still got the appetite and desire for it, which is the most important thing. When you keep them in training as a five-year-old, you hope they still have that. She was entitled to win on ratings, but you just never know first time out. She was carrying a bit of extra condition, and she'd not run for a good while, so we're thrilled - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: It's massive and it's one of the biggest days in British racing. To be here with a filly like Kalpana is amazing. She's tough. It didn't work out for her in the Arc, but the owners are sportsmen and they said to roll the dice if Andrew [Balding, trainer] was happy. He gave us the green light on Wednesday and thank god he did - Barry Mahon, owners' racing manager.It was very important for Kalpana because she's been knocking on the door all year. Things didn't go right for her in the Arc, but Andrew and the team thought she was well so they rolled the dice. Bar the last day, she's gone down on her sword every time this year - Colin Keane, jockey.

We're disappointed not to win but the horse who beat us is very good. Kalpana is having a proper blow now, so hopefully that will put her spot on for what we're doing. We didn't want it to be a falsely run race and it wasn't, it was a nice even pace. She had every chance, a good horse has beaten her and she'll come on for the run.  We need to discuss plans. She's in the Arc and the Fillies & Mares and it's up to where the powers at be want to go. This was a prep and the Arc was always the plan, but we'll just have to see how the fields develop. She'd had a couple of easy weeks after the King George. She's a big filly now and she'll come on for that - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: I'm very proud of Kalpana and she's run her heart out again. She did nothing wrong, she had every chance but was just beaten by a quick one on the day. I'd have thought the step up in trip helped. It was a career-best effort and we'll be working back from Paris in October. She's a class act and she's tightened up since her two runs this season. She's come on again and we're excited by the autumn. She hasn't won a race this year so she has no penalty, so going to the September Stakes could be an option. It's on our doorstep and you're guaranteed the surface. She won it last year and it's possible, but if the Prix Vermeille looked a good shot then it's a Group 1 at the end of the day. There's an extra week from that and the Arc this year so anything is possible  - Andrew Balding, trainer.It was a huge run and we're over the moon with Kalpana. She's a very good filly and although ground doesn't affect her, she's probably a little bit better on softer ground. It gives us a bit of encouragement that we could still have a big autumn with her. In the last number of years it's been on the soft side [at Longchamp], but we know she has the option of coming back here on Champions Day too. Today was her big target in the first part of the season and we'll see how she comes out of it, but hopefully there's a chance she can turn up in the Arc. She's danced every dance. She's been to Ireland and taken on Aidan O'Brien's filly [Whirl], who is very talented, and she ran her heart out in the Tatts Gold Cup. It looked like we had it at the furlong pole, but the winner is very good and he kicked into gear in the last half-furlong, and it's probably where that faster ground has caught her out a bit, but she's a great filly and she didn't lie down- Barry Mahon, owners' racing manager.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Kalpana is a wonderful filly and William Buick gave her a wonderful ride. This filly hadn't even done any fast work this time last year, so it's been a pretty steep trajectory from Wolverhampton to here. I've never known a horse improve as much. I even recall mentioning to Barry Mahon [Juddmonte racing manager] that we might put her in a sale this time last year but every time we started to do more with her, she's just improved and improved. She didn't love the ground today but she coped with it. She's such a diamond and has a very special temperament - Andrew Balding, trainer.
I still think Kalpana is a bit green and a bit raw. I think she's going to continue to improve with time and age. I'd be very excited about her and the sky's the limit - P J McDonald, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Glasgow Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I didn't really know which way the race was going to pan out. I thought there might be a few of the lads battling for the lead and we had a plan to sit in and pick the pieces up but Kalpana jumped great and I got a lovely pitch the whole way round. Once I got into the dip and I sat into her in the rising ground she stretched and galloped to the line - P J McDonald, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.
