quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Auguste Rodin Irish EBF Athasi Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: She won well back on nicer ground. I thought Kensington Lane was way too big a price today but she is a Group Three winner now. She's in the Guineas, so she'll probably go there. She has a lot of gate speed so she's one that could end up in the US, in one of those ten-furlong Grade Ones later on in the year. If she goes abroad on a turning track, a mile and a quarter will be no problem to her - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.notes: Kensington Lane been improving slowly. Her form is rock-solid. At Down Royal she had a good look when she got there and was just collared by one of Joseph O'Brien's, who has won twice since. We've always liked her and I'd say there's a little bit more improvement in her - Gavin Ryan, jockey.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

quotes.notes: The stirrup leather broke, I was without one iron and unfortunately the race was over - Oisin Murphy, jockey of Khaadem.

By reading the form, I knew they were going to go hard, and I couldn't ask for any more. For a nine-year-old gelding against the best sprinters in the world, third is quite a good job. Khaadem thinks he's two, honestly. The winner was head and shoulders above everybody else. It's a shame I couldn't catch Ag Bullet, but third is good enough. Full credit to Charlie Hills. A nine-year-old gelding getting third in a Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint against the best sprinters in the world, amazing effort. The blinkers helped and we've done a lot of gate schooling and the race went really well. The winner was far too good but I'm just delighted with the run - Frankie Dettori, jockey.

Khaadem seems to thrive being here. He's nine years old and he won his first race as a two-year-old, so we go back a long way. He's won some fantastic races back in England - two Jubilees at Royal Ascot - and he's won some amazing prize-money, so he's given us all a lot of joy. Horses have such good characters and he's certainly got one. I think we have to go [Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint]. It just makes sense - Charlie Hills, trainer, speaking to Bloodhorse.Khaadem fluffed the start. That's why he was so far back. I got him in a good spot and he decided to run. He's a character and we love him for it - Frankie Dettori, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Khaadem got a fantastic ride there off the pace and he never looked like he was going to get beat; he travelled beautifully through the race. He loves the place and it's the first time he's had the ground, pretty much since he ran here last time. I think fast ground is key to him. He had a lovely pitch, they went a good strong pace in front, but he just travels so well. He's such a versatile horse; he was making the running over five furlongs two years ago. I just really felt there's a different trajectory to running like a good horse over six, and it seems to have suited him very well - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: I've always had massive faith in Khaadem and that's why I've kept him for so long. He won a Group 2 last year over five furlongs and this year I wanted to try to race him properly again and make sure he got the six well. The horse is very, very fast. He's got his quirks but most good sprinters do and he's just taken time to come to himself - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: We were pleased with that. It was a little bit loose over on the side Khaadem was but he's run a really good race.  We'll definitely look at the Flying Five - Charlie Hills, trainer.

Khaadem has never really come back like his Stewards' Cup win until today. It's taken a while and he's a quirky horse, but very talented. He took everything in his stride and the race unfolded perfectly for him. I'm made up. He always wears his heart on his sleeve - Charlie Hills, trainer.

We only bought Khaadem at the end of last year from Shadwell and we're over the moon. These are hard races to win but he's just seriously fast. He's a proven horse and the Hays like to have runners in Dubai, so it was an easy decision to make to buy him. You'd have to go to Ascot after that and take on the rockets there and you'd have to keep him over the same trip too - Alex Cole, owner's racing manager.

I guess we will have to look at the Group 1 at Haydock. Magical Memory won this race and just got touched off there. I think Khaadem is a very good horse who is only going to get better and better - Charlie Hills, trainer.

Khaadem is hugely talented but has his quirks. He's just a bit hot-headed and has been hard to settle, hence the hood in the paddock before. I think Ascot and a stiff six will suit him. He might just prefer a little bit more give in the ground in time but he's an exciting horse - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Conditions Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.notes: Khaadem is a lovely horse - he's got size and scope. One of the reasons for bringing him here was we wanted to go softly with him, try to give him more experience until we move him up to the bigger races. He's in the Middle Park and Sheikh Hamdan will probably decide where he wants to go, but there's a good possibility he'll go there - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Randox Health EBF Novice Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.notes: Khaadem got struck into when he ran here last time and has grown up a lot since then - Dane O'Neill, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He needed his return at York and was drawn on the wrong side. He looks a picture of health and seems in just as good a form going there as he did last year when he won the same race. He enjoys being ridden a bit differently from time to time and came from the back last year but he's undoubtedly a fast horse, who has won a King George over five furlongs at Goodwood in the past. 13-06-24

He wintered in Dubai and I was delighted with his first run back here when third in the Listed Cathedral Stakes at Salisbury late last month. We rode him a little differently there as he was held up to come with a late run, which I think suited him. He has an entry in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes on Saturday, and I'm currently wanting to give it a go. Glorious Goodwood will again be on our radar as he has a real liking for the course having won the Stewards' Cup and King George. 21-06-23

quotes.raceTitle: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (Smullen Series)
quotes.notes: She had a lovely run first time out and most of her owners are in England so we decided to run Killashee Warrior at Leopardstown on Champions Day. We let her have a crack at the Ingabelle, where she flew, and she did what she should do today. The ground was too deep to risk her on at the Curragh last week and I don't think she was in love with today's track and while the ground was lovely, it can be trappy. We've always had an eye on a three-year-old campaign with her and she has earned her break, so we'll see what next year brings - Eddie Harty, trainer.

quotes.notes: I was pleased with Kind Of Blue. That was his first run back and we've had a clear run with him this spring, whereas last year was really messy. He was really well behaved too. He'll go to Ascot if he's in one piece and he'll improve fitness-wise - James Fanshawe, trainer.
Kind Of Blue ran really well and I am just really pleased to see him run well again. He loves it at Ascot so we look forward to going back there again with him - James Fanshawe, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco British Champions Sprint Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Kind Of Blue was unraced before the start of this season but has made giant strides and run some cracking races in defeat. He's improved with every race and there's no greater man than James Fanshawe to prepare a Champions Sprint winner here - he knows what he needs - James Doyle, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfair Sprint Cup Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: It was a great run, I'm very pleased with Kind Of Blue. It looked like at the furlong pole we were going really well, but he's run a great race. He's come a long way and I think the bit easier ground helped him. He's getting the hang of it, he's a very exciting horse to have in the yard and I'd say there's a good chance we'll go to Ascot [on Champions Day] - James Fanshawe, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet/British EBF Conditions Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: I've been lucky enough to sit on King's Trail a couple of times at home and he was impressive when he won here the first time. It was a very messy race and he'll have learned plenty from the first couple of furlongs. He's straightforward and has a great mind for a Sea The Stars. I had to wake him up a little to get a position, but you couldn't fault his attitude at all. He's done nothing wrong and I'm sure he'll have a few stiffer targets now - Billy Loughnane, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Make The Move To Midnite Handicap
quotes.notes: That was all very smooth. Billy [Loughnane] always thought Knebworth was going to win. He hit the two-furlong pole, quickened and went away. That's his ninth win for us and we hope he'll go to Doncaster for the Lincoln meeting - Derrick Blake, part-owner.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a great old warrior who ran well to finish third at Doncaster on Sunday. The softer it is the better his chances are. He'll be ready to go again soon. 18-09-24

quotes.notes: Komorebi ran super. From stall nine it's a slightly awkward draw and he's not the quickest early. We had a nice run around, the pace wasn't very fast and the winner was in the box seat. He felt like he'd improve again. He'd probably prefer better ground and we'll see what Mr Fabre wants to do, but he potentially could get further - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet Ayr Gold Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.notes: Korker seemed to get away reasonably well, he was tracking the pace and he finished strongly - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Sri Lanka, The Jewel Of Asia Handicap
quotes.notes: Korker was very good and he especially jumped the gates nicely. He was very relaxed at the start and he picked them off. He bumped into a horse rated 111 at Ascot [Emaraaty Ana] and wasn't far behind him. His last three runs have been very good and he's been frustrating at the gates before, but he's really come on. He's grown up now. He's got a bit of a confidence booster now and after speaking to the boss that might be it for the year, so he'd be ending it on a high - Clifford Lee, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Eddie And Violet Smith Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Korker has been so unlucky as he keeps missing the break and deserves his win. I've ridden him loads and when he doesn't miss the break, he never actually races through, but when you miss it slightly he hits the frame. He didn't miss it today, but we couldn't get into stride in the first furlong. I thought we were going to get lapped but he really got me back into it - Clifford Lee, jockey.
Korker was very relaxed for a sprinter. He'll go for the Holyroodhouse Handicap at Royal Ascot.

quotes.raceTitle: Lee Thomas Christy Memorial Nursery Handicap
quotes.notes: Korber is a little bit quirky in the stalls, hence he goes in last with the hood on, but he jumped reasonably quickly and had a nice smooth run. He's a high-class horse, who we've thrown in the deep end, and he's proved he's got a lot of ability. We'll see what Listed races are around for him and I'm sure he'll be a lovely horse next year - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He came back a little bit tight from his last run at Hamilton but we should be able to get him back for the Wokingham. He can be a bit slowly away but Jack Nicholls seems to get a good tune out of him and we'll stick with him. It's a good opportunity for Jack to ride in a race like that.   12-06-25

A horse I have a lot of time for. He was most unfortunate not to win on his debut at York last year when missing the break, giving up several lengths and only going down by a head. He has not done a lot wrong since, winning three times as a juvenile and ending up the season on a mark of 92. On his second run this season at York last time he defied top weight with an impressive win over 5f, but the handicapper has really hammered him hard with a 9lb rise. He was going for the Holyroodhouse after that but it will be tough now off 104. We will still head to the royal meeting and see how that pans out, but off his new mark we will have to start looking at Listed and Group 3 races for him. I think there is more to come - I certainly hope so after such a sharp hike in his mark. 01-06-22

quotes.notes: I ran Lady Iman over six [furlongs in the Airlie Stud] when my jockey kept telling me she was five. She arrived up on Ryan's [Moore] outside at the furlong pole in that race at the Curragh, it was the first time I went 'wow' with her and then he [Moore] outgalloped her. I was down that day, a bit upset with myself for that. From day one she's had a temperament to die for and my job has been to feed her and not get in her way. She has two-year-old written all over her and it looks like Roger [O'Callaghan, owner's son] will get his own way for the Nunthorpe and Ger will get his own way for the Breeders' Cup!  - Ger Lyons, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

It was a proper horse race. I love races like that. Aidan [O'Brien] and Ryan decided that they knew they wanted 7f and they were going to run the speed out of Lady Iman. We loved up to win the race at the furlong pole and I thought if she wins from here she's a very good horse but the winner outstayed me, it is as simple as that. Colin has been telling me for some time that we are a speed horse and that 5f would be her best trip. I think I am disappointed to lose but pleased to have learned something but if you take the winner out of it she got 6f well. I was talking to the owners and we are going to look at 5f. That would be more up her street at the minute. We will try toi fill in the spaces between now and the end of the season. I did float the idea that she could be a Breeder's Cup filly going for 5f like we did last year but that's for down the road - Ger Lyons, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Stud Irish EBF Blackbeard Fillies Sprint Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.notes: Lady Iman came to me with a reputation and she's done everything easy. Colin said she gets to the front and she idles, which is lovely. I asked the question where to now and Colin said wherever you want. We'll sit down with Tony and Roger (O'Callaghan), it's all about the sire and doing the right thing by the filly going forward. You don't rule anything in or out. There are plenty of nice races here. People have to put guns to my head to get over there (Ascot). I'll do whatever I'm asked to do by the owners but at this moment in time we'll sit back. She had Queen Mary written all over her but it's not the be all and end all. She's doing everything easy so we'll keep taking it and keep taking what I can at two. Who knows, she could be the next filly to win a Phoenix - Ger Lyons, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Holden Plant Rentals First Flier Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Lady Iman is a lovely filly. Colin [Keane, rider] was very impressed with her. He said she has plenty of speed. I'm thinking of Naas [Group 3 Juvenile Fillies Sprint Stakes] next. I'll sleep on it and talk to Colin, but I've no problem with her getting six furlongs, but she has plenty of speed and will learn plenty from that. I've never taken this filly off the bridle, so I don't know her limit - Ger Lyons, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: She's a nice filly, Lady Iman was plenty green when we got there and had a good look the whole way up the straight. You would imagine she would appreciate an extra furlong, she handles a good surface and ticks a lot of boxes. She was very professional from the moment she walked into the yard - Colin Keane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.notes: Lady Lilac is improving and with another year under her belt she will be a nice filly - Joseph Murphy, trainer.

quotes.notes: It was strong form from Leicester, obviously Lady Roisia was entitled to take a nice step forward. She moved into contention well here today. I thought she would go and kick clear but just showed a bit of greenness inside the furlong. She just rolled around a little bit, so she's value for a little bit more. She's looking at the big screen on the inside and she was left alone out in front with just over two to run, so she's done well - Hector Crouch, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: The first of Talent's offspring I've trained and she was also the first two-year-old winner for her dam. Obviously, I have a soft spot for her, but she's training well and will  go for a trial, maybe at Chester. 27-04-26

She was having a good look around but once I got serious with her she knuckled down and asserted. She's won in different circumstances and she's going to improve - Hector Crouch, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Pertemps Network Spring Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Last year you questioned whether Lake Forest was fully concentrating on the job in hand and since he's been gelded he's moving better and everything just seems easier. His mind is more focused on being a racehorse. He's only small but he's got a lot of ability - Maureen Haggas, trainer's wife.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: Lake Forest just ran awfully at Newmarket. He was in a state beforehand, he was upset, he was stupid to post and he was edgy in the stalls. Today he was really calm and really good going down. We saddled him in the stables and walked him across. He'd run a very good race in the July Stakes. We'd always planned to come here and his race last time nearly put us all off but why not have a go? You couldn't fancy him really although I said to my son I thought he'd run well. I think he'll get further. Tom said he went too early today - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Jewson St Helens EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Lake Forest is a sweet horse who's been fat and lazy all winter and suddenly came to hand three weeks ago. When Tom asked him to pick the bridle up, he went whoosh. He's got a good character and a nice attitude - Maureen Haggas, assistant trainer.

horse_profiles.owner_name: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

quotes.notes: Lambourn won the Vase here last year and won two Derbies. He was trained for the Leger after but didn't stay that day. It was nice to bring him back here though hard bringing him back that far in distance. He was a little bit rusty but he kept finding and he'll improve from today and we can look forward to the rest of the year with him - Ryan Moore, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.Lambourn didn't make it easy for Ryan at stages and he hit the rail just round the bend. But Ryan always knew he had all bases covered. The concern was the drop in trip but he's been here before - and from the crowd and the atmosphere it was great to see a dual Derby winner here. Obviously he'll get stepped up in trip next time and is likely to be targeting the Coronation  Cup, that would be the natural next step - Kevin Buckley, Coolmore UK representative.

Lambourn is a straightforward horse, we know his running style, he's behind the bit. He travelled sweetly today and we were in a lovely rhythm all the way down the back and I started to pick it up. Things were going well but Tom was always there breathing down my neck and I didn't feel like I went through the two pole as well as I'd like to. He just kind of stayed on so there's a question mark over whether he actually stayed the trip or not - Sean Levey, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: They went very slow. Lambourn is a high-tempo, mile-and-a-half horse. Everything was perfect with him; we wanted to get a racecourse run or gallop in him before the Leger or the Arc. The race was kind of a mess really. It was a hack around to halfway, then a sprint up the stretch - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Lambourn is just so laid-back, I can't tell you. Ryan gave him a lovely, uncomplicated, straightforward ride. He knew him to a tee from winning on him at Chester and everything Wayne [Lordan] told him. He's so relaxed, and the horse coming with him [Sir Dinadan] was only going to help him, and you can see he was pricking his ears all the way up the straight. I knew Ryan would be very happy about that as he would have been delighted to have company and would love to get into a battle. He has that personality, that attitude, it's like everything in life when sports people have that attitude and he's that straightforward, genuine and just does whatever you want for you, whenever he can. He's like his dad, if you put him in first gear, he stays in first gear; if you put him in third gear, he'll stay in third gear. He's not influenced by anything around him, but always wants to please and never overdo himself. He could be a King George or an Arc type of horse. The way he races, I'd imagine he'd race that way regardless of the trip. You'd imagine he'd get further but he has lots of class - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred Derby (In Honour Of His Highness Aga Khan IV) (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.notes: Australia [Lambourn's sire] is a great Derby winner, very genuine, and that's what Lambourn is - uncomplicated, genuine and committed. He always has been. His runs this year have been very good - he was second to Delacroix, and then was very impressive in Chester. Chester again - you have to be on your game and you have to stay, and that's the way he was. Ryan loved him in Chester and he obviously can't ride them all. He was always going to be an Irish Derby horse, a Leger horse, and Wayne said he definitely would stay further. He saves plenty for himself and he gives himself a chance to get any trip - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Lambourn looked a thorough stayer and while he was a little on and off the bridle, once the penny dropped he came home really strongly. He got the trip really well and he's gone through the line nicely. We'll just have to see how they all get on in the trials but we were thinking of sending him to Epsom as they learn so much when they go to Chester - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He had a brilliant three-year-old season, winning the Derby and Irish Derby. We're very happy with him and we're going to train him for the Coronation Cup. The plan is to have a run before it, potentially in the Mooresbridge [May 4, Curragh]. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: I was concerned passing the seven furlong marker and saw William [Buick] just crouching a bit lower and at no point during the race bar the line did I think Lazy Griff was going to finished where he did, which makes it all the more amazing a performance. He was probably feeling the ground at every stage, which only underlines what an unbelievably tough horse he is. Good to soft ground at Donny in September, we're looking forward to it! - Charlie Johnston, trainer, speaking on Racing TV the following day.

quotes.raceTitle: Betfred Derby (In Honour Of His Highness Aga Khan IV) (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.notes: That's a fantastic run. I didn't think Lazy Griff would love the track. I thought he'd be better in Ireland or at Doncaster as he's quite a heavy-topped horse, to the extent we felt if the ground wasn't as soft as it was he wouldn't be here. Maybe we were in the right place, but he's tough, he's honest, and he's going to give his owners a lot of fun - Charlie Johnston, trainer.Lazy Griff did everything perfectly. He was a little bit nervous in the paddock but down to the start he was well behaved and moving really well. This kind of track suits him and when I came downhill with Mickael [Barzalona, on Midak] I told him there was nobody able to follow us, we were cruising. The horse in front was so lazy in the turn I thought he would stop at a point, but he never gave up and went to the end. I'm so proud of my horse. It's a great run and it's the same form as the Chester Vase. He would be able to make the German Derby, but I just spoke to the trainer who was asking me if he could go in the St Leger. I think that can also be an option, he stays really well. We'll just see how he comes back from this race - Christophe Soumillon, rider.

That was fantastic, especially as Lazy Griff missed a piece of work about a week ago and for a short while it was touch and go if we'd get here. I'm sure we can get him better as he was only 80 per cent fit. That certainly bodes well for going forward and Joe said he appreciated the juice in the ground. We'd be a bit hesitant about very fast ground in the future, but he's in English, Irish and German Derbys and you'll certainly see him in one of them. With a syndicate like this, there's one Classic they're dreaming of, but I might be thinking of a different one. He's a very smart horse - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I stood in the paddock after the Chester Vase last season and said this horse will win the St Leger. Nothing that happened in the interim dented that confidence, so it was very disappointing to run out of road at the most crucial time. He had surgery on his knee in September and was out of action until Christmas, but he came back into work in the first week in January and he's been back cantering since the middle of February. If everything goes perfectly he could be ready in time for the Ormonde Stakes, which should give us a good idea whether we should be campaigning him in Cup races or races like the Coronation Cup and King George. Ideally, he'll run with some cut in the ground, and something like the Irish St Leger looks tailor-made for him later in the year. 21-04-26

quotes.notes: James [Doyle] was telling us that if there was only one group then maybe he would have won. But he was kind of on his own and it wasn't easy to manage his effort. He battled hard and we saw the real Lazzat today, but it wasn't ideal because the horses were spread about on the track. That's racing but he's a really tough horse and I'd think he's the best sprinter in Europe this year. We'll have a bit of a break now and prep him for early next season. There's a few options on the international stage like Saudi Arabia and the Al Quoz Sprint in Dubai, because there's not much going on in the first couple of months of the season in Europe, but we'll see what connections want to do - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

It was too sharp for Lazzat. It was my fear because he likes to be in front and at the three-furlong marker, he was already asking him to keep up. He stayed on well, he was fighting and he wasn't beaten far. Hopefully, next month there will be a bit more cut in the ground for the Champions Sprint over six furlongs or the Prix Foret over seven furlongs - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: ARC Prix Maurice de Gheest - Fonds Europeen de l'Elevage (Group 1) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: The feeling of James [Doyle] on board was that Lazzat was a little bit too fresh. He burst out of the stalls with too many revs, whereas at Ascot he pointed his ears and breathed very well. This time he [Doyle] didn't feel completely in control and he felt the horse used up too much gas. That's why he hit a flat spot before responding well to hang on to second. I always felt Sajir was the horse to fear at Royal Ascot but, of course, he was withdrawn at the start. When he was withdrawn I felt that was one of the toughest parts of the opposition out of the way, because on fast ground he's a really good horse. Lazzat goes on soft ground and we can look forward to the Champions Sprint at Ascot. We'll have to choose between the Sprint Cup at Haydock, which is at the midpoint between here and Ascot, and the Prix de la Foret over Arc weekend, which is sponsored by Qatar and where they focus on having plenty of runners  - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

Lazzat has got a really high cruising speed, and James [Doyle, jockey] didn't know what to expect because he didn't know him. I told him, you know how you won the first race today? Just do the same. He rode him with plenty of confidence. He could be the best sprinter in Europe, and maybe in the world one day. I saw all the races from the Japanese horse and he is a late challenger, so I thought it was going to be tough to respond to him, because I didn't know how much petrol he would have left, but he was on top of it today. Physically and mentally with all the experience he has got travelling all over the place, he has matured - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

When Lazzat won the Maurice de Gheest [over six-and-a-half furlongs] it was his best performance at three, and it was also the shortest trip he ran over. After that we had a go at the Golden Eagle over 1,500 metres [seven-and-a-half furlongs] and although he was under pressure the whole way and it was probably a bit far, he was only beaten in the final stride. We know he's a very good 'flyer' but there are not many opportunities over seven furlongs, so we'll specialise at this trip where there is a real programme for him to follow. He could go straight to Royal Ascot for the Jubilee and then we'd think about races like the July Cup, the Maurice de Gheest and the Haydock Sprint Cup. The only race over further I'd be tempted by now would be the Breeders' Cup Mile - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: ARC Prix Maurice de Gheest (Group 1) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: That's just incredible. I was hoping he'd be able to keep a lid on him as long as possible, but Lazzat has just taken lengths out of them. We've tried to keep him to easier targets for as long as possible, but he was physically magnificent before the race and his training has been excellent. He's entered in the Prix de la Foret, but we're also very tempted by the Golden Eagle in Australia, which is a race that is made to measure for him. We'll see how he comes out of this but the most important thing is to space his races out - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

I'm not sure I learned a lot because I know Lazzat has a lot of natural speed and that's why I didn't want to step him up past 1,400 metres [seven furlongs]. He'll now go for either the Prix Paul du Moussac or the Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot; I really want to keep him in that rhythm. I'd love him to get a lead one day but you can't restrain him or allow the race to unfold at a false pace. It's fine making all but I think we'll have to consider running a pacemaker for him at some stage. He was looking around a bit there but I think he'll improve in terms of maturity with time and racing - Jerome Reynier, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran an extremely fast time at Chantilly and one of those in behind him [James's Delight] won a Group 2 at the Curragh next time out. He needed to win that day to show he belonged among the best sprinters in Europe, and he's been in very good form ever since. He's won the Maurice de Gheest over 1,300 metres [six and a half furlongs], so I see him as a 'flyer' as much as a pure sprinter, and so the stiff track at Ascot should play to his strengths. 11-06-25

quotes.notes: I think it was a very good trial and I liked the way Legacy Link fought her way back and galloped out strongly. Colin [Keane] feels she should go to Epsom. I mentioned the Prix Diane before but all being well we'll go to Epsom. She's got a great mind on her but she was short of match practice. I'd like to have got a run into her earlier but there was nowhere to go - John Gosden, joint-trainer.For the first half Legacy Link was a little bit fresh and gassy and we went along on the wrong lead for the first half. When she got to the front she was a little bit starstruck but, when Kieran's [Shoemark] filly came to her and didn't get away, I always thought we'd outstay her. I'd imagine she'd come on a lot from today. It's obviously a completely different test again [at Epsom] but there's no better man [John Gosden] to get her ready on the day and I think she'll appreciate going a mile and a half - Colin Keane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

She just got shuffled back a bit further than he'd have liked. When he tried to get a run he couldn't and she more or less finished on the bridle. She'd been working very powerfully at home before that and, as disappointing as it was to get beaten at Haydock, it was a perfect prep for a step up to six furlongs at Ascot. She's come out of it really well and that looks like the way to ride her over six.  12-06-25

I'm not sure we need to be in a tearing hurry to go up in trip, but it's there if we need it. If you do too much too soon, you could ruin them. It's a long old year and why can't she be a nice four-year-old as well? She's a lovely, big filly and is nice enough to look after.  There aren't many options for her next run, they're all difficult. I didn't expect her to do it that way but she broke well and controlled the race ears pricked and I had a nice freebie. I went steady and built it up, I knew she had a turn of foot  so I didn't want to go too quick as I though she could use it late on and she battled to the line. She'll learn plenty today without having a hard race - Cieren Fallon, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.notes: I put a question mark next to the Prix d'Ispahan at Longchamp in three weeks, and I wanted to ask Alex Cole [racing manager for owners Jim and Fitri Hay]. He rang me yesterday and asked if I'd gone nuts, but I said 'let's just wait and see what happens at the weekend'. It's still a massive ask, but we've got a good horse and Linwood is probably out of handicaps now - Richard Hannon, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: This is renowned as an undulating track, I wanted to go forward but I'd have had to fight for it so I took the realistic option to follow. Linwood had to learn today and he did. I always felt like he was going to win. There was that tricky moment where he had to get himself in order and go through that gap. He gave me a great feel, he has a great mentality so fingers crossed he can build on today- Sean Levey, Jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He won a handicap by five and a half lengths at Newmarket last November and went up 10lb for that, but I thought before Saturday's Spring Cup that he was a Group horse in the making and he showed that was the case by leading all the way under a big weight. He had a flat period last year, when I thought we might have over-egged how good he was, but he's looking now like he's everything we hoped for. 21-04-26

quotes.notes: I haven't really seen the race. I was at the stalls, and then I only saw them head on. I heard Maltese Cross have his name mentioned, so I know he was going to be close at least. It's great to win. We were a little underwhelmed at Newbury, he didn't really look perfect but today was better. They drew clear of the third too, which is a good sign. He likes a battle. If he's fit and well, he'll go to Epsom - William Haggas, trainer.Maltese Cross was an extremely exciting horse for us over the winter and we expected a lot from him at Newbury, but it actually left a few questions to be answered as he didn't win by far. He impressed me today. He didn't win by far but he's showing more of his racing style. He had to roll his sleeves up and is extremely exciting. He'll relish the Derby trip and the track won't be a problem. He's every bit ready to go for Epsom - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Hunters Prestige British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: I liked the way he stayed on up the hill. Maltese Cross wants a mile and a half really but I'm never too keen to run them too far at two. We'll probably leave him now as he's a nice horse for next year. I think he'll learn a lot from that and he liked the ground, so we'll aim him at a race in the spring and see where we are. We think he's a nice prospect - William Haggas, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's a lovely filly and we're surprised she hasn't broken her maiden yet. Hopefully she can do so soon and she'll be going over a mile and a half. We've always thought an awful lot of her and she's got a lovely pedigree. 27-04-26

quotes.notes: Mgheera is a good sprinter and it's very exciting. We've got plenty of work into her, but she's always slowly away and that certainly wouldn't be a problem at Ascot. It should really suit her, especially that stiff five furlongs from being held up. There's a chance she might ship down to Australia after Ascot but we will have to persuade the owners to stay a bit longer as she would have a real chance in a Nunthorpe - Ed Walker, trainer.

It's quick ground out there and Mgheera loved it. Tom Marquand rode her at home and told me not to worry, she's got the action of a real fast-ground filly. Oisin [Murphy, jockey] nailed it. I was worried she was stuck behind [fourth home] Keran and that she wasn't going anywhere, but he wheeled out and got a lovely clean trip - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's in great nick and has done everything right since joining us from France for this season, winning at Longchamp and then in the Temple Stakes. I'm really excited to see her step up in grade. She'll have to improve again but you wouldn't rule it out. 10-06-25

She stays in training and we have three shots with her before she retires to Australia. She'll follow the same campaign as last year in the Prix de Saint-Georges and Temple Stakes - both of which she won in 2025 - before the King Charles III at Royal Ascot. She seems as good as ever, if not better, and I'm sure we can make those races count. 22-04-26

She did well last year, although her season ended up a little frustratingly, so we're going to go back to basics and start her off in the Commonwealth Cup Trial at Ascot. She has loads of speed. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: I'd expect Military Code to improve and it'll be interesting to see where he goes next, whether it's over five or six furlongs. He's got plenty of speed for five furlongs, but I do think he will stay six - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: We came here with a bit of confidence, although he went on the drift in the market, which is probably just been the week we've had. Military Code had done some nice work, as a physical specimen you can't fault him and we've got a couple of two-year-olds around him that we like as well so hopefully they're a little group who will come along together. He was a bit green at the start but he's done it professionally and picked up well. We'd hoped he'd be an Ascot type - Charlie Appleby, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.notes: It was easy to know what happened. They jumped and went for three furlongs and Ryan [Moore] made that decision when they were going that he was going to take his time on Minnie Hauk. That was the right thing to do but then the pace went out of the race so Ryan ended up in a slowly run mile and a quarter on a mile and a half filly and he had no chance then. With her, you'd want an end-to-end mile and a quarter at the top level for her to come into her best. She'll leave that run well behind her I'd imagine and, if we did go to Royal Ascot [for the Prince of Wales's] she'd be going forward and there'd be no taking back - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Clem Murphy Memorial Irish EBF Mooresbridge Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.notes: You'd be delighted with that. We wanted a nice, even pace so Minnie Hauk could get back into gear a little bit. We didn't want a dawdle, so it was lovely for her. She travelled with all the zest she did last year and won very snugly. You couldn't be happier with her and Ryan was very happy. He said he just let her point her toe a bit the last furlong. The Tattersalls Gold Cup is the plan, and that was the perfect prep for it. If the Tattersalls Gold Cup went well, she could go to Ascot for the Prince of Wales's. We were thinking of keeping her at a mile and a quarter for her first three runs - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

They just went very fast and Minnie Hauk just got trapped out a little bit. I think she'll stay [in training] next year - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Minnie Hauk never really settled, and when I asked her to take some blows, she never took it. So I think she just over-raced today - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Minnie Hauk ran a great race. We're delighted with her. We'll get her home and see how she is and make a decision [on her participation at the Breeders' Cup] - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.We're very proud of Minnie Hauk she just got caught. She's run a blinder. I thought she'd won and I'm sure she's got a great future, and I look forward to her running many more times - Michael Tabor, co-owner.Minnie Hauk is a big galloper and she took the front so easily. When she came on the bit I thought, 'Now it's time to go', and we are going to win easy, but I was squeezing her to keep going. If you take Daryz out, she would be one of the most impressive fillies to win the Arc, but that is racing. Sometimes you just have to accept you get beaten by another one - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

Minnie Hauk cruises and she's a lovely mover, and obviously the Arc and the Breeders' Cup Turf are there for her. A lot of people have done a lot to look after her, so I appreciate everyone's hard work and I'm delighted. Ryan gave her a class ride and he was very cool on her. She's classy and it was a very confident ride. It wasn't going to be a micky mouse race, they were going to go an even gallop without going crazy. It's up to the lads. Ryan said possibly the Arc for Whirl and the Breeders' Cup for this filly depending on ground. Whirl, as we saw at Goodwood, handles soft ground, but she handles the other ground as well. Minnie Hauk has run on soft ground, but we always thought the quicker the ground the better she'd be, and she skipped over that. She has a lot of options, but the better the race the better she'll be - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking to ITV Racing.

The boss [John Magnier] said he asked Ryan where to go with Minnie Hauk and he said she could go to the Yorkshire Oaks and the boss said what about giving her a break and train her for the Vermeille to give her a French prep for the Arc. So all those things are open.  I think she can do either those things but if she was going down the Arc trial route, she'd have to have a couple of easy weeks and obviously if she was going to York then she wouldn't have those couple easy weeks. She had a very easy race today as the tempo wasn't strong so she should come out of it well. I'd imagine we'd have a fair idea in the next week. Looking at her, she probably would love York - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

I'm delighted with Minnie Hauk. She's very classy and Ryan gave her a beautiful ride. He loved her the last day [at Chester] and then again today, so she's very exciting. She's obviously learning - she went to Chester and learnt a lot and was still green, and she was always improving from mid-race. What you love about her is that she's a great traveller; she has a lot of class. Ryan felt he was going very easily today on her and usually what that means is that she will be able to step up a couple of grades into even higher-class races. It's lovely for the lads and for everyone to have another filly like that. - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Minnie Hauk is still learning a little bit. Aidan had a lot of faith in her. She travelled around strongly and I got to her quite easy, and then she was a little green in front. When the other filly came back she went on again. She's a talented filly and she stayed on well. I'm very happy with her and hopefully she'll build on this - Ryan Moore, jockey.

That [the Oaks] is the plan. Aidan always thought Minnie Hauk would improve a lot for this run. She's a very kind, uncomplicated filly with a great attitude. The step up in trip obviously helped and you'd be thinking of the Oaks. Ryan was niggling away just to get her interested, but she's kind and always answers to the jockey and she just kept on finding. Ryan was quite sweet on her - Paul Smith, representative of Coolmore, owners.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She had a fantastic season last year, winning the Oaks, Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks before her second in the Arc, which was a great run. Maybe with the benefit of hindsight we should have finished up with her after that and left her alone, because she was only a three-year-old filly. There's no doubt she's stronger this year - she's twice as wide and we couldn't have been happier with her at the Curragh on Sunday morning, she came up in front. She seems in great form. She'll probably be trained for the Tattersalls Gold Cup and could go to the Mooresbridge on the way. Then she might go to Ascot for the Prince of Wales's Stakes as we think she might be the one of ours best suited to it. She could then go back up to a mile and a half and could definitely end up in the Arc again, but it's going to depend on how the three-year-olds fare as well. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet Thirsk Hunt Cup Handicap
quotes.notes: That was perfect, although Mirsky probably travelled too well into the race. I didn't want to get there that early, but I didn't want to let him down either. Thankfully, he's a willing companion and kept sticking his head out. He had a nice run at Musselburgh and probably tightened up for it. He's a good early summer horse as he comes to hand pretty quickly. He showed that last year and has done it well again today - Jockey Mark Winn, Speaking to Racing TV.

Mirsky ran well a few times last year without winning, but we always felt he had something like this in him. It maybe took us a while to get the hang of him, but he's won his last two now, which is great. The Hunt Cup would be a possibility now - David O'Meara, trainer.

Mirsky was second in the Clipper Logistics at the Ebor meeting last year but that's his first win for us. It was a long enough last furlong, he's a strong traveller and seems best ridden prominently - David O'Meara, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran some good races last year without winning and will do all the same races again. On his work at home, he looks like he'll take a step forward. 14-04-25

horse_profiles.breeder_name: Miss K Rausing & Sunderland Holding Inc

quotes.raceTitle: Jockey Club Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: When she was a two-year-old I thought she'd be our Oaks filly but she's been nothing but horrifically disappointing. Miss Alpilles finally won at Haydock and since then we always thought she wanted soft ground until Kieran Shoemark rode her at Ffos Las and said she hated soft. So we ran her on fast ground at Goodwood last time and here we are today. It's extraordinary - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She did nothing wrong on fast ground at the end of last year. She relaxes well now and stays, so she'll start in the Sagaro Stakes at Ascot. She could be a fun mare for staying races. 22-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Prix du Cercle - Don Juan Cuneo Solari (Listed Race) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Rob Hornby has built up a really good rapport with Miss Attitude and she has to be delivered late as she tends to stop when she gets to the front. We've always thought she was a very smart filly but unfortunately she's had a multitude of issues. Now I've just got to talk the owners into supplementing her for the Nunthorpe. To be honest it's a bit of a no-brainer as we've already seen this year the five-furlong division is wide open. She beat [King George Stakes winner] JM Jungle in a Listed race at York, so why wouldn't you try? - Jack Channon, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's rated 92 and wasn't beaten far at Newcastle when fourth last time. The main goal for her this year will be black type. She'll go for the Listed Lansdown Stakes at Bath on April 20 and then she'll be campaigning in stakes races for the rest of the year. 02-04-25

quotes.notes: Mission Central is rapid. Quick ground would only help because he's so fast. He travelled very well through the whole race and kept going. He's progressing lovely and the plan is to go to Royal Ascot - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Heider Family Stables Round Tower Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Mission Central learned a bit today, he had to get down and knuckle down. I'd say he's quick, five would be no problem to him, and that's slow ground. He shows a lot of pace. Wayne [Lordan] said he felt he was only hacking and the lads in the race felt they were flying; that's the sign of a speed horse. I suppose he could be a Flying Childers type of horse, he's very fast and I'd imagine that's the type of horse he is - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

We ran Mission Central in Dundalk the first day and he was a bit worse than green so that's why we gelded him. He's been perfect since and we'll go up to a Listed or Group race with him next time. He's a very quick horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He did great to win on Champions Day last year. He's a gelding, so he'll have to work for a living this year! He'll be working with Brussels and Charles Darwin and will run in the sprinting division. 31-03-26

Seven is a lovely trip for him, he is in the handicap at Leopardstown next Saturday, so we will see how he comes out of it, if not, we will find another little race for him and probably try him in stakes company from seven to a mile. He'll have a winner's penalty, but in fairness, he has good form around Leopardstown and it is a good pot so we'll see how he is - Chris Armstrong, Aidan O'Brien's stable representative.

quotes.notes: Mitbaahy had only ever won over this trip at Chester, which is a very easy six, and there were some question marks over whether he would get home. I just kept filling him up and I could feel at halfway he was coming good. He came alive at the two pole and it was just a case of getting the run out of him. He has won from the back over five furlongs before, so I knew he had the turn of foot - Jamie Spencer, rider

quotes.raceTitle: Net World Sports Queensferry Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: We put a line through his last performance at Newbury when Mitbaahy was drawn on the wrong side of the track. He'd also been on the wrong side at Haydock, while he also ran better than his finishing position at Ascot. So while his form figures weren't that flattering, his runs had been better than they looked. I think winning has opened up some more options for him going into the autumn. He's in the Sprint Cup at Haydock and I think he'll get an entry for the Champions Sprint at Ascot too - Roger Varian, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Mitbaahy is in the Abbaye, but I'm not sure if he'll go there. There is Champions Day and he's a nice horse - Roger Varian, trainer.

Mitbaahy was very good last time at Hamilton and we are starting to work him out now he is getting stronger. He is a talented horse. He won't run at Royal Ascot. He was put in that in case he didn't win here today and then we would have looked to exploit his handicap mark. The most obvious place to go is to come back here on Coral Eclipse Day for the Charge, which is over five furlongs - Roger Varian, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He came to us at the end of last year and I love how laid-back he is for a sprinter. He's straightforward to deal with and pretty bombproof really. I couldn't have been any happier with his first run for us when fourth in the Abernant, but over five furlongs at Newmarket in the Palace House they were always going a stride too quick for him. He then beat two Group 1 winners in the Greenlands Stakes last month and the stiff track at the Curragh really seemed to suit him. He clearly gets six furlongs well and the target at this stage is the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes but if the ground were to come up very soft on Tuesday, then I think we'd look at the King Charles III Stakes over five furlongs. Either way, the track will suit him and Jamie Spencer rides.

He enjoyed a good campaign in 2022 and it was great to see him back in the winner's enclosure last time when taking the Listed Queensferry Stakes at Chester in good style. He had his excuses earlier in the year and now he's back to form we could look at the Haydock Sprint Cup. He's pretty useful on his day. 25-08-23

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I was very happy with her winning reappearance. She still looked a bit green so we might look at going to Killarney for a winners' race before she steps into stakes company. 22-04-26

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She ran some good races last season and was fifth behind Precise in the Fillies' Mile. She'll go into a trial for the Guineas or Oaks. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Betfair Sprint Cup Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: I thought Unequal Love might run well but I wasn't expecting Montassib to enjoy that ground and I thought they were both drawn away from the real action. We relied on Bucanero Fuerte going forward, which he did, and Unequal Love was always travelling well, whereas Cieren [Fallon] had to get after Montassib. On softer ground they come back to him and that would suit him better, but he's the most genuine horse at home and Cieren always thinks there's more to come. The Champions Sprint was always the race I was looking forward to. You would think the race would suit him, but he'll now be one of the favourites and things are different when you're expected to win - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Jenningsbet Nun Street Newcastle Open Now Chipchase Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: I'm not sure where we'll go now, but Montassib won't go to Goodwood for the Stewards' Cup. He'd have to carry a Group-race penalty now. I think we'll stick to stakes races and go wherever we can get a bit of dig in the ground - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Cammidge Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I do believe I should have won the Ayr Gold Cup on Montassib, he reversed the form at York and he's improving all the time. He's got so much quicker - Cieren Fallon, rider.

"It's only taken us three years to find Montassib's right trip, but we got there in the end. He had a bit more luck than he did at Ayr. He really is a lovely horse and one of those nice ones to have around. He was a good two-year-old then had a problem with his heart, and had the whole three-year-old campaign off. He's still got a few miles on the clock and lots of racing left in him. There isn't much left for him unless something comes up at Doncaster, but that might be it for the year. He's definitely stepped up his last two runs" - Maureen Haggas, assistant trainer.

Montassib found the ground quick enough but I wanted to make the most of him by setting him alight two and a half furlongs out. It's nice that he could get his head back in front - Cieren Fallon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Pick Your Places Handicap
quotes.notes: I thought Montassib was certain not to cope with conditions and told everyone he'd dislike the ground, but he coped with them. Most Exceed And Excels don't like that ground, but he won nicely and I don't know what we'll do, but the Buckingham Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot would seem an obvious target - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Watch Racing TV In Stunning HD Novice Stakes
quotes.notes: It was probably as you'd have hoped from Montassib. Four-runner races can get a bit muddly but he travelled into the race and duly put his head in front. He's had a good experience, the ground is plenty quick enough and he handled that fine. It's good to have him back on the racecourse. He looks like he belongs in a Newbury or Ascot paddock and hopefully he'll be ending up at those racetracks in the near future - Tom Marquand, jockey.

A lot of credit goes to to John Hammond [racing manager to Gerard Augustin-Normand] because it wasn't my idea to run. Monteille worked well and he urged me to run. When she picked up she was really good. She really needed her comeback and she was very impressive today. We'll see how she comes out of the race but I think the owners would like to go to Ascot - Mario Baratti, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's been in good form since her win at Chantilly, though we haven't had to do a lot with her. She'll have one light canter in the middle of this week and then the partners will decide together, but Ascot remains an option. She's in the Goffs London Sale before the meeting. 11-06-25

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He looked very smart when he won at Leopardstown on his final run last year, winning a seven-furlong maiden by eight lengths. We're very happy with him and we think he could be a legitimate Epsom horse. We're not sure whether he'll start at a mile or a mile and a quarter, but we have it in our heads that he'll start in one of the trials and could be a Derby horse. We think he could get the trip, although you couldn't be sure. There's also a chance he could go to a trial at Chantilly for the French Derby. He's a horse that's a little bit under the radar. 31-03-26

quotes.notes: Moody just did enough there at 1m6f, I'll say 1m4f may be her best trip. The Munster Oaks here next month will be next - Paddy Towmey, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Noblesse Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.notes: I'm delighted for connections, Moody is the first horse I've had for them [owners]. She had two runs in France and looked to have a positive profile. She looks like a nice filly. We like these races in Cork. There's the Give Thanks and the Munster Oaks and I'd like to keep winning as many of those as I can, so we'll aim her at one of those - Paddy Twomey, trainer.

Moojed has become very professional and he was pointing his ears the whole way, and I'm delighted he's chosen this race to win for the first time. I thought he was well capable of at least being placed and he's still maturing physically, so I think there's more to come - Francis Graffard, trainer.

I thought there was a lot to be disappointed about because I hoped Moon Target would win. She was drawn wide, which I thought might help, but she got knocked about. It wasn't smooth for us. I still thought we might beat Aidan's filly a furlong out, but she kept going well. She's got a very long action so perhaps Goodwood didn't suit her as much as Newmarket. I suppose she'll run in the Fillies' Mile, and hopefully we can do better there - Sir Mark Prescott, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Moon Target won so nicely. She seems extraordinarily relaxed and doesn't do much work at home, but she's always gone very well. All the trainers often say they've got a couple better at home, well I haven't. She was just immediately the best of them and everybody was surprised when I said she can go - Sir Mark Prescott, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.Moon Target has got a really potent turn of foot. Hopefully she's a Stakes filly and has all the right attributes to go to a decent level - Luke Morris, jockey.

horse_profiles.breeder_name: Woodstock B/S Ltd & Troy Bloodstock Ltd

quotes.notes: More Thunder feels like a Group 1 horse. York will come quick, but there's a nice option in France [Foret] over seven which is a Group 1 and he might get some cut in the ground, which definitely isn't against him - Tom Marquand, jockey.

I need to watch to watch the race again but for me they didn't go fast at all and he really struggled to get momentum. I think More Thunder is better going fast Tom came in and said if we run over this trip again they'll need to go hard. He feels 6f is his best distance. I think he deserves a shot at a Group race now. We had wanted to go up to seven at some stage and today was a good opportunity. We'll have a crack at a six-furlong sprint now ? he's in everything. He only won when his head was down but this year there have been a lot of times when my head has been up and we've got beat -  William Haggas, trainer.
Delighted with the way More Thunder ran, a little frustrated with the outcome - William Haggas, trainer.

At some stage More Thunder is going to go into stakes races, but he's low enough in the handicap to be competitive [in the Wokingham]. He had three pounds less weight than he should have had today, and that would've made the difference so the handicapper shouldn't put him up too much - William Haggas, trainer.

More Thunder travelled very well and finished his race off well. Wiliam Haggas wanted to start him off over six with a view to going seven furlongs next time. He's strengthened up and has been showing more speed this year - Philip Robinson, racing manager to owner Saeed Suhail.

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs EBF Stonehenge Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: It was a good race, the second is a smart horse who ran well at Ascot last time out. Morris Dancer was finishing well at Goodwood and the step up to a mile suited him. He's still learning, it's only his fourth start, he was a bit green in front so hopefully he can take another step forward. He's not the tallest but he's got plenty of strength. He just bounced out of Goodwood and was doing all his best work late and, with the ground in good condition, we thought we'd come here. It's fantastic for his sire Palace Pier, who's going great guns. We've put him in the Champagne and could drop him back in trip. We'll see how he comes out of this and make a plan - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

We're thrilled with Morris Dancer, he's run a great race. He won at Haydock and he just had a little bit of a niggle, so we backed off. He's come here on the minimum work and he's run a great race. William [Buick] said don't be frightened stepping up to a mile, so we'll go a mile somewhere next - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Anglesey Lodge Equine Hospital Woodlands Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: We thought Moss Tucker might need the run like he's done the last couple of seasons but as Billy (Lee, jockey) said it was a very good performance off ten stone. He seemed very relaxed in the prelims, was good in the gates and just went up through the gears. Billy said he had a little blow, as you'd expect, at the half-furlong pole but he has a touch of class about him and knows his job. Hopefully he might be able to go to the Greenlands if the ground was suitable, he doesn't have to have it heavy or very soft but once there's kindness in it we'll be looking at the likes of that. It fits in well and then he has two entries at Royal Ascot but obviously the ground is a proviso there too - Ken Condon, trainer, speaking on Racing TV

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Flying Five Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: Moss Tucker has been a great story with how he has progressed. Going in here we would have been delighted to be placed and then the heavens opened which helped us a good bit. He was very good here last time a month ago in the Phoenix Stakes, which was a career best and this was another one - Ken Condon, trainer.

The Abbaye has been the plan all year. Moss Tucker ran well there last season after missing the break and does handle those testing conditions. He might go straight there but if the ground is on the right side for him in the Flying Five he'll go here. He was good out there today. He enjoyed it and Billy said he never thought they were going to get to him. He just lengthened all the way to the line. He didn't have the likes of Art Power to contend with but he was good and for a sprinter he's ultra-reliable. He goes better when its heavy or testing but seems to go on all ground - Ken Condon, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Hatstone Solicitors Waterford Testimonial Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Moss Tucker is very honest, reliable and solid and he is still improving. He is very straightforward and I hope he will have a productive year again next year - Ken Condon, trainer.

We've asked Moss Tucker to run two quick races before. He's a very relaxed horse and is very tough, very likeable. He's got better with racing and has a good record at this track. Shane (Foley, rider) said he was always holding them and always comfortable. I thought Quarantine Dreams ran with good credit after Ascot where he was drawn on the wrong side. Those were different ground conditions and it is never ideal running two together but the race suited both horses and both connections were independently keen to run. Moss Tucker will have a break now for a little while Quarantine Dreams may run in the Phoenix Sprint - we'll campaign him in conditions' races, Listed and Group 3s. Six furlongs would be even better for him - Ken Condon, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Thank You To All The Frontline Workers From Tipperary Racecourse Handicap
quotes.notes: Moss Tucker has gotten quicker and sharper with racing and has a very good attitude. We've asked him a few questions and it's great to finish off his season like that. He'll be a nice four-year-old for all of those sprint handicaps. Up to seven furlongs will be fine for him - Ken Condon, trainer.

entries.raceInstanceTitle: William Hill Two Year Old Trophy (Listed Race)
Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran a great race when second at Cork on Friday. He took a blow inside the furlong pole but rallied back. He looks a nice horse going forward. We might step him up into black-type company and a mile and a quarter looks a nice trip for him at the moment. The Leopardstown Derby Trial might come up nicely for him or we could look at Chester. 27-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Blandford Bloodstock Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.notes: Andrew Balding has always liked Mubasimah and he said this morning that she would run a big race and she has won nicely. She'll be a nice horse next year and when they came to her she pulled out a bit more - Philip Robinson, racing manager to Sheikh Juma Dalmook Al Maktoum.

quotes.raceTitle: Sumbe Prix du Calvados (Group 2) (2yo Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: I was extremely impressed. Andre said beforehand My Highness needed to prove herself at this level. But she couldn't have been more impressive, she got a bit of cover and then just got home very easily. It's great for the stallion - I think it's his first Group 2 winner and we'd expect good things from this filly going forward. I'm sure a mile will be her optimal distance and I'm sure we'll be looking at the autumn and all those fabulous two-year-old races - Hugh Anderson, Godolphin managing director.

horse_profiles.breeder_name: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C

quotes.notes: The object was to cover Narissa  up because she pulled very hard in the Boussac. She broke well but was drawn wide and Mickael [Barzalona] had to slot in quite a long way back. She dropped the bit pretty quickly and then came home in really good style, so we're very happy. For a comeback, it all went just how we'd hoped and she'll run in the Poule all being well -  Nemone Routh, representing the Aga Khan Studs.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He ran a great race on Sunday in a Group 3 in France, which was no surprise because I've never seen him looking so well. He finished off last year really strongly, winning two big handicaps, and he's more than up to running in Group races. He loves heavy ground - that's the key to him. 31-03-26

horse_profiles.owner_name: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith

quotes.raceTitle: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: Never So Brave has kept on improving. To win over seven furlongs then to win over a mile then drop back to seven again shows he's pretty versatile. He's probably got an exciting campaign ahead. He did it pretty well today but Oisin said that he felt that a mile is probably going to be the better spot for him - Anna Lisa Balding.

I was confident enough because if Never So Brave was relaxed he was good enough to be winning. He's very good and I'm thrilled with his progression. We put him in the Lennox but he's versatile in terms of trip from six furlongs to a mile. I don't know where he goes, this opens up a few options as he showed he gets a mile - Andrew Balding, trainer.I reverted to plan B. I didn't know what the pace would turn out to be but it turned out to be quite strong and Jamie [Spencer, on Point Lynas] slipped us and was ten lengths ahead turning into the straight. Luckily I had a real reliable companion underneath me and Never So Brave filled me with confidence. He quickened so well and even a furlong and a half out I felt I'd go away and win. He's quite talented but it's difficult for a horse to come out of a handicap and into a Group race like he's done but he's improved leaps and bounds through the winter and since Andrew [Balding, trainer] has got him. He's an exciting horse. To ride such a good winner like this is a privilege - David Probert, jockey.

Never So Brave was gelded over the winter which may have helped him, but I know Sir Michael [Stoute] always had a high opinion of him - he ran him in the Jersey Stakes last year - and he was probably a Group horse in a handicap today. He settled well today, and I think the key to him is to try to get him to relax at an early stage of the race. He's got an excellent turn of foot if he can do that. He has been easy to train - the guys at home have done a brilliant job with him because he's not a very patient horse, he wants to get up the gallops first and get his exercise done, and they've done a lovely job with him. I'm really thrilled - Andrew Balding, trainer.Never So Brave was very good. His work has been excellent. I was worried he might get stuck in traffic from that draw, but he didn't, and I deliberately started a bit further back to allow the race to happen in front of him. If anything he got there very easily. He's a four-year-old now and I'd hope he will step up to Pattern company - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

Never So Brave showed some nice form last year and he's come out this year and practically won as he liked at Thirsk. He's just kept progressing and this was a step up to find out whether we're still going in the right direction and he's done everything he was asked to do. It's difficult to say how high he'll go but he did that quite nicely and if he got the mile, you'd like to think he'd be a Britannia horse - Philip Robinson, racing manager to Saeed Suhail, owner.

quotes.notes: Everything went wrong and usually when everything goes wrong in that calibre of race it's all over, so all credit to Night Raider. We've always had big faith in the horse and gelding him has made a huge difference. He has an enormous stride length now ? at Newmarket last time it was half a metre larger than at any point in his career previously and one of the biggest we've ever seen. I just wonder whether maybe something was pinching him before the gelding operation, I'm not sure. We had maybe questioned his resolution before but we're not questioning it now! He will go straight to Royal Ascot - Richard Brown, owners' representative.Night Raider is a fantastic horse. It didn't really go to plan and that wasn't his style of running. But I was able to switch him and get daylight, and then he picked up nicely for me - Clifford Lee, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: HKJC World Pool Palace House Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.notes: Night Raider is a high-class horse and we always knew he had a huge engine. He won his first two races over seven furlongs on the all-weather and we then tried to turn him into a miler and ran him in the Guineas, but he was just too keen, too free and too fractious. Gelding has really made him and brought him on. He is 10kg lighter than last year and I thought he looked tremendous in the paddock. I thought if he jumped quick and got into a rhythm he'd handle the undulations, which he did.  He was a bit fractious in the stalls last year as a full horse, but the gelding has calmed him down a bit. He's been working nicely - he does a lot on his own, as you don't need to work him with other horses. That's a great result for Wathnan Racing and Richard Brown, who has always had huge faith in him. I think it would be Royal Ascot now. He is also in at York, but that might come too quickly for him. I think he'd stay six furlongs - Karl Burke, trainer.We gelded Night Raider because he wasn't doing things 100% right. It was a good decision by the whole team and it's transformed him, he's a much more relaxed character. I know looking at the race and the way he ran you wouldn't think that but that's what he is - a real ball of speed. He tired a bit late on as he was entitled to  given we went ferocious fractions but I like the way he pulled out. Last year when one came to him he folded quite tamely whereas there he went again - James Doyle, jockey.
When everything goes smoothly for him and Night Raider is relaxed in the prelims and at the start, he's a horse with a lot of natural ability - Karl Burke, trainer.
Night Raider was very comfortable going a good gallop. He beat two decent benchmarks in Wiltshire and Annaf - Oisin Murphy, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: Boost Your Acca At BetMGM Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: The idea was to go straight to the Guineas with a racecourse gallop at the Craven meeting. Another run is probably the right thing to do, Danny [Tudhope, jockey] said Night Raider could do with another run, he's still green in front but he's obviously a very good horse - Karl Burke, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's just come back to us after a little operation. He's a very quick horse who has been gelded, which will help him because he was edgy. He'll be entered in the five-furlong sprints, although I still think he can stay six. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (New Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Nighttime is a colt who looks very obviously like he'll enjoy running over further next season, so for him to run that well today was a huge bonus. We've been beaten again by one of Aidan's very good horses. This horse can only grow and strengthen over the winter and he'll be trained for the Prix Jockey Club via the Poule d'Essai, and he's more evidence of the legacy we've been left by Wootton Bassett - Christopher Head, trainer.

Nighttime showed today that he has plenty of pace and that he handles this type of ground, both good signs for the future. We already had the Lagardere on his programme and he's shown he has the quality at this trip.  He has the right profile to tackle that race; he has speed and softer ground won't bother him - Christopher Head, trainer.
