quotes.notes: Noble Champion had a set-back in January that messed up our prep for the Greenham; he needed that run, we knew that, we always thought he was a Guineas horse and we really believed a lot in him, and then we thought we'll go a sensible route and ran him in a conditions race at Goodwood over a mile, there wasn't much pace and he was keen and just got it all wrong. Brought him back to six - he'd shown so much speed at home, and we thought six, we even thought we might end up supplementing him for the Commonwealth Cup, he has so much speed, that didn't work, and finally the trainer got it right! He's as good a work horse as we've had; he's got such a high cruising speed and he's just a very, very smart horse - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's another Royal Ascot winner but he's been off for a long time, having suffered an injury at Goodwood. He's a 7f specialist and I don't want to start him back at 6f or a mile, so he'll wait for the Spring Trophy at Haydock next month. He seems to have made a full recovery, which is obviously excellent news as he was really going places at the time he hurt himself. Let's hope he can pick up where he left off. 22-04-26

She's a very nice filly who finished a good second on her debut at Gowran in September. She was ready to run but hadn't come in her coat at that stage, but she's coming now. She has a few nice entries and is one that we hope can progress. 27-04-26

He's our highest-rated two-year-old from last year. He'll have no problem getting a mile and we'd be hopeful he'll be going beyond that as the year goes on, when we think we might be able to travel a bit with him. We're working towards the French Guineas to start. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: Ryan thought that he had the race in the perfect place four out, picked up the pace to the two and he thought the race was for us. He said that just the last hundred yards, it just felt like Nostrum had a puncture, he didn't get home. We've always thought that he would handle ease in the ground, but I think maybe that dead ground has just probably caught him out in the last stages. He's a very, very good horse, we are not going to lose any faith in him. He will have all the best entries and we will just have to re-group and get it right next time - James Savage, assistant trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Edmondson Hall Solicitors Sir Henry Cecil Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: We could go a mile and a quarter when we want. We have just got to think about it (where we go next) to be honest. Nostrum will tell us (if he is ready to go back into Group One company) but on that evidence you would think he is. I don't know (about going big) - we might get windy closer to the time! - Sir Michael Stoute, trainer.

Nostrum wasn't good enough today but he's a big scopey horse with a great mind on him. I haven't really thought about what next year might hold for him, but he'll have no problem getting a mile - Sir Michael Stoute, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tattersalls Stakes (Registered As The Somerville Tattersall Stakes) (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: It was very pleasing. I thought it was a very warm race but Nostrum did it very nicely first time and was entitled to come and run in a race like that. I was relieved and was pleased with the performance. I don't know if we will see him again this season. We will take him home and chill him out and relax him and put him back in fast work. It is a difficult time of year especially for two-year-olds when the weather turns so we don't know but I would like to give him one more run - Sir Michael Stoute, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He has a huge amount of ability but might not be entirely straightforward, and we might look to drop him back to six furlongs. Hopefully, he can turn into a horse for something like the Lennox, with the dream of getting him to France for the Foret. 14-04-25

quotes.notes: Hopefully Notable Speech can follow in the footsteps of Frankel and Night Of Thunder in his stud career. It's great he's been kept in training. Today we've seen the real Notable Speech. He's got some turn of foot. There aren't too many horses who can quicken like he can - Charlie Appleby, trainer.It was a great training performance by Charlie [Appleby]. When Notable Speech went to America in the spring it was a nightmare from start to finish. He didn't get a chance to show what he can do. We all knew he'd be in good shape here and it's been a great job by everybody. The race fell apart in front of me a little bit. He's explosive. He's an absolutely top-class miler and he's done it across the Atlantic, as well as here. He's got a super temperament to go with his ability - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: FanDuel Breeders' Cup Mile presented by PDJF (Grade 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Notable Speech has got that electric turn of foot. He's tailor-made for this track and the experience at Woodbine has been the making of him coming into a race like today. Will's [Buick] ride there was copybook, if you could've written a script on how to go round there, that was it. I was confident [watching the race], people would be praying for the cutaway but the longer we could sit on the rail the better because no one's got a turn of foot like him - Charlie Appleby, trainer, speaking to NBC.I've been everything on this horse, I've been a hero, a villain, but Charlie [Appleby] always fills me with great confidence. Notable Speech broke better today than we'd hoped. He was probably a bit unlucky in this race last year, as he lacked that two-turn mile experience, but he's a different horse this year - William Buick, jockey.

The normal outer turf track here is beautiful, a European style of racing. Now, obviously, we're on the inside track for these races, so it changes the dynamics a lot and our horses find it challenging.I  was not going to give up my position on Notable Speech. He's an experienced horse so I could do that with him. You have to be brave for a little bit there, but he was. Once he got into that position, he relaxed beautifully and he got into a nice rhythm. For me, he was winning from there on out - William Buick, rider.

quotes.raceTitle: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.notes: William [Buick] was really disappointed, Notable Speech didn't hit the line like we thought he would -  Charlie Appleby, trainer.

It's disappointing when you have a race like that and they've gone the pace they have. From our point of view, it was a bit hard to watch. Notable Speech was sat there, travelling like he was, and you knew it was going to turn into a sprint. We will put it behind us and he has run a solid race. I take on board what William said afterwards and, if you wanted to pigeon-hole him into a trip now that he is older and stronger, then seven furlongs is his gig. I still wouldn't walk away without taking a good strong view of the Sussex again, but we all know the City Of York Stakes is going to be one hell of a race this year - Charlie Appleby, trainer.
I'm delighted. Will said Notable Speech showed all his usual enthusiasm. He travelled and was one of the last to come off the bridle but then got tired close home - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix du Moulin de Longchamp (Group 1) (3yo+) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: Charlie [Appleby] is very philosophical and it's all now geared towards the Breeders' Cup, where Notable Speech will get the ground he needs. We all saw at Goodwood and Newmarket that he has fantastic acceleration on the right surface - Hugh Anderson, Godolphin chief executive.

Notable Speech was firing on all cylinders coming in here today. He's a brilliant Guineas winner, with a very rare turn of foot. He showed that again today and I'm delighted. Full credit to Charlie and the whole team, they've done such a good job with him to get him back after a disappointing run in the St James's Palace where he was obviously too bad to be true. He's such a brilliant horse. He's a horse that really excites you and it's a real privilege to be riding him - William Buick, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.raceTitle: St James's Palace Stakes (Group 1) (Colts) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: It's disappointing. That's obviously not the horse we know from Newmarket. Notable Speech relaxed nicely and I thought everything was going how I expected. Take nothing away from the winner, who has danced every dance, but we've not run anywhere near what we can do - William Buick, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qipco 2000 Guineas Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings) (British Champions Series)
quotes.notes: Notable Speech really was impressive. He's the kind of horse who I've not known for that long. I came back from Dubai and rode him in February and here we are. I've not very often believed in a horse as much as this guy. I've had that much belief in him and sometimes you go home at night and think 'have I lost the plot all together?' because that's how he does things, he does it so easily and his change of gear is incredible. The race couldn't have worked out any better, fair play to the team he was in great form today. He's done nothing but improve. He's an out-and-out miler, he's all about speed. He's got a strong mind, I really think he's a horse who is going to keep improving - William Buick, jockey, speaking to ITV.

quotes.raceTitle: Virgin Bet Best Odds Daily British EBF Conditions Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.notes: I was very pleased with how well Notable Speech has done physically since the last time I rode him. He's really filled out and I think he's grown a little as well, which is always nice to see. I couldn't be more happy with him. I tested him a little bit today and he had it covered in a stride. I had to try and pick a path with him but he's genuine and easy to deal with and he's got a bright future ahead of him. Obviously at the moment it's all wet [on the grass] so this was a nice opportunity for him to have another run on this surface. He'd handle a little bit of cut in the ground but he's a very fast horse with a low action, so he would like decent ground. He's a speedy miler. It was a really good performance and he deserves to go up in grade now. I thought this was a warm race and he gave away weight to all of them, so I'm delighted - William Buick, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She was placed in the German Oaks last year and has some nice form lines. We like what we see of her and we're aiming to start her around the second half of May. 22-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Down Syndrome Centre Cork Rated Race
quotes.notes: It was an inspired purchase by David Kelly, he spotted Oh Cecelia. She liked racing in isolation. She was good and tough at Naas and that's probably another step forward again. It's very pleasing and I think we'll have a go at the Polonia Stakes in early May. She's going in the right direction and after running yesterday it was lovely that she was able to pull out well and do that today. She was slightly unlucky yesterday and didn't get a run when she needed it, but she was eyecatching towards the line. She ate up last night and and jogged up well this morning so we said we would come again and I'm glad we did - Ken Condon, trainer.

Oh Cecelia was fit from her all-weather runs and we didn't do a whole pile with her. We weren't sure about the very deep ground but Billy said she just travelled everywhere.  We'll find something similar in the next few weeks, those three-year-old only races are good when you find them. She obviously copes with the soft ground and she did everything right there - Ken Condon, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish EBF Auction Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: I think Oh Cecelia is very progressive and she is the best 2yo I have around the place. She is very straightforward, always looks well, always works well, very sound, clear winded - Jack Davison, trainer, speaking to RacingTV.

Oliver Show has run a massive race. Huge credit to Charles Eddery and Chas Robinson who brought him back from Bahrain. He's a progressive horse - I thought he was maxed out where he is but he looks like there may be a little bit left. He goes well fresh and I'd say we'll probably work back from the Royal Hunt Cup - George Boughey, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He was meant to come back for the Lincoln but got stuck in Bahrain, where he was completely outpaced over six furlongs in January. He could go to the Guineas meeting if he gets back in time, then maybe go for this month's Spring Cup at Newbury. 02-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Dubai Turf Sponsored By DP World (Group 1) (Turf)
quotes.notes: That was a great sense of relief. It's not easy coming out of a winter in England and I think Ombudsman will come on for the race. He was coming here at 90% but it was enough to get the job done. I think William was wise, he thought he'd give the ground away by coming wide, lose the ground there but get a clear run in the straight. He'll go to Royal Ascot now for the Prince of Wales's and we'll see how we go from there - John Gosden, joint-trainer.Ombudsman showed there on his first run of the year what he can do in a very competitive field. A lot of the runners had run this winter and I'm very pleased with him. It was very smooth and he's going to have an exciting year - William Buick, jockey.

Ombudsman ran a super race. He's had some season. We had a slightly awkward draw and there was a very good pace to run at. It was always going to be between myself and Calandagan [as it unfolded]. I took the race to him but his stamina probably kicked in and in the last furlong he pulled away. I'm proud of his run - William Buick, jockey.

I didn't expect Danon Decile to take back, I thought he wanted to chase the pace. Rab did his job beautifully and his horse finished third. Ombudsman put in an amazing performance, unbelievable, so I'm delighted with him. He's a very, very special horse and he showed all his attributes today - William Buick, rider, speaking to ITV Racing.

We thought Delacroix would go forward and the French horse [Sosie] would sit handy but of course it's all happened the other way round. That happens in small fields and it didn't turn out the way we thought. Ombudsman has run a wonderful race. We were trapped rather wide, got close to the pace and Delacroix has then come and run as down late. It was one of those kind of races with a small field that can get messy but full marks to the winner who has gone and outstayed the lot of them - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

Sheikh Mohammed is without doubt the nicest and easiest owner I've ever trained for, he says 'do what we think is right'. We ran Ombudsman a little tenderly last year, listed, Ryan [Moore] rode him in Deauville, won a Group 3, put him away. He's come back this year and ran a super race in the Brigadier Gerard - I think the winner of that is exceptional - we were giving 3lbs, he got first run, but I think if the ground had been there, he'd have been with us today. But he's a special horse and it's just a question of an owner giving you the time to let them mature and get there, I never get pushed, he'll never be the horse he was unless I had such a patient owner. He's got a turn of foot and he [Buick] knew it, it was a matter of getting out but I did notice when he finally got daylight there was a furlong to go - John Gosden, joint-trainer. Ombudsman was impressive. They went a hard gallop. I was always going to have to ride for a bit of luck, and he quickened instantly. I thought he was impressive. He is a cool horse, a very talented horse. They went a hard gallop. We were drawn one, we always thought they would go a good gallop. We had to ride for a bit of luck and I had to look for a couple of gaps. The horse was good enough to quicken up from it; he quickened up well and won well in the end. He was the unknown quantity in the race. I thought he was impressive, very impressive. I think that was a taste of what's to come for sure. He's got low miles on the clock, he's an exciting horse for sure - William Buick, jockey.

At halfway you were relying on things to happen from where I was. Luckily, they did happen. Ombudsman will be far better off a stronger pace. Every horse is better on better ground but he did it again today and I think he won with a good bit up his sleeve. I don't think we can stand here and say how far he will go. He's gone so far already, so I see no reason why he won't go further. He's a great-to-look-at individual - William Buick, jockey.

She had ran this sort of distance last year at Gowran and we felt on pedigree that stepping her up would suit her. She is in the Nassau, she will be in the races on Arc weekend, she can run in the Blandford Stakes too. quotes.notes: I'm delighted and all credit to the team at home. Opera Ballo has always had the engine there but, like his father [Ghaiyyath] he can be a bit energetic. We came here today with an open mind as we had a penalty and were dropping back in trip against a stellar field this year. William [Buick] and I had discussed it enough times in the past [letting him lead] and, when the pace angles weren't there, we felt it was the right time to start him from the front. He's not a one-trick pony though and he'll probably go back up in trip for the Prix D'Ispahan and it would be perfectly manageable to drop him in - Charlie Appleby, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.I spoke with Charlie [Appleby, trainer] yesterday and it was quite obvious to us that it was a good opportunity for Opera Ballo to try and do it from the front. He's always been sharp into his stride and he was especially so today but he was measured in front and he went through the gears lovely. He's always been held in high regard and it's a nice way to start his domestic season - William Buick, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

We felt that we have a good horse on our hands for some time now. Opera Ballo was still a bit headstrong in the first quarter mile but, like William [Buick] says, they just can't go fast enough for him. He doesn't take a lot of training but he's got his Group one and he's a horse who is exciting going forward - Charlie Appleby, trainer, speaking to Racing Dubai.

The race set up a little bit better for Opera Ballo, he had cover which was crucial, stepping up a furlong in trip. We were wanting to learn something tonight, and we wanted to teach him something as well. We always thought he was a horse worthy of going to the top level at some stage, and he showed tonight he's on his way there - William Buick, jockey, speaking on Racing Dubai TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Edmondson Hall Solicitors Sir Henry Cecil Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: We would have been disappointed if Opera Ballo hadn't won today to be honest. He has a proper engine, it's just a case of getting it to go in the right direction. We'll be taking baby steps with him but he's a horse for next year possibly over a mile and a quarter. There's a race at Deauville we could look at - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

Opera Ballo settled much better than at Newmarket last time and it's good to see him get it done. He's very much a work in progress, the hood has helped a lot. I'm not quite sure what Charlie has planned but he appreciated a bit of juice in the ground and I wouldn't say Royal Ascot is a definite at this stage - Alex Merriam, assistant trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: "European Road To The Kentucky Derby" Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Opera Ballo was very smooth. I was very pleased with him. I do think he's a work in progress, but it's all there for him - William Buick, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.raceTitle: Unibet Supports Safer Gambling Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.notes: Opera Ballo is a beautiful horse. Just watching him going around the paddock was nice and he really impressed me with the way he went about his business. He was very professional. He jumped with the blind, but he got away lovely and I managed to find a nice slot. He was still actually quite green, he overraced a little bit, and he'll probably be better with a little bit of cover going forward, but from the gate it was all about getting him out and into a rhythm. When I asked him to stretch at the two pole, he lengthened away quite quickly and gave me a nice feel. I think another run with experience would definitely benefit him, especially if the option was there to get a mile on some turf. I think it would help getting him to switch off early ? we've seen his finishing kick ? and it could enhance that - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

I will admit he was a tad disappointing in the Dewhurst as he was one of the last off the bridle and didn't seem to quite finish off up the hill. I then stupidly ran him in heavy ground at Doncaster. He is one of those horses that things come easily to and he can be a little bit dreamy at home - he is always looking for low-flying seagulls. This race today did have a couple of late withdrawals, which didn't help the depth of the field and so we wound up the second favourite. He has run how you hoped he would run. He is a nice horse and deserves to take his chance [in the 2,000 Guineas] - John Gosden, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Duke Of York Clipper Logistics Stakes (Group 2)

Obviously Pierre Bonnard is a Derby horse. We'll start him in a Derby trial and all he should do is get better. We weren't sure [about the soft ground] and that's why it was good to come and see if he would handle the slower ground. They do a beautiful job here with the ground and it was lovely to get another run into him. He's a beautiful horse with a long stride and a beautiful mind, and he stays very well, so he's very exciting for next year - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.This is just mad, to win two Group 1s on the same day under hands and heels rides. Fortunately we went a decent gallop and he was very comfortable with the rhythm. He takes a little bit of time to get going so I was keen to launch my challenge early. But the way he finished, what joy! - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

Christophe [Soumillon] seemed very happy with Pierre Bonnard. He is a lovely big horse and still a big baby at home. He does everything very easy. I think at the moment he looks like a Derby trial horse for next year. Endorsement ran a lovely race too, it was very solid - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

We gave him a little flick to see if we thought Ascot would be for him but he's still on the leg, he's still weak. quotes.notes: Precise was very special last year and only just made the Guineas [at Newmarket]. Because she's a homebred it makes it very special. It's difficult to breed a Classic winner - next to impossible - so when it happens it's very exciting. We knew there was massive improvement and, in all fairness to Ryan Moore [rider of True Love], it was a difficult decision [on who to ride]. Wayne was super cool on the winner but Ryan had to ride True Love this time. We knew it was possible this could happen. It was an even pace, but Wayne said when he started to move and put her into top gear, she just took off and said she ran through the line. We came here thinking it was possible she could go back to Epsom in two weeks if the lads decide to do that. It would be very exciting and another very difficult decision for Ryan, as Amelia Earhart is in there and favourite. Will Precise get a mile and a half- You don't know until you try it but she's out of a Galileo mare [Way To My Heart] with a lot of stamina in her pedigree, so there's every chance she would even though she's by Starspangledbanner. It's exciting and I'm delighted for everybody - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Precise looks serious and a special filly. Everything she has done from day one has been so easy. We weren't sure how good she was but she looks a serious filly, make no mistake. That was even more impressive than Minding. Don't get me wrong, Minding was a top filly but this filly is different gear. We put those two fillies in there to make it a good strong gallop and she came through it great and gets better with every run. Christophe was sitting motionless most of the way and she does it so easy. I think she's a Classic filly. They'll both [Precise and Diamond Necklace] be trained for the Guineas, whether it be France, Britain or Ireland. The lads will decide. I don't think we'll see either of them again this year. When you get a special one you have to look after them - Aidan O'Brien. trainer.I was impressed when Precise won last time at the Curragh and came past us in three strides [when Soumillon was aboard favourite Composing in the Group One Moyglare]. She looks she can still improve a lot and loves to have horses to target. She missed the jump a bit, so I came behind Wayne [Lordan, on Composing] and she was really cruising the whole way. When I asked her to quicken, I came a bit early I think but when I asked her to go, she went past them like a train - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

Precise is a lovely filly. She's growing and maturing all of the time. You don't know when she'll stop improving and she's very classy. She travelled very strongly and galloped right through the line. That was a win and you're in for the Breeders' Cup and she'd love that fast ground, she's a slick mover. Now she's a Group 1 winner we can go gentle with her - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Precise is a very professional filly. She has pace, and what you like about her is that when you get down into her she gets seven [furlongs] quite well. She looked comfortable. Just when I hit the front a furlong out she pricked one ear, which is always a nice thing. She travelled good and I hit the line well enough [to suggest] that going up another furlong is an option -  Wayne Lordan, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She had a temperature about three weeks ago so we're going back gentle with her. We gave her a day away at the Curragh and we'll take her back and train her for Newmarket and see what happens. I was super-impressed with her when she won the Fillies' Mile last year - she went through the last furlong coasting. She then travelled over for the Breeders' Cup and all we thought she had to do was get round, but she picked up an infection. She's not overly big but is still 30kg up on last year's racing weight, which doesn't usually happen with a filly of that size. I'd imagine she'll end up going straight to the 1,000 Guineas and then go to the Oaks after that. Plenty are saying she's by Starspangledbanner so won't stay a mile and a half, but my instinct is that she's an incredible filly. I could be totally wrong, we've only trained a few Starspangledbanners, but everything she does suggests she'll stay. She has loads of personality, but she relaxes. 31-03-26

quotes.raceTitle: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.notes: I think Prince Of India is ready to step up in class and once he gets some more give in the ground he'll appreciate that too. I think he's fast enough for this distance and as he gets stronger he will develop into a real sprinter. I do think there's more to come - Marco Botti, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Coolmore Stud No Nay Never Fairy Bridge Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.notes: If any horse deserved to win a stakes race, it is Princess Child, but you don't always get what you deserve. I don't know how many times she has been placed in stakes races without winning one, and we were campaigning her aggressively to win one. She had built a whole load of black type, but you have to win one too. I would say that will be a career best, and when a horse wins a race they get confidence from it. We'll see where next, but she is a Group winner now, which is kind of job done, but we will try and win another one now - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Ahonoora Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.notes: Once we straightened up I knew I would pick them up because they were kind of paddling in front. Princess Child is a very consistent filly and hopefully she can progress into stakes company again and get her head in front - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: She's got better every year with racing and ran great when second in the Express Stakes behind Celestial Orbit last time after not doing badly in a messy race on her comeback. She could take on Celestial Orbit again in the Lanwades Stud Stakes. 22-04-26

horse_profiles.owner_name: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: He has an unbelievable pedigree and was just raw and babyish the first day. Even today Proposition was still very raw but when Ronan (Whelan) galvanised him, he galloped out strong to the line. He'll be a lovely middle-distance horse for next year, he handles that ground and will get further. He isn't too bad - Chris Armstrong, stable representative

quotes.raceTitle: British Stallion Studs John Dunlop EBF Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: It's not a huge surprise that Protection Act was able to take a step up in grade but he's a horse who we've minded through the spring and just allowed him to come to hand when he's ready. He's obviously achieved plenty over a mile so far, but it would be no surprise to see him get further. He relaxes and seems to find the line. There are lots of options for a horse like him. He could go to something like the Heron Stakes [on May 28], and he's in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot. All options really are open for him at the moment - George Boughey, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a big, rangy horse who did everything on raw ability last year. He's taken a bit of time to come to hand this spring but will improve as the summer goes on and we might miss the Craven meeting. I think he'll be seen to better effect when he goes up in trip, possibly to ten furlongs. He'd be near the top of the pile and is really exciting. 02-04-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

quotes.notes: Puerto Rico looked a little bit rusty on his first run of the year so we'll try again. I think a mile will be his trip - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

Puerto Rico is pacey, he stays and we wanted to see what he would be like over a mile. He handles soft ground, although we were thinking of going to the Breeders' Cup with him, but when Gstaad went to the Breeders' Cup, we said we'd let him come here. He'll start in a Guineas. He's a classy horse who I see as a real miler but because he's so relaxed I think he will get further - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Puerto Rico has a lot of talent, but he's a horse who looks around a bit and you have to make sure he concentrates. He was a little bit upset in the stalls but I made sure we got a good start because he's very happy when he can dominate from the front. I wanted to go forward and I saw that the horse we had to beat [Cape Orator] was upsides but wasn't travelling as well on the home turn. I got a good blow into him there and I knew he'd see the trip out well. He looks like he'll be a very good horse at this trip next year - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (New Course) (Turf)
quotes.notes: I was probably running Puerto Rico over a little bit too short because he was showing us loads of speed. He ran over six furlongs up until Doncaster. That was his first run over seven and he won. The horse that was third to him that day [Cape Orator] won yesterday, so the form got very strong overnight. Christophe [Soumillon] gave him a beautiful ride. He's a lovely, big, powerful, mature horse with loads of speed. The lads were thinking of the Breeders' Cup and they asked about ground, but Christophe said ground and trip would be no problem. I'd say he definitely could be one for the Juvenile Turf - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Ryan [Moore, jockey] said he thought the ground would be a big help to Puerto Rico and for me to ride him confidently, and it was the same with Aidan before the race. There's nothing hard, we ride for the horses. He jumped the gates really well and I took him to the front and he was really relaxed. He was hanging out for a while but in the straight when I took him to the rail he picked up really well and I felt nobody was following me - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

That was very polished. Puerto Rico is a nice horse and showed a great attitude, Sean was very happy with him. He's not ground dependent and he's been knocking on the door, I thought he ran particularly well in the Richmond Stakes at Goodwood. It's nice to get his Group 2 win on the board and it's been a while since Seahenge won this for us, and Westphalia before that. He's by the sire of the moment Wootton Bassett out of a Galileo mare and he's got a very good pedigree. I haven't had a chance to speak to Aidan but he's entered up in all the right places so he's a horse to look forward to - Kevin Buckley, Coolmore representative.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a very good horse and could be anything. He missed two months early last year, so he was a good bit behind everyone else and was probably playing catch-up all the time. I was running him over six furlongs early in the year and I remember he was flat out the whole way in the Richmond and still finished second. He just kept progressing - he improved when he went from six to seven furlongs, winning the Champagne Stakes and the Lagardere, then again up to a mile when he won another Group 1 in France. He's done very well physically. He's scopey, strong and his mind has really gone the right way. He could be one to take on the older milers and travel to all the big Group 1s. He's very uncomplicated; he can make the running or drop in. 31-03-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Gowran Classic

stable_tour_quotes.notes: A lovely filly who was unlucky not to break her maiden last year. She has an Irish 1,000 Guineas entry. She's been a bit slow to come to hand this season but she's coming. 27-04-26

horse_profiles.breeder_name: Hellwood Stud Farm & R C Dollar

quotes.notes: When I rode Purosangue the last day, he bumped into a really nice horse of Karl's (Burke, trainer). I was very confident he'd stay the six and he stayed well. He was a willing partner who has been so consistent all year and deserved to finish off the year on a high note. He wouldn't be the biggest but he's solid. He's got great mental strength and I'd be confident he'd train on" - P J McDonald, jockey.

We're just thrilled Purosangue is back on form - he created a very good impression first time out, and we just thought he did things the wrong way round at Newmarket. That was much more like it, and he was beaten by a very good horse. He won on pretty good ground at Haydock so I think he's quite versatile. He looks like he'll be made for the Roses at York - Andrew Balding, trainer.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: He's a nice horse who we inherited from Andrew Balding. He was a useful horse for him last year in top-notch handicaps (fourth in the Ayr Gold Cup). He has run only once for us, at Pontefract in early April. He missed the break, started late and actually made up a lot of ground, finishing fourth in quite a decent 6f handicap won by Arklow Lad. He ran a belter at Newbury on Saturday, finishing fourth, but he would have been at least placed had he not got hemmed in. If there's any soft in the going description it will enhance his prospects and I think he's got a nice big handicap in him this year. 20-05-26

entries.raceInstanceTitle: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies & Mares)

quotes.raceTitle: Childwickbury Stud Fillies' Trial Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: I was really disappointed at Newmarket. We wanted to roll forward but Falakeyah was just too quick for us and Qilin Queen didn't come down the Dip too well either. I told Hollie Doyle to be bold today because she keeps galloping and she nailed it. She wasn't very good in the prelims before her last run but she was much better today. She was still a bit buzzy but that's just her and not something I'd worry about. If all is well we'll probably roll the dice at Epsom. She's very game, athletic and will stay well - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.notes: Qilin Queen is a nice filly going forward. She made a pleasing debut at Newbury but was quite green that day. It was noticeable how professional she was today and she's a tall, leggy filly who'll strengthen and improve for the year. I've no doubt she'll  train on and make a nice 3yo too - Ross Coakley, jockey, talking to RacingTV.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: It's lovely to have her back. She had a great time in 2025 and we'll try to get her some Group 1 form this year. She could start in the Nottinghamshire Oaks over 1m2f or join American Gal in the Dahlia Stakes at Newmarket. If she doesn't look like being competitive at the top level here, we could look at races on grass in America. She goes on fast ground, is well balanced, not very big and good out of the stalls. 22-04-26

quotes.notes: Qirat has always threatened to be a good horse, I've just never managed to get it out of him until today. He was here to set the pace and go 12-second furlongs from the front. That's what he was here to do and the longer he lasted, the better it was for everyone concerned with him. That was the idea. Having watched the clock, I think he achieved that, and the last thing I said to Richard Kingscote before he got on him was, 'Keep going on this fellow. He isn't going to stop and he could run really well here' - Ralph Beckett, trainer. I feel like a villain, but when I saw it wasn't a grey nose coming towards me I kept going. Ultimately, we were there as a helping hand to go an even gallop and we were somewhat ignored early then took a lead off Wayne Lordan. Towards the cutaway I was thinking Qirat was going well, but you always expect the horses rated 20lb higher to be coming through. I could see Rosallion coming, but my horse kept pulling out. I think Ralph [Beckett, trainer] was happy to have me on as I like being in front, like my fractions and it worked out okay. It's a bit surreal but great to be going to Hong Kong on a positive note - Richard Kingscote, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Most Top Price Runners Handicap
quotes.notes: Conditions hadn't gone Qirat's way but he was at his best back on the easier surface. I've always thought he was well handicapped and with a bit of rain he may well have won the Britannia at Royal Ascot - Hector Crouch, rider, speaking to ITV Racing.

stable_tour_quotes.notes: I can't say any of us were expecting him to win the Sussex, but Richard Kingscote was brilliant on him. He was in the best shape he'd been in all year and that combination meant it all came to pass. We're likely to go back to Goodwood for the Celebration Mile and the Sussex again. He might go for the Diomed on Derby weekend along the way. 27-04-26

quotes.raceTitle: Singspiel Stakes Sponsored By Emirates Airline (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: There was no pace early. Ryan [Moore] had Quddwah in completely the right position, he kicked off the bend and won very well. We'll see how he is but I think that's the plan [The Dubai Turf on World Cup Night], it's a win and you're in and he saw out the extra furlong well - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer, speaking to Racing TV.Quddwah is a very straightforward horse who is very consistent at this level. The race worked out nicely for him and he showed a good attitude. It was a solid performance - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.raceTitle: Zabeel Mile Sponsored By Phi Advertising (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.notes: We didn't go that quick and I was happy to press on early with Quddwah. He stuck at it well. He's been very consistent over the years and he always gives his running. - James Doyle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

We're delighted with Quddwah. Ascot was very excusable as it was too quick that day and he didn't let himself down on the ground. When he's got these sorts of conditions he's a very good horse, as you saw today. We'll talk to Sheikh Ahmed and see what he would like to do for the future, but races like the Celebration Mile, the Jacques le Marois and the Prix du Moulin all come into discussions. We'll see how he is after the race and make a plan - Simon Crisford, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Prix du Haras de Fresnay-le-Buffard Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (3yo+ No Geldings) (Straight Course)
quotes.notes: I thought Quddwah ran super, obviously lacking experience going into a championship race. The ground was a little bit quick for him and I think his career is all ahead of him. I think it was a very solid run and we'll look forward to seeing him on his next start. We'll talk to [owner] Sheikh Ahmed and see what he wants to do, but an obvious next race would be the Leopardstown Mile - Simon Crisford, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: Bet With Ascot Donation Scheme Paradise Stakes (A Queen Anne Stakes Trial) (Listed Race)
quotes.notes: Quddwah won at Newmarket nicely and we were due to run him at the July meeting in a Listed race, but just before he got a little issue and we had to put him away. However, he'd always shown he was a horse on the up. We'll have to see what Sheikh Ahmed [Al Maktoum, owner] wants to do but the Diomed is probably the next step up. He's a bit immature and Epsom might be a lot, but we have to look at what the options are and he just wants bringing along in a nice manner. He is in the Queen Anne and I don't think I'd have reservations about that, because he'll come on a lot from this and it just depends on what happens in the next few weeks. This is only his third race, so he's still got his whole future ahead of him. He's a very nice horse to have in the stable. He picked up well and finished off nicely, showing a lovely turn of foot. I think today's small field with this ground was the perfect start of him - Ed Crisford, joint-trainer.

quotes.raceTitle: William Hill Lengthen Your Odds Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.notes: Quddwah had to be quite brave as the second took us off a line a bit but he showed a real likeable attitude. I'd never sat on him, but he's got a good pedigree and will go further - he's got a lovely relaxed character and should improve for further. The ground is on the dead side of good, it's not bad, and rode quite nice on him. The third horse gives some substance to the form and I'd say the race will work out. He's got a bit of quality - James Doyle, jockey.
